- Word: Microsoft Word for Mac 16.115 (build 16.115.26100424), platform `darwin`.
- Transport, sessions 1 and 2: `verifyInWord` (`src/lib/word-verifier.ts`). It opens each specimen by path, reads Word's window and dialog state, and never saves.
- Transport, session 3: `neurotic_docx_bench/scripts/word_pdf.py` in its default batch mode (`--label wfv --no-check-preset`). It stages each file inside Word's container as `NNNNN__wfv__<file>`, opens it, and exports a PDF when Word reads it. When Word shows an alert, it brings Word forward, answers a repair prompt No and then the OK that follows, and logs the alert's words. A file's outcome comes only from an alert that names its staged file, never from timing (`wordpdf_outcomes.py`, reproduced at the end). The specimens' SHA-256 were checked against the files handed to the driver after each run, and no specimen was rebuilt between build and run.
- Transport, sessions 4–13: the same driver in the same mode, run in the foreground, as its documentation requires. Single-specimen runs are attributed by the same parser. The runner and the helper that copies one specimen into its own run are reproduced at the end.
- Outcomes: `clean-open` means Word opened the document with no dialog. `repair-warning` means Word showed "Word found unreadable content … Do you want to recover the contents of this document?". `open-error` means Word showed "Word experienced an error trying to open the file." In session 3, `inconclusive` means Word loaded no document in two passes and no alert named the file. Word stayed alive throughout, and `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports` holds no Word report from any session. In session 3 the driver itself restarted Word after runs of empty loads, as designed.
- Specimens: built in code from `MINIMAL_PARTS` (`tests/support/minimal-docx.ts`). The `398-dup-theme-*` specimens are built from `tests/fixtures/broken/package.word-duplicate-theme.docx`, which was only read. The probe script that builds, validates and opens them is reproduced at the end of this file. No fixture or manifest was changed.
- Validator: the `word-valid` and `strict` columns record `validate()` **at probe time**, before the policy changes the probes motivated. They are not current verdicts. Session 1 (02:18Z–02:26Z) ran against `wfv/46-plan-audit` (199c2d5b); session 2 (03:10Z–03:19Z) ran against `wfv/51-directory-staging` (ad072db8). Session 3's columns are `validate()` at `wfv/57-central-directory-names` (ab7f311d), run on the exact files Word was given. The columns for sessions 4–6 are `validate()` at `wfv/62-ct-duplicate-declaration` (3126dcfc). They were recomputed after the sessions on the exact files Word was given, and every SHA-256 was checked against its record. Session 7's columns are `validate()` at `wfv/65-override-partname` before (9960b273) and after (34d0ace3) the #450 fix, recomputed the same way; the verdicts recorded at build time equal the 9960b273 ones. Sessions 8–13's columns are `validate()` at 49922e9a, the commit the specimens were built against, and at `wfv/66-partname-review-fixes` (e08611b1) after the #453 and #458 fixes, recomputed the same way with every SHA-256 checked; the verdicts recorded at build time equal the 49922e9a ones. Session 14's columns are `validate()` at ed34e3bf. Session 15's columns are `validate()` at `wfv/87-zip64-rekey` (8252ce4f), the commit the specimens were built against, recorded at build time on the exact files Word was given; every SHA-256 was re-checked against its record after the runs. Session 16's columns are `validate()` at `wfv/98-iri` (98902c85), recorded the same way. Session 17's columns are `validate()` at `wfv/100-word-probes-s16` (3ebe3e7f, whose source is layer 99's), session 18's at `wfv/101-glossary-header` (ab1fba79), session 19's at `wfv/108-segment-doc` (4c86cbfe), session 20's at `wfv/113-glossary-eager` (52fdbd8b), and sessions 21 and 22's at `wfv/115-word-probes-s20` (cb36e27a), recorded the same way.

## What the observations decide

- **#388: package relationships.** A zero-byte, truncated or undeclared-prefix `_rels/.rels` makes Word offer recovery, and the readable control opens clean. Word-valid passed all three, so `xml-syntax` and `xml-undeclared-prefix` on `_rels/.rels` are now Word-blocking.
- **#392: `WORD/` folder.** A package with every Word part under `WORD/` opens clean. With its main part malformed, Word refuses it exactly as it refuses the lower-case control. That matches the current policy, which matches `word/` by OPC part name.
- **#396: content-types stream spelling.** A stream stored as `[CONTENT_TYPES].XML` opens clean. Malformed, it makes Word offer recovery, as word-valid predicts. That matches the any-case lookup.
- **#397: unknown declared encoding.** `word/document.xml` declaring `X-UNKNOWN-ENCODING` makes Word refuse the file, and the `windows-1252` control opens clean. Word-valid passed it, so this was a false negative; `xml-encoding` now follows the `xml-syntax` path policy. Session 2 confirms the inferred scope:
    - the same declaration in `word/styles.xml`, in the content-types stream and in `_rels/.rels` makes Word offer recovery;
    - a `word/document.xml` declared UTF-8 holding a lone Latin-1 byte makes Word refuse it;
    - word-valid fails all four;
    - in `docProps/core.xml` the declaration also makes Word offer recovery, but word-valid passes it (#409).
- **#351: equivalent part names.** Every duplicate probed makes Word offer recovery, even when both spellings hold identical bytes: case variants, an unreserved escape (`word/%73tyles.xml`), a backslash (`word\document.xml`), and two content-types streams. Word-valid passed the escape and backslash duplicates. A single backslash name is read as `/`: the main part stored only as `word\document.xml` opens clean (#374).
- **#408: escaped item names (OPC [M1.8]).** Any stored name with a percent-escaped unreserved character makes Word offer recovery:
    - the styles part stored only as `word/%73tyles.xml`;
    - the main part stored only as `word/%64ocument.xml`;
    - the sidecar stored as `document.xml.%72els`;
    - an unreferenced extra `word/%78tra.xml`, which settles the cause, since nothing points at it;
    - the styles control (its part missing, its relationship kept) opens clean, so a missing target is not the cause;
    - word-valid passed the first two and the extra item.
- **#398 and #402: `.RELS` sidecar.** A `.RELS`-spelled document sidecar opens clean. With two theme relationships, Word offers recovery for both the `.rels` control and the `.RELS` variant, as word-valid now predicts for both. An external hyperlink resolved through a `.RELS` sidecar opens clean, as the `.rels` control does, but word-valid fails it. That is the #402 false positive: the sidecar lookups must fold case. Through a `.%72els` sidecar, Word offers recovery; that is #408.
- **#409: core properties.** A truncated `docProps/core.xml`, or one declaring an unknown encoding, makes Word offer recovery. Word-valid passes both, because docProps findings are downgraded. The `docProps/app.xml` control opens clean. Session 3 settles the rule (below).
- **#401: `word-content-type-invalid`.** An `invalid-*` type on an existing part makes Word refuse the file or offer recovery: styles, the main part and core properties. The same type on an `Override` for a missing part, or on a `Default` that covers no part, opens clean. The check over-reported; it now reports only declarations that apply to a stored part.

Session 3 adds:

- **#409: properties parts are read through their relationships.** Truncated, undeclared-prefix and unknown-encoding `docProps/core.xml`, `app.xml` and `custom.xml`, each named by its package relationship, make Word offer recovery. The same defects in unreferenced `core.xml`, `app.xml` and `custom.xml` open clean. A truncated core part stored as `props/meta.xml` and named by the core-properties relationship makes Word offer recovery, and its well-formed control opens clean. So Word reads what the relationship names, wherever it is stored. Word-valid passes every one of these (lane 409 implements the rule).
- **#410: real encodings libxml2 cannot decode.** `word/document.xml` declaring `macintosh`, `x-mac-cyrillic`, `IBM866` or `UTF-7` makes Word refuse the file. The `windows-1252` control with non-ASCII text opens clean. Word-valid already fails all four, so the policy stands; the README now says it covers these labels.
- **#411: identical stored names and dot segments.** Two entries stored under the identical name `word/document.xml` make Word offer recovery, whichever entry is malformed, and so do two `..` item names. At ab7f311d word-valid fails all five.
- **#408: every unreserved escape probed.** `%41` (upper-case letter), `%30` (digit), `%2D` and `%2d` (hyphen), `%2E`, `%5F` and `%7E` in an unreferenced extra item all make Word offer recovery. The `%20` control (a reserved character) opens clean. An extra `[Content_Types].%78ml` item beside the real stream makes Word offer recovery too, so the check is right to report a stream spelling (review X F1).
- **#436: escaped `/` and `\` (OPC [M1.7]).** An unreferenced `word%2Fxtra.xml` makes Word offer recovery, and `word%5Cxtra.xml` makes it refuse the file. Word-valid passes both.
- **#414: `Override` PartNames that are not part names.** The session 3b styles specimens are confounded (#432, below). Session 3c adds an `Override` with `ContentType="invalid-x"` for a part that does not exist. With the plain `PartName` `/word/nothere.xml`, it opens clean. With `..`, `#fragment` or a backslash, Word offers recovery, and with `?query` it refuses the file. Word-valid passes all four.
- **#432: a styles part typed by the generic Default.** Removing the styles `Override`, so that `word/styles.xml` falls to `<Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/>`, makes Word offer recovery. Nothing reports it.
- **#431: duplicate content-type declarations.** Two `Default`s for one extension (identical, or differing in case) and two `Override`s for one part (identical, conflicting, or differing in case) all make Word offer recovery. Word-valid and strict pass all five.
- **#433 and #434: package relationships structure.** A foreign element anywhere in `_rels/.rels`, whether beside the relationships or wrapping the main one, makes Word offer recovery, and so does a root other than `Relationships`. Word-valid passes all three; strict fails them through the XSD walk only.
- **#435: no content-types stream.** Without `[Content_Types].xml`, Word offers recovery. Word-valid reports `ct-missing` as a warning only.
- **#380: no main part.** An empty ZIP and a package without `word/document.xml` make Word offer recovery. Word-valid passes both. A package whose main relationship is removed is inconclusive.
- **#437: an unreferenced malformed part under `word/`.** A truncated, unreferenced `word/xtra.xml` opens clean, but word-valid fails it. This is a false positive of the `word/` folder rule; reachability, as for the properties parts, would fit both observations.

Sessions 4–6 add:

- **#380: a removed main relationship.** With the `officeDocument` relationship removed and `word/document.xml` kept, Word offers recovery. All three #380 shapes are therefore Word-blocking. Word-valid at 3126dcfc passes this one.
- **#414: `Override` PartNames with a well-formed content type.** The `Override` has `ContentType="application/xml"` and names a missing part. The plain `/word/nothere.xml` opens clean. Word offers recovery for each of the other nine:
    - `..`, `?query`, `#fragment` and a backslash;
    - no leading slash, an empty segment and a trailing slash;
    - an escaped `/` (`%2F`) and an escaped unreserved character (`%6F`).

    With `invalid-x` in session 3c, the query form made Word refuse the file; here it makes Word offer recovery. Word-valid and strict pass all nine.

- **#408: an escape in a folder segment.** An unreferenced `f%6Fo/xtra.xml` makes Word offer recovery, and the `foo/xtra.xml` control opens clean. Word-valid already fails it.
- **#433: a part-level relationships part.** A foreign element appended to `word/_rels/document.xml.rels` makes Word offer recovery, and the unchanged control opens clean.
- **#437: Word reads what it reaches through relationships it understands.** Three specimens open clean:
    - an unreferenced, truncated `customXml/item9.xml`;
    - a truncated `word/xtra.xml` named only by a relationship of an unknown type;
    - a truncated `word/xtra.xml` with its own `Override` and no relationship.

    Word-valid fails the last two, so they are false positives. Neither an unknown relationship type nor a declared content type makes Word read a part.

- **#409: a core-properties relationship Type with a trailing space.** A truncated core part named by such a relationship opens clean, and so does its well-formed control. Word does not read the part as core properties. Word-valid agrees and passes both (review Z F2).
- **#411, review Y: Word reads central-directory names.**
    - A `..` name that is only in the central directory makes Word offer recovery: `evil/../x.xml` with local name `x.xml`.
    - So does a central `a/../x.xml` whose unicode-path field says `x.xml`.
    - A `..` name that is only in the local header opens clean: central `word/extra.xml`, local `../evil.xml`.
    - So does a central `x.xml` whose unicode-path field says `../evil.xml`.
    - Two central entries both named `word/document.xml`, with distinct local names, make Word offer recovery, as #411's identical names do.

    Word-valid fails the two specimens Word opens clean. Its extraction judges the name JSZip loads, which comes from the local header or the unicode-path field.

- **#443: non-ASCII stored names.** Word offers recovery for any stored name holding a non-ASCII character, raw or percent-escaped, at the package root or under `word/`:
    - the CP437 byte `0x82`;
    - UTF-8 `é`, with or without flag bit 11;
    - `%C3%A9` and `%E9`.

    The ASCII controls `cafe.xml`, `word/cafe.xml` and `caf%20.xml` open clean. Word-valid passes all six recovery specimens.

Session 7 adds:

- **#414: the remaining `PartName` rules.** Each specimen is an `application/xml` `Override` for a missing part, as in sessions 4 and 5. Word offers recovery for a last segment ending with `.` (`/word/nothere.xml.`), a space, `[` and `]`, and a literal `é`. Word-valid at 9960b273 already fails all four. The `/word/nothere.xml` and `/word/no%20there.xml` controls open clean.
- **#450: a folder segment ending with `.`.** Word opens `/word./nothere.xml` (twice, once in a run of its own), `/word/sub./nothere.xml` and `/x./nothere.xml` clean. Word-valid at 9960b273 fails all four, a false positive. At 34d0ace3 word-valid warns and passes them, and strict still fails them under [M1.9].
- **#451: a percent-escaped non-ASCII `PartName`.** `/word/caf%C3%A9.xml` is a valid part name, but Word offers recovery, as it does for the non-ASCII stored names of #443. Word-valid and strict pass it.

Sessions 8–13 add:

- **#432: every part typed by the generic Default.** Typed only by `<Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/>`, a related settings, fontTable or webSettings part makes Word offer recovery, and so do the main part and styles with their `Override` removed. Each control with the part's proper `Override` opens clean. Word-valid at 49922e9a passes all five; strict fails only the main part.
- **#443: a non-ASCII name that a relationship targets.** The styles part stored as `word/stylés.sty`, typed by an `sty` `Default`, makes Word offer recovery whether its relationship targets `stylés.sty` or `styl%C3%A9s.sty`. The ASCII `word/styles.sty` control opens clean. The unreferenced stored names `word/caf%C3%A9.xml` and `word/a%80b.xml` make Word offer recovery too (session 12). Word-valid passes all four.
- **#451 and #408: which percent-escapes Word refuses.** In an `Override` `PartName` and in an unreferenced stored name alike, Word offers recovery for an escape of a character in the RFC 2396 unreserved set, and for any escape of 0x80 or above:
    - RFC 3986 unreserved: `%41`, `%39`, `%2D`, `%2E`, `%5F`, `%7E`;
    - the RFC 2396 marks `!`, `'`, `(`, `)`, `*`: `%21`, `%27`, `%28`, `%29`, `%2A` and `%2a`;
    - 0x80 and above: `%80`, `%FF`, `%E9`.

    It opens clean `%01`, `%7F`, `%22`, `%24`, `%25`, `%26`, `%2B`, `%2C`, `%3A`, `%3B`, `%3C`, `%3D`, `%40`, `%5B` and `%7B` in a `PartName`, `%26`, `%3A`, `%5B` and `%7F` in a stored name, and a literal `!` in both. Word-valid catches only the RFC 3986 part, so it passes the marks and the escapes of 0x80 and above (false negatives).

- **#437: Word parses some related parts at open, and others only when the document uses them.** Malformed, a related settings, fontTable or webSettings part, an unused but related numbering part, and a `customXml` item named by a document `customXml` relationship each make Word offer recovery. A malformed footer referenced from `w:sectPr` makes Word refuse the file, and malformed comments referenced by a comment range make it offer recovery. The same footer, comments or footnotes, related but unused, open clean. Word-valid fails the unused footer (twice), comments (twice) and footnotes, which are false positives, and passes the `customXml` item, a false negative.
- **#453: dot-only folder segments.** `/word/.../x.xml`, `/word/..../x.xml` and `/.../x.xml` make Word offer recovery, while `/word./x.xml` opens clean again. Word-valid at 49922e9a passes the three, because the #450 tolerance caught them. At e08611b1 they break their own rule ([M1.10]) and fail word-valid.
- **#458: an `Override` without a usable `PartName`.** Without the attribute, with `PartName=""` and with `PartName="/"`, Word offers recovery, and word-valid fails all three.

Session 14 adds:

- **#459: Markup Compatibility in the content-types stream.** `xmlns:mc` declared on `Types` and left unused opens clean. `mc:Ignorable="x"` on `Types` makes Word offer recovery, alone or with an ignored `<x:Foo/>` child; word-valid at ed34e3bf passes both, and strict fails both through `xsd-error`. An ignorable namespace declaration in `[Content_Types].xml` is itself enough for Word to offer recovery. Both `mc:AlternateContent` orientations, whose Choice and Fallback each hold one `Override`, make Word offer recovery too, but each also carries `/word/a%41b.xml`, which Word refuses alone (session 11), so those two do not separate the MCE cause.
- **#464: bytes before the archive.** A 2-entry ZIP, or 4096 spaces, in front of the minimal package make Word offer recovery, with the package's offsets relative to its own start and with them rewritten as absolute. Word-valid at ed34e3bf fails the prefixed ZIP through `zip-bytes-after-eocd` and passes both space prefixes, as strict does.

Session 15 adds, for review AM's suspected findings on layers 78 and 79:

- **#514 (F4): the main document's relationships part.** `word/_rels/document.xml.rels` missing its root end tag, or zero bytes, makes Word offer recovery. Word-valid at 8252ce4f passes both, since layer 78 stopped blocking on that part; strict fails both through `xml-syntax`.
- **#515 (F6): a second `officeDocument` relationship.** Any second `officeDocument` relationship in `_rels/.rels` makes Word offer recovery: to a well-formed `alt/document.xml` with or without a main-type `Override`, to a malformed one, and to `word/document.xml` again. A well-formed `alt/document.xml` with a main-type `Override` and no relationship opens clean, so the relationship is the cause. Word-valid and strict pass the well-formed second relationship and the same-target one.
- **#516 (F8): headers, endnotes, themes and glossaries.** A malformed header stored as `hdr/header1.xml` and referenced by `w:headerReference` makes Word refuse the file, and its well-formed control opens clean. Malformed endnotes at `en/endnotes.xml` used by `w:endnoteReference`, a malformed theme at `th/theme1.xml` and a malformed glossary at `g/glossary.xml`, each named by a document relationship, make Word offer recovery. A malformed `word/header1.xml` or `word/endnotes.xml` that is related but not referenced opens clean. Word-valid passes the four stored outside `word/` and fails the two unused ones.
- **#517 (F9): generic content types.** Word offers recovery for the main part typed by a `text/xml` Default, an `application/xml` Override or a `text/xml` Override, and for styles typed by an `application/xml` Override or a `text/xml` Default. Word-valid passes all five, and strict passes all but the `text/xml` Default on the main part (`ct-undeclared-part`).
- **F5 and F7 open clean.** A styles relationship typed `http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/2007/relationships/styles` with a malformed `word/styles.xml`, a `styles` relationship in `_rels/.rels` to a malformed `word/styles2.xml`, and a comment range without `w:commentReference` with a malformed `word/comments.xml` all open clean, as word-valid predicts.

Session 16 adds, for review AR's suspected items and its finding F1 on layers 89–92:

- **#539: a header referenced only from the glossary.** A `w:headerReference` only in the `w:sectPr` of a glossary `w:docPartBody`, naming a malformed `word/glossary/header9.xml` through the glossary document's own relationships part, makes Word offer recovery. Its well-formed control opens clean, so the malformed header is the cause. Word-valid at 98902c85 passes both; strict fails the malformed one through `xml-syntax`.
- **Endnotes referenced only from a footnote open clean.** A `w:endnoteReference` only inside a footnote (the main document references the footnote) with a malformed `word/endnotes.xml` opens clean, as does its well-formed control. Word does not follow every story's references, and word-valid passes both.
- **#540: a MIME parameter on a content type.** Word offers recovery for the main part's `Override` with the main type plus `; charset=utf-8`, the styles `Override` with the styles type plus `; charset=utf-8`, and the styles `Override` `application/xml; charset=utf-8`. Word-valid and strict at 98902c85 pass all three.
- **#535 (F1): a main part stored elsewhere, typed by a generic Default.** A main part stored as `word/document.bin` typed by `Default Extension="bin" ContentType="text/xml"`, and one stored as `docProps/document.xml` typed by a `text/xml` `Default` for `xml`, each make Word offer recovery. Word-valid at 98902c85 fails both through `word-part-content-type-generic`, and strict passes both. A `.bin` main typed by a `bin` `Default` with the main type opens clean.

Session 17 adds, for the questions session 16 left open:

- **#549: the glossary reads like a main document.** The glossary document's own relationships part, missing its root end tag or zero bytes, makes Word offer recovery, even when the glossary references nothing. Malformed footer, footnotes, endnotes and comments parts that the glossary references (`w:footerReference` in its `w:sectPr`; `w:footnoteReference`, `w:endnoteReference`, `w:commentReference` in a `w:docPartBody`) each make Word offer recovery, and each well-formed control opens clean. A malformed header the glossary relates but does not reference opens clean. Word-valid at 3ebe3e7f passes all of them except the malformed footnotes, which it fails through `word-footnote-reference-missing`.
- **#550: content types must equal the part's type, ignoring case.** Word offers recovery for `; charset=utf-8` on the settings, fontTable, webSettings and referenced-header `Override`s; for `;charset=utf-8` (no space) and `; foo=bar` on the main part; for a trailing space on the styles type; and for styles typed by a `Default` `application/xml; charset=utf-8`. The main and styles types in upper case open clean, as do the settings and header controls with the plain type. Word-valid passes every refused shape, and strict fails only the trailing space (`xsd-error`).

Session 18 adds, for review AS's suspected item S3 (#441):

- **A literal non-ASCII stored name is refused alone.** An unreferenced well-formed `word/café.xml` makes Word offer recovery in NFC and in NFD, stored alone, as do the NFC/NFD part pair, an NFC/NFD folder pair and a case pair. Word-valid at ab1fba79 fails all five (`opc-part-name-word-refused`, `opc-equivalent-part-names`), so its failure of NFC/NFD pairs agrees with Word.

Session 19 adds, for the glossary's eagerly parsed parts, which #549 left unobserved:

- **#562: the glossary's own styles, settings, fontTable, webSettings and numbering are read.** Each specimen pairs a reached glossary that references no story with one part related from the glossary's own relationships part (`word/glossary/styles.xml`, `settings.xml`, `fontTable.xml`, `webSettings.xml` or `numbering.xml`, each with its Word `Override`). When that part is missing its root end tag, Word offers recovery, for all five types; every well-formed control opens clean. Word-valid at 4c86cbfe passes all ten. ### Session 33: 04:45Z–05:23Z on 2026-10-25, validator columns at 8b79bc78

Adversarial reviews BE and BG's suspected items on #619 (#623, #624, #625, #631, #632), with clean controls in every chunk. The driver opens each chunk's files in name order, so the controls were queued 4th and 5th of 8 in `s33a`, last in `s33b` and `s33e`, 5th and 6th of 8 in `s33c`, and 3rd and 4th of 6 in `s33d` ([#671](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/671)). In every chunk Word stalled or crashed on a specimen, and the driver reopened it in a later pass, after the rest of the queue, so a specimen reopened after both controls ([#672](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/672)). `s33c`–`s33e` were built at 5cd8ada8, whose tree is 8b79bc78's, so one pair of validator columns holds for every chunk. Where a specimen renders, the PDF Word wrote says whether Word read the reference: session 26's footer prints "Footer" under the minimal document's "Hello".

### Session 34: 06:02Z–06:09Z on 2026-10-25, validator columns at ef5d8107

The adversarial review of #632's fix (empryo devin/swe-2), findings 1, 2 and 4 (#634, #635, #636), each wrapped shape beside its direct twin, with clean controls in every chunk. The specimens sort before their chunk's controls, so the controls were queued last: two each in `s34a` and `s34b`, and the one control in each of `s34c` and `s34d` ([#671](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/671)). In `s34a` and `s34b` Word stalled or crashed on a specimen, and the driver reopened it in a later pass, after the controls ([#672](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/672)). In `s34c` Word crashed on the control after the specimen's declined recovery offer, and the control opened clean after the driver relaunched Word ([#673](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/673)).

```python
"""Stage the 56 never-probed package fixtures for Word session 41.

Bytes come from git (wfv/release-deadline), never from a working tree, and are
checked against the sha256 recorded in .scratch/pin-136/verdicts.json. Pairs stay
adjacent; each chunk holds 7 fixtures plus a known-clean control queued last.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate")
ROOT = REPO / ".scratch/word-probes"
REF = "wfv/release-deadline"
verdicts = json.loads((REPO / ".scratch/pin-136/verdicts.json").read_text())
by_path = {v["relativePath"]: v for v in verdicts}

pairs = [
    ["broken/package.drawing-arc-radius.docx", "working/package.drawing-arc-radius-integer.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-anchor-open.docx", "working/package.word-anchor-open-repaired.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-attached-toolbar-utf8.docx", "working/package.word-attached-toolbar-utf8-repaired.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-cell-ends-with-table.docx", "working/package.word-cell-ends-with-table-repaired.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-choice-requires-on-descendant.docx", "working/package.word-choice-requires-on-ancestor.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-choice-requires-undeclared.docx", "working/package.word-choice-requires-declared.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-drawing-extent-negative-cx.docx", "broken/package.word-drawing-extent-negative-cy.docx",
     "broken/package.word-drawing-extent-negative.docx", "working/package.word-drawing-extent-positive.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-duplicate-font-table.docx", "working/package.word-duplicate-font-table-removed.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-duplicate-settings.docx", "working/package.word-duplicate-settings-removed.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-duplicate-theme.docx", "working/package.word-duplicate-theme-removed.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-duplicate-web-settings.docx", "working/package.word-duplicate-web-settings-removed.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-empty-drawing.docx", "working/package.word-empty-drawing-removed.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-footnote-reference-missing.docx", "working/package.word-footnote-reference-present.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-hyperlink-relationship.docx", "working/package.word-hyperlink-relationship-repaired.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-move-from-deleted-text.docx", "working/package.word-move-from-text.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-numbering-picture-bullet.docx", "working/package.word-numbering-picture-bullet-removed.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-row-without-cell.docx", "working/package.word-row-without-cell-repaired.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-sdt-id-empty.docx", "working/package.word-sdt-id-empty-repaired.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-text-contains-paragraph.docx", "working/package.word-text-contains-paragraph-lifted.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-textbox-choice-deleted-text.docx", "working/package.word-textbox-fallback-deleted-text.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-textbox-deleted-instruction.docx", "working/package.word-textbox-inner-deletion.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-textbox-deleted-text-shape.docx", "working/package.word-textbox-deleted-text-shape-repaired.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-textbox-deleted-text.docx", "working/package.word-textbox-deleted-text-removed.docx"],
    ["broken/package.word-undeclared-part.docx", "working/package.word-undeclared-part-removed.docx"],
    ["broken/package.zip-bytes-after-eocd.docx", "working/package.zip-no-bytes-after-eocd.docx"],
    ["broken/package.zip-concatenated-copy.docx", "working/package.zip-concatenated-copy-removed.docx"],
    ["broken/package.zip-eocd-comment-overrun.docx", "working/package.zip-eocd-comment-declared.docx"],
]
order = [p for pair in pairs for p in pair]
assert len(order) == 56 and len(set(order)) == 56 and set(order) == set(by_path), "pair list must cover the 56 exactly"

control = ROOT / "s40a/src/s40a-control-minimal.docx"
control_sha = hashlib.sha256(control.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
chunks = [order[i:i + 7] for i in range(0, 56, 7)]
for n, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
    label = f"s41{'abcdefgh'[n]}"
    run = ROOT / label
    (run / "src").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    specs = []
    for rel in chunk:
        data = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(REPO), "show", f"{REF}:tests/fixtures/{rel}"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
        sha = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        assert sha == by_path[rel]["sha256"], rel
        name = Path(rel).name
        (run / "src" / name).write_bytes(data)
        v = by_path[rel]
        specs.append({"name": name.removesuffix(".docx"), "relativePath": rel, "file": name, "sha256": sha,
                      "wordValid": {"valid": v["wordValid"]["valid"], "errors": v["wordValid"]["errorCodes"]},
                      "strict": {"valid": v["strict"]["valid"], "errors": v["strict"]["errorCodes"]}})
    cname = f"{label}-control-minimal.docx"
    shutil.copyfile(control, run / "src" / cname)
    specs.append({"name": cname.removesuffix(".docx"), "relativePath": None, "file": cname, "sha256": control_sha,
                  "wordValid": {"valid": True, "errors": []}, "strict": {"valid": True, "errors": []}, "control": True})
    (run / "specimens.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps(s) + "\n" for s in specs))
    print(label, len(specs), [s["file"] for s in specs])

`stage_pass2.py`:

```python
"""Give each session-41 chunk a pass2/ run dir with byte-identical src and specimens."""
import hashlib
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
for label in sys.argv[1:]:
    run = ROOT / label
    second = run / "pass2"
    (second / "src").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    for src in sorted((run / "src").iterdir()):
        dst = second / "src" / src.name
        shutil.copyfile(src, dst)
        assert hashlib.sha256(src.read_bytes()).digest() == hashlib.sha256(dst.read_bytes()).digest(), src
    shutil.copyfile(run / "specimens.jsonl", second / "specimens.jsonl")
    print(label, "pass2 staged:", len(list((second / "src").iterdir())), "files")

`logcheck.py`:

```python
"""Read each file's Word verdict straight from a word_pdf.py run's own log.

Usage: python3 -I logcheck.py RUN_DIR [RUN_DIR ...]

A run dir holds src/, pdf/manifest.jsonl, word_pdf.log and (optionally) the
outcomes.jsonl that wordpdf_outcomes.py wrote. The verdict here is derived
independently of outcomes.jsonl, from the dialog text the driver logged:

- "Word found unreadable content in <staged>"            -> repair-warning
- "Word experienced an error trying to open ... (<staged>" -> open-error
- any other dialog naming the staged file                  -> other-dialog
- a non-empty PDF and no dialog naming the file            -> clean-open

Staged names are NNNNN__wfv__<file>, NNNNN being the file's index in sorted
order; Word truncates long names, so dialogs are tied to files by that index.
Writes RUN_DIR/logcheck.jsonl and prints one row per file.
"""
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

RECORD_START = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d+ \| ")
DIALOG_MARKERS = ("Word said: ", "Microsoft Word says: ", "-- Word window text: ")
STAGED = re.compile(r"(\d{5})__wfv__")
FULL_STAGED = re.compile(r"(\d{5})__wfv__([^\s\"'()]+?\.docx)")


def records(log: str) -> list[str]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for line in log.splitlines():
        if RECORD_START.match(line) or not out:
            out.append(line)
        else:
            out[-1] += "\n" + line
    return out


def dialog_texts(record: str) -> list[str]:
    texts = []
    for marker in DIALOG_MARKERS:
        start = 0
        while (at := record.find(marker, start)) != -1:
            body = record[at + len(marker):]
            end = body.find("\n-- ")
            texts.append(body if end == -1 else body[:end])
            start = at + len(marker)
    return texts


def kind_of(text: str) -> str:
    if "found unreadable content" in text:
        return "repair-warning"
    if "experienced an error trying to open" in text:
        return "open-error"
    if "password" in text.lower():
        return "password-prompt"
    return "other-dialog"


def check(run: Path) -> list[dict]:
    names = sorted(p.name for p in (run / "src").iterdir() if p.suffix == ".docx")
    log = (run / "word_pdf.log").read_text(errors="replace")
    for index, name in FULL_STAGED.findall(log):
        assert names[int(index)] == name, f"{run}: staged index {index} is {name}, sorted order says {names[int(index)]}"
    manifest = {}
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        manifest[row["original_filename"]] = row
    outcomes = {}
    if (run / "outcomes.jsonl").exists():
        for line in (run / "outcomes.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
            row = json.loads(line)
            outcomes[row["file"]] = row["word"]["outcome"]
    evidence: dict[int, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {i: [] for i in range(len(names))}
    for record in records(log):
        stamp = record[:23]
        for text in dialog_texts(record):
            for index in {int(i) for i in STAGED.findall(text)}:
                flat = " ".join(text.split())
                item = (kind_of(text), f"{stamp} {flat if len(flat) <= 160 else flat[:100] + ' … ' + flat[-55:]}")
                if item[0] not in {k for k, _ in evidence[index]}:
                    evidence[index].append(item)
    rows = []
    for index, name in enumerate(names):
        kinds = [k for k, _ in evidence[index]]
        entry = manifest.get(name, {})
        pdf = Path(entry.get("path_out") or "/nonexistent")
        pdf_ok = entry.get("status") == "ok" and pdf.is_file() and pdf.stat().st_size > 0
        if "repair-warning" in kinds:
            verdict = "repair-warning"
        elif "open-error" in kinds:
            verdict = "open-error"
        elif kinds:
            verdict = kinds[0]
        elif pdf_ok:
            verdict = "clean-open"
        else:
            verdict = "no-evidence"
        conflict = (verdict == "clean-open") != pdf_ok
        rows.append({"file": name, "staged": f"{index:05d}__wfv__{name}", "logVerdict": verdict,
                     "outcomesVerdict": outcomes.get(name), "pdf": pdf_ok, "status": entry.get("status"),
                     "conflict": conflict, "evidence": [e for _, e in evidence[index]]
                     or ([f"PDF {pdf.name} ({pdf.stat().st_size} bytes), no dialog named the file"] if pdf_ok else [])})
    (run / "logcheck.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps(r) + "\n" for r in rows))
    return rows


for arg in sys.argv[1:]:
    run = Path(arg)
    print(f"== {run}")
    for r in check(run):
        flag = "" if r["logVerdict"] == r["outcomesVerdict"] and not r["conflict"] else "  <-- MISMATCH"
        print(f"  {r['file']:<52} log={r['logVerdict']:<15} table={r['outcomesVerdict']!s:<15}{flag}")
        for e in r["evidence"]:
            print(f"      {e}")

"""Join both passes of every session-41 chunk: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts."""
import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
rows, problems = [], []
for label in [f"s41{c}" for c in "abcdefgh"]:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        verdicts = {p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]}
        agreed = len(verdicts) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(p1["logVerdict"]) if agreed else "unknown"
        word_clean = outcome == "clean-open"
        validator_ok = spec["wordValid"]["valid"]
        row = {"chunk": label, "file": name, "relativePath": spec.get("relativePath"), "sha256": spec["sha256"],
               "pass1": p1["logVerdict"], "pass2": p2["logVerdict"], "agreed": agreed, "outcome": outcome,
               "wordValid": validator_ok, "validatorMatchesWord": agreed and validator_ok == word_clean,
               "control": bool(spec.get("control"))}
        rows.append(row)
        if not agreed or not row["validatorMatchesWord"]:
            problems.append(row)
(ROOT / "s41/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
fixtures = [r for r in rows if not r["control"]]
print("files:", len(rows), "fixtures:", len(fixtures), "controls:", len(rows) - len(fixtures))
print("both passes + both logs agree:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
print("validator word-valid matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
by = Counter((r["relativePath"] or "control").split("/")[0] + " " + r["outcome"] for r in rows)
for k, v in sorted(by.items()):
    print(f"  {k}: {v}")
print("problems:", json.dumps(problems, indent=1) if problems else "none")
```

`record.py`:

```python
"""Write the session-41 Word observations into the layer-136 manifest.

Broken entries: replace the 'unknown' placeholder pinned in 3308e0a4 (Word had
never been asked, so there is no observation to retire into history).
Working twins: add entries with the validator verdicts of .scratch/pin-136.
observedAt is the end of the confirming second pass (UTC, from pdf/manifest.jsonl).
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate")
MANIFEST = REPO / ".scratch/wt-136/tests/fixtures-all.manifest.json"
PROBES = REPO / ".scratch/word-probes"
m = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text())
results = [r for r in json.loads((PROBES / "s41/results.json").read_text()) if not r["control"]]
verdicts = {v["relativePath"]: v for v in json.loads((REPO / ".scratch/pin-136/verdicts.json").read_text())}
by_path = {e["relativePath"]: e for e in m["entries"]}
assert len(results) == 56 and all(r["agreed"] and r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in results)

def observed_at(chunk: str, file: str) -> str:
    for line in (PROBES / chunk / "pass2/pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            at = datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
            return at.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z")
    raise KeyError(file)

updated = added = 0
for r in results:
    rel, sha = r["relativePath"], r["sha256"]
    assert verdicts[rel]["sha256"] == sha, rel
    word = {"outcome": r["outcome"], "sha256": sha, "observedAt": observed_at(r["chunk"], r["file"]), "wordVersion": "16.115"}
    if rel.startswith("broken/"):
        entry = by_path[rel]
        assert entry["word"] == {"outcome": "unknown", "sha256": sha}, rel
        entry["word"] = word
        updated += 1
    else:
        assert rel.startswith("working/") and rel not in by_path, rel
        v = verdicts[rel]
        m["entries"].append({"relativePath": rel, "strict": v["strict"], "lenient": v["lenient"], "word": word})
        added += 1
assert all(e["relativePath"].isascii() for e in m["entries"])
m["entries"].sort(key=lambda e: e["relativePath"])
m["totalFixtures"] = len(m["entries"])
MANIFEST.write_text(json.dumps(m, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
print("updated", updated, "added", added, "total", m["totalFixtures"])
```

`control-verdict.mts`:

```ts
// word-valid/strict verdicts of a session-41 control at the wt-136 head, computed as verdicts.mts does.
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { validate } from "../../wt-136/src/scripts/office/validate.js";

const file = process.argv[2];
const run = async (profile: "strict" | "word-valid") => {
    const r = await validate(file, { profile });
    const errorCodes = Array.from(
        new Set(
            r.issues
                .filter((i) => i.severity === "error")
                .map((i) => i.code)
                .filter((c): c is string => Boolean(c)),
        ),
    ).sort();
    return { valid: r.valid, errorCodes };
};
const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(file)).digest("hex");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ file, sha256, wordValid: await run("word-valid"), strict: await run("strict") }));
```

"""Render the session-41 observations section of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md."""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
verdicts = {v["relativePath"]: v for v in json.loads(Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/pin-136/verdicts.json").read_text())}
CONTROL = {"wordValid": {"valid": True, "errorCodes": []}, "strict": {"valid": True, "errorCodes": []}}  # control-verdict.mts at c0a244f5

def cell(v):
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{c}`" for c in v["errorCodes"])

def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)

rows, raw = [], []
for label in [f"s41{c}" for c in "abcdefgh"]:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        v = verdicts.get(s["relativePath"], CONTROL)
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        name = f"`{s['relativePath']}`" if s["relativePath"] else f"`{s['name']}` (control)"
        rows.append(f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | {name} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
                    f"{checks[0][s['file']]['logVerdict']} | {checks[1][s['file']]['logVerdict']} | {cell(v['wordValid'])} | {cell(v['strict'])} |")
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            raw.append(json.dumps({"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "relativePath": s["relativePath"], "sha256": s["sha256"],
                                   "observedAt": t.isoformat(), "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"],
                                   "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"], "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))

scripts = ["build.py", "stage_pass2.py", "logcheck.py", "compare.py", "record.py", "control-verdict.mts", "section.py"]
out = ["### Session 41: 01:16Z–01:52Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at c0a244f5", "",
       "The 56 package fixtures layer 136 pins: the 29 `tests/fixtures/broken/package.*` single-defect specimens and their 27 `tests/fixtures/working/package.*` twins, "

       "Each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (`logcheck.py`, below) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. "
       "A row counts only when both runs and both readings agree, and all 64 do. "
       "The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Rows are listed in staging order; the driver opens a chunk's files in name order.", "",
       "| Run | Observed | Fixture | SHA-256 (first 16) | Word, run 1 | Word, run 2 | word-valid at c0a244f5 | strict at c0a244f5 |",
       "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |", *rows, "",
       "<details><summary>Raw records, session 41</summary>", "", "```jsonl", *raw, "```", "", "</details>", "",
       "<details><summary>Session 41 staging, log check, cross-check and manifest scripts</summary>", ""]
for name in scripts:
    lang = "ts" if name.endswith(".mts") else "python"
    out += [f"`{name}`:", "", f"```{lang}", (ROOT / "s41" / name).read_text().rstrip("\n"), "```", ""]
out += ["</details>", ""]
(ROOT / "s41/section.md").write_text("\n".join(out))
print(len(rows), "rows,", len(raw), "raw records")

### Session 42: 03:40Z–03:53Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at b6b80433

The stored item names `opc-item-name-refused` reports and the package view refuses (#629), for the kinds no earlier session had probed. Each specimen is `MINIMAL_PARTS` plus one unreferenced, well-formed `<x/>` entry, built with `buildRawZip` (the name verbatim in the local header and the central directory), so the specimens differ only in that entry's stored name. `629-name-control` stores the entry as `word/xtra.xml`, which places a part; `629-dotdot-segment` repeats session 3's `..` finding with the name in both headers. Each chunk ends with session 40's minimal control, queued last ([#671](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/671)). Every chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. A cell shows both readings when they differ. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; 10 of the 11 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Rows are listed in builder order; the driver opens a chunk's files in name order.

`s42builder.mts`:

```ts
// Session 42 (2026-10-26): Word's verdict on the stored item names `opc-item-name-refused` (#629) reports and the
// package view refuses, for the kinds no session probed: a leading `/` or `\`, a drive (`C:/…`, `c:…`), and an empty,
// `.` or `...` segment. Each specimen is MINIMAL_PARTS plus one unreferenced, well-formed `<x/>` entry, built with
// buildRawZip (the name verbatim in the local header and the central directory), so the specimens differ only in that
// entry's stored name. `629-name-control` stores it as `word/xtra.xml`, which places a part (session 3 opened
// `foo/xtra.xml` clean). `629-dotdot-segment` repeats session 3's `..` finding with the name in both headers, as the
// known positive. Each chunk ends with the s40a control's exact bytes (MINIMAL_PARTS through JSZip, sha b705a9a7…),
// which Word opened clean in sessions 40 and 41; rebuilding it would change JSZip's entry dates.
// Run from the layer 136 worktree root as a copy: BUILD_DIR=<chunk>/src CHUNK=s42a pnpm exec tsx s42builder.tmp.mts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { validate } from "./src/scripts/office/validate";
import { MINIMAL_PARTS } from "./tests/support/minimal-docx";
import { buildRawZip } from "./tests/support/raw-zip";

const withExtraEntry = (name: string) => async (): Promise<Uint8Array> =>
    buildRawZip([...Object.entries(MINIMAL_PARTS).map(([part, content]) => ({ name: part, content })), { name, content: "<x/>" }]);
const S40A_CONTROL = "/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes/s40a/src/s40a-control-minimal.docx";
const control = async (): Promise<Uint8Array> => {
    const bytes = readFileSync(S40A_CONTROL);
    const sha = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    if (!sha.startsWith("b705a9a7e3509d7e")) throw new Error(`s40a control changed: ${sha}`);
    return bytes;
};

const chunks: Record<string, Array<[string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>]>> = {
    s42a: [
        ["629-leading-slash", "#629: unreferenced entry stored as `/word/xtra.xml`", withExtraEntry("/word/xtra.xml")],
        ["629-leading-backslash", "#629: unreferenced entry stored as `\\word\\xtra.xml`", withExtraEntry("\\word\\xtra.xml")],
        ["629-drive-absolute", "#629: unreferenced entry stored as `C:/word/xtra.xml`", withExtraEntry("C:/word/xtra.xml")],
        ["629-drive-relative", "#629: unreferenced entry stored as `c:xtra.xml`", withExtraEntry("c:xtra.xml")],
        ["629-name-control", "#629 control: the same entry stored as `word/xtra.xml`", withExtraEntry("word/xtra.xml")],
        ["s42a-control-minimal-end", "control", control],
    ],
    s42b: [
        ["629-empty-segment", "#629: unreferenced entry stored as `word//xtra.xml`", withExtraEntry("word//xtra.xml")],
        ["629-dot-segment", "#629: unreferenced entry stored as `word/./xtra.xml`", withExtraEntry("word/./xtra.xml")],
        ["629-triple-dot-segment", "#629: unreferenced entry stored as `word/.../xtra.xml`", withExtraEntry("word/.../xtra.xml")],
        [
            "629-dotdot-segment",
            "#629 known positive (#411): unreferenced entry stored as `word/a/../xtra.xml`",
            withExtraEntry("word/a/../xtra.xml"),
        ],
        ["s42b-control-minimal-end", "control", control],
    ],
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = process.env.BUILD_DIR;
if (!dir) throw new Error("BUILD_DIR is required");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const verdict = async (profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
        try {
            const r = await validate(path.join(dir, file), { profile });
            return {
                valid: r.valid,
                errors: [...new Set(r.issues.filter((x) => x.severity === "error").map((x) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`))],
            };
        } catch (error) {
            return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
        }
    };
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        control: issue === "control" || name === "629-name-control",
        wordValid: await verdict("word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict("strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(path.join(dir, "..", "specimens.jsonl"), JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}

`compare.py`:

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-42 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in ("s42a", "s42b"):
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0]) if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": spec["control"],
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s42/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<34} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} readings={','.join(r['readings'])} word-valid={r['wordValid']} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

`section.py`:

`````python
"""Render the session-42 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s42/section.md.

Reads each chunk's specimens.jsonl (validator columns at b6b80433, written by the builder), both runs'
logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and s42/results.json from compare.py.
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
STORED = {
    "629-leading-slash": "/word/xtra.xml",
    "629-leading-backslash": "\\word\\xtra.xml",
    "629-drive-absolute": "C:/word/xtra.xml",
    "629-drive-relative": "c:xtra.xml",
    "629-name-control": "word/xtra.xml",
    "629-empty-segment": "word//xtra.xml",
    "629-dot-segment": "word/./xtra.xml",
    "629-triple-dot-segment": "word/.../xtra.xml",
    "629-dotdot-segment": "word/a/../xtra.xml",
}
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s42/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


rows, raw = [], []
for label in ("s42a", "s42b"):
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        stored = f"`{STORED[s['name']]}`" if s["name"] in STORED else "none (control)"
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {stored} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            raw.append(json.dumps({"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "storedName": STORED.get(s["name"]), "sha256": s["sha256"],
                                   "observedAt": t.isoformat(), "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"],
                                   "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"], "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))

out = [
    "### Session 42: 03:40Z–03:53Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at b6b80433",
    "",
    "The stored item names `opc-item-name-refused` reports and the package view refuses (#629), for the kinds no earlier session "
    "had probed. Each specimen is `MINIMAL_PARTS` plus one unreferenced, well-formed `<x/>` entry, built with `buildRawZip` "
    "(the name verbatim in the local header and the central directory), so the specimens differ only in that entry's stored name. "
    "`629-name-control` stores the entry as `word/xtra.xml`, which places a part; `629-dotdot-segment` repeats session 3's `..` "
    "finding with the name in both headers. Each chunk ends with session 40's minimal control, queued last "
    "([#671](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/671)). Every chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of "
    "byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by "
    "`wordpdf_outcomes.py`. A cell shows both readings when they differ. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both "
    "readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; 10 of the 11 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and "
    "second runs. Rows are listed in builder order; the driver opens a chunk's files in name order.",
    "",
    "| Run | Observed | Specimen | Stored name | SHA-256 (first 16) | Word, run 1 | Word, run 2 | Outcome | word-valid at b6b80433 | strict at b6b80433 |",
    "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    *rows,
    "",
    "<details><summary>Raw records, session 42</summary>",
    "",
    "```jsonl",
    *raw,
    "```",
    "",
    "</details>",
    "",
    "<details><summary>Session 42 builder, cross-check and section scripts</summary>",
    "",
    "Staging the second runs and reading the logs used session 41's `stage_pass2.py` and `logcheck.py`, above, unchanged.",
    "",
]
for name, path, lang in (("s42builder.mts", ROOT / "s42builder.mts", "ts"), ("compare.py", ROOT / "s42/compare.py", "python"),
                         ("section.py", ROOT / "s42/section.py", "python")):
    out += [f"`{name}`:", "", f"````{lang}", path.read_text().rstrip("\n"), "````", ""]
out += ["</details>", ""]
(ROOT / "s42/section.md").write_text("\n".join(out))
print(len(rows), "rows,", len(raw), "raw records")
`````

```ts
// Session 43 (2026-10-26): settle Word's dialog for the empty segment (`word//xtra.xml`), which session 42 left
// `unknown` (it never opened, but run 1's outcomes table read the error that followed the recovery offer). The specimen
// is session 42's exact bytes (sha 3292bc6f…), alone in its chunk so no other broken file shares the batch, and the
// chunk ends with the s40a control's exact bytes (sha b705a9a7…), named to sort last (#671).
// Run from the layer 136 worktree root as a copy: BUILD_DIR=<chunk>/src CHUNK=s43a pnpm exec tsx s43builder.tmp.mts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { validate } from "./src/scripts/office/validate";

const PROBES = "/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes";
const copyOf = (file: string, shaPrefix: string) => async (): Promise<Uint8Array> => {
    const bytes = readFileSync(path.join(PROBES, file));
    const sha = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    if (!sha.startsWith(shaPrefix)) throw new Error(`${file} changed: ${sha}`);
    return bytes;
};

const chunks: Record<string, Array<[string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>]>> = {
    s43a: [
        [
            "629-empty-segment",
            "#629: unreferenced entry stored as `word//xtra.xml` (session 42's bytes)",
            copyOf("s42b/src/629-empty-segment.docx", "3292bc6f8b7283c9"),
        ],
        ["s43a-control-minimal-end", "control", copyOf("s40a/src/s40a-control-minimal.docx", "b705a9a7e3509d7e")],
    ],
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = process.env.BUILD_DIR;
if (!dir) throw new Error("BUILD_DIR is required");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const verdict = async (profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
        try {
            const r = await validate(path.join(dir, file), { profile });
            return {
                valid: r.valid,
                errors: [...new Set(r.issues.filter((x) => x.severity === "error").map((x) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`))],
            };
        } catch (error) {
            return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
        }
    };
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        control: issue === "control",
        wordValid: await verdict("word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict("strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(path.join(dir, "..", "specimens.jsonl"), JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}
```

`compare.py`:

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-43 chunk: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in ("s43a",):
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0]) if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": spec["control"],
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s43/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<34} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} readings={','.join(r['readings'])} word-valid={r['wordValid']} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

`section.py`:

`````python
"""Render the session-43 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s43/section.md.

Reads each chunk's specimens.jsonl (validator columns at 6473f54b, written by the builder), both runs'
logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and s43/results.json from compare.py.
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
STORED = {
    "629-leading-slash": "/word/xtra.xml",
    "629-leading-backslash": "\\word\\xtra.xml",
    "629-drive-absolute": "C:/word/xtra.xml",
    "629-drive-relative": "c:xtra.xml",
    "629-name-control": "word/xtra.xml",
    "629-empty-segment": "word//xtra.xml",
    "629-dot-segment": "word/./xtra.xml",
    "629-triple-dot-segment": "word/.../xtra.xml",
    "629-dotdot-segment": "word/a/../xtra.xml",
}
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s43/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


rows, raw = [], []
for label in ("s43a",):
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        stored = f"`{STORED[s['name']]}`" if s["name"] in STORED else "none (control)"
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {stored} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            raw.append(json.dumps({"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "storedName": STORED.get(s["name"]), "sha256": s["sha256"],
                                   "observedAt": t.isoformat(), "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"],
                                   "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"], "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))

out = [
    "### Session 43: 06:25Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at 6473f54b",
    "",
    "Settles the empty segment session 42 left `unknown` (#629). The specimen is session 42's `629-empty-segment` "
    "(`word//xtra.xml`), copied byte for byte, alone in its chunk so that no other broken file shares Word's batch. The "
    "chunk ends with session 40's minimal control, queued last "
    "([#671](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/671)). It ran twice, as two separate driver runs of "
    "byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by "
    "`wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` "
    "otherwise; both rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs.",
    "",
    "| Run | Observed | Specimen | Stored name | SHA-256 (first 16) | Word, run 1 | Word, run 2 | Outcome | word-valid at 6473f54b | strict at 6473f54b |",
    "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    *rows,
    "",
    "<details><summary>Raw records, session 43</summary>",
    "",
    "```jsonl",
    *raw,
    "```",
    "",
    "</details>",
    "",
    "<details><summary>Session 43 builder, cross-check and section scripts</summary>",
    "",
    "Staging the second runs and reading the logs used session 41's `stage_pass2.py` and `logcheck.py`, above, unchanged.",
    "",
]
for name, path, lang in (("s43builder.mts", ROOT / "s43builder.mts", "ts"), ("compare.py", ROOT / "s43/compare.py", "python"),
                         ("section.py", ROOT / "s43/section.py", "python")):
    out += [f"`{name}`:", "", f"````{lang}", path.read_text().rstrip("\n"), "````", ""]
out += ["</details>", ""]
(ROOT / "s43/section.md").write_text("\n".join(out))
print(len(rows), "rows,", len(raw), "raw records")
`````
