`s53builder.mts`:

```ts
// Session 53 (2026-10-26): the shapes the review of layers 156-160 says the content-type layers judge without evidence.
// - s53a/s53b (#739): a second relationship to an eagerly read part. A footer relationship the body references, to the
//   main document, the related numbering part or the styles part, each typed with another Word type (session 50's and
//   49's refused shapes), with a calibration typed correctly; and the styles part also the target of the main
//   document's settings relationship, typed with the settings type (and its calibration typed styles).
// - s53b-s53h (#740): shapes the recovery sentence cites a session for but Word was never shown. Settings, fontTable and
//   numbering typed with the four other s49a/s50c spellings (session 50 showed `application/octet-stream` only); the
//   main document typed with each other mapped Word type (session 50 showed the styles type only); settings,
//   numbering and styles typed with other mapped types (sessions 49/50 showed one pair each); an empty numbering
//   ContentType (layer 157 covers styles, settings and fontTable only).
// Run from a worktree root as a copy: BUILD_DIR=<chunk>/src CHUNK=s53a pnpm exec tsx s53builder.tmp.mts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } from "./tests/support/minimal-docx";
import { validate } from "./src/scripts/office/validate";

const W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main";
const REL = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships";
const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const SIDECAR = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const MAIN_TYPE = `${WML}.document.main+xml`;
const STYLES_TYPE = `${WML}.styles+xml`;
const P = MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>;
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n`;

type Kind = "numbering" | "settings" | "fontTable";
/** The relationship segment, the part body and the content type of each kind (the bodies session 47 used). */
const KINDS: Record<Kind, { root: string; ct: string }> = {
    numbering: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:numbering xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.numbering+xml` },
    settings: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:settings xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.settings+xml` },
    fontTable: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:fonts xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.fontTable+xml` },
};
/** The other mapped Word content types the rows type a part with. */
const TYPES = {
    main: MAIN_TYPE,
    styles: STYLES_TYPE,
    theme: "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.theme+xml",
    glossary: `${WML}.document.glossary+xml`,
    header: `${WML}.header+xml`,
    footer: `${WML}.footer+xml`,
    footnotes: `${WML}.footnotes+xml`,
    endnotes: `${WML}.endnotes+xml`,
    comments: `${WML}.comments+xml`,
    settings: KINDS.settings.ct,
    fontTable: KINDS.fontTable.ct,
    numbering: KINDS.numbering.ct,
};
const SPELLINGS: Array<[string, string]> = [
    ["octet-upper", "APPLICATION/OCTET-STREAM"],
    ["octet-charset", "application/octet-stream; charset=utf-8"],
    ["image-png", "image/png"],
    ["foo-xml", "application/foo+xml"],
];

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string, to: string) => {
    if (text.split(from).length !== 2) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};
const relationship = (id: string, segment: string, target: string) =>
    `<Relationship Id="${id}" Type="${REL}/${segment}" Target="${target}"/>`;
const appendRels = (rels: string, extra: string) => replaceOnce(rels, "</Relationships>", `${extra}</Relationships>`);
const overrides = (ct: string, ...entries: Array<[string, string]>) =>
    replaceOnce(
        ct,
        "</Types>",
        `${entries.map(([part, type]) => `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`).join("")}</Types>`,
    );
const retype = (ct: string, part: string, own: string, type: string) =>
    replaceOnce(ct, `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${own}"/>`, `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`);
const control = () => buildDocx({ ...P });

/** The minimal package plus `word/<kind>.xml` related from the main document's sidecar as rId2, typed `type`. */
const withRelated = (kind: Kind, type = KINDS[kind].ct): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    [`word/${kind}.xml`]: KINDS[kind].root,
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rId2", kind, `${kind}.xml`)),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, [`word/${kind}.xml`, type]),
});
const relatedTyped = (kind: Kind, type: string) => buildDocx(withRelated(kind, type));
const mainTyped = (type: string) => buildDocx({ ...P, [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/document.xml", MAIN_TYPE, type) });
const stylesTyped = (type: string) => buildDocx({ ...P, [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/styles.xml", STYLES_TYPE, type) });

/** `parts` plus a footer relationship (rIdF) to `target` (relative to word/) that the body's section references. */
const withReadFooter = (parts: Record<string, string>, target: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...parts,
    "word/document.xml": replaceOnce(
        replaceOnce(parts["word/document.xml"]!, `xmlns:w="${W}"`, `xmlns:w="${W}" xmlns:r="${REL}"`),
        "<w:sectPr>",
        `<w:sectPr><w:footerReference w:type="default" r:id="rIdF"/>`,
    ),
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(parts[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdF", "footer", target)),
});
const mainFooterCoReach = (type: string) =>
    buildDocx(withReadFooter({ ...P, [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/document.xml", MAIN_TYPE, type) }, "document.xml"));
const numberingFooterCoReach = (type: string) => buildDocx(withReadFooter(withRelated("numbering", type), "numbering.xml"));
const stylesFooterCoReach = (type: string) =>
    buildDocx(withReadFooter({ ...P, [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/styles.xml", STYLES_TYPE, type) }, "styles.xml"));
/** The styles part also the target of the main document's settings relationship (review S5), typed `type`. */
const stylesSettingsCoReach = (type: string) =>
    buildDocx({
        ...P,
        [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rId2", "settings", "styles.xml")),
        [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/styles.xml", STYLES_TYPE, type),
    });

type Row = [string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>];
const spellingRows = (kind: Kind): Row[] =>
    SPELLINGS.map(([slug, type]) => [
        `${kind.toLowerCase()}-override-${slug}`,
        `#740: a related word/${kind}.xml typed ${type}`,
        () => relatedTyped(kind, type),
    ]);
const mainRow = (name: keyof typeof TYPES): Row => [
    `main-override-${name.toLowerCase()}-type`,
    `#740: main document Override typed with the ${name} content type`,
    () => mainTyped(TYPES[name]),
];
const relatedRow = (kind: Kind, name: keyof typeof TYPES): Row => [
    `${kind.toLowerCase()}-override-${name.toLowerCase()}-type`,
    `#740: a related word/${kind}.xml typed with the ${name} content type`,
    () => relatedTyped(kind, TYPES[name]),
];
const stylesRow = (name: keyof typeof TYPES): Row => [
    `styles-override-${name.toLowerCase()}-type`,
    `#740: word/styles.xml typed with the ${name} content type`,
    () => stylesTyped(TYPES[name]),
];
const withControls = (chunk: string, rows: Row[]): Row[] => [
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal`, "control", control],
    ...rows,
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal-end`, "control", control],
];
const [fontTableSpellings, numberingSpellings, settingsSpellings] = [
    spellingRows("fontTable"),
    spellingRows("numbering"),
    spellingRows("settings"),
];

const chunks: Record<string, Row[]> = {
    s53a: withControls("s53a", [
        [
            "coreach-footer-main-calibration",
            "#739 calibration: a footer relationship the body references targets word/document.xml, typed main",
            () => mainFooterCoReach(MAIN_TYPE),
        ],
        [
            "coreach-footer-main-styles-type",
            "#739: the same, the main document typed with the styles content type",
            () => mainFooterCoReach(STYLES_TYPE),
        ],
        [
            "coreach-footer-numbering-calibration",
            "#739 calibration: a footer relationship the body references targets the related word/numbering.xml, typed numbering",
            () => numberingFooterCoReach(KINDS.numbering.ct),
        ],
        [
            "coreach-footer-numbering-settings-type",
            "#739: the same, numbering typed with the settings content type",
            () => numberingFooterCoReach(KINDS.settings.ct),
        ],
        [
            "coreach-footer-styles-calibration",
            "#739 calibration: a footer relationship the body references targets word/styles.xml, typed styles",
            () => stylesFooterCoReach(STYLES_TYPE),
        ],
        [
            "coreach-footer-styles-settings-type",
            "#739: the same, styles typed with the settings content type",
            () => stylesFooterCoReach(KINDS.settings.ct),
        ],
    ]),
    s53b: withControls("s53b", [
        [
            "coreach-settings-styles-calibration",
            "#739 calibration: word/styles.xml is also the target of the main document's settings relationship, typed styles",
            () => stylesSettingsCoReach(STYLES_TYPE),
        ],
        [
            "coreach-settings-styles-settings-type",
            "#739 (review S5): the same, styles typed with the settings content type",
            () => stylesSettingsCoReach(KINDS.settings.ct),
        ],
        ...settingsSpellings,
    ]),
    s53c: withControls("s53c", [...fontTableSpellings, ...numberingSpellings.slice(0, 2)]),
    s53d: withControls("s53d", [
        ...numberingSpellings.slice(2),
        [
            "numbering-override-empty",
            '#740: a related word/numbering.xml whose Override has ContentType=""',
            () => relatedTyped("numbering", ""),
        ],
        mainRow("theme"),
        mainRow("glossary"),
        mainRow("header"),
    ]),
    s53e: withControls("s53e", [
        mainRow("footer"),
        mainRow("footnotes"),
        mainRow("endnotes"),
        mainRow("comments"),
        mainRow("settings"),
        mainRow("fontTable"),
    ]),
    s53f: withControls("s53f", [
        mainRow("numbering"),
        relatedRow("settings", "main"),
        relatedRow("settings", "numbering"),
        relatedRow("settings", "header"),
        relatedRow("settings", "fontTable"),
        relatedRow("settings", "theme"),
    ]),
    s53g: withControls("s53g", [
        relatedRow("numbering", "main"),
        relatedRow("numbering", "styles"),
        relatedRow("numbering", "header"),
        relatedRow("numbering", "fontTable"),
        stylesRow("main"),
        stylesRow("numbering"),
    ]),
    s53h: withControls("s53h", [
        stylesRow("header"),
        stylesRow("fontTable"),
        stylesRow("theme"),
        stylesRow("comments"),
        relatedRow("settings", "comments"),
        relatedRow("numbering", "comments"),
    ]),
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = process.env.BUILD_DIR;
if (!dir) throw new Error("BUILD_DIR is required");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const verdict = async (profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
        try {
            const r = await validate(path.join(dir, file), { profile });
            return {
                valid: r.valid,
                errors: [...new Set(r.issues.filter((x) => x.severity === "error").map((x) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`))],
            };
        } catch (error) {
            return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
        }
    };
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        wordValid: await verdict("word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict("strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(path.join(dir, "..", "specimens.jsonl"), JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}

"""Join both passes of the session-53 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
CHUNKS = ("s53a", "s53b", "s53c", "s53d", "s53e", "s53f", "s53g", "s53h")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0]) if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": "control-minimal" in spec["name"],
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s53/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

"""Render the session-53 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s53/section.md.

Reads the chunk's specimens.jsonl (validator columns at 0b26c414, written by the builder), both runs'
logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and s53/results.json from compare.py.
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
CHUNKS = ("s53a", "s53b", "s53c", "s53d", "s53e", "s53f", "s53g", "s53h")
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s53/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


rows, raw, starts, ends = [], [], [], []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        starts.append(times[0])
        ends.append(times[1])
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        shape = s["issue"].replace("|", "\\|")
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {shape} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            raw.append(json.dumps({"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "sha256": s["sha256"],
                                   "observedAt": t.isoformat(), "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"],
                                   "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"], "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))

out = [
    f"### Session 53: {min(starts):%H:%M}Z–{max(ends):%H:%M}Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at 0b26c414",
    "",
    "The content-type shapes the review of layers 156–160 says those layers judge, or explain with a session, that no earlier session "
    "showed Word ([#739](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/739): a second relationship to an eagerly read part; "
    "[#740](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/740): the spellings and types the recovery sentence cites a session for). "
    "Each chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word "
    "log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings "
    "agree, and `unknown` otherwise; all 64 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is "
    "the builder's description of the specimen. The part bodies are session 47's empty roots.",
    "",
    "- A footer relationship the body references (`w:footerReference`) whose target is the main document, the related numbering part "
    "or the styles part gets the recovery offer, typed with its own type (the calibrations) and typed with session 49's and 50's refused "
    "types alike. So does `word/styles.xml` when the main document's settings relationship also targets it, typed styles or typed "
    "settings. Word-valid accepts all eight: false negatives, and the review's shapes are refused whatever the Override says.",
    "- `word/settings.xml`, `word/fontTable.xml` and `word/numbering.xml`, related by the main document, get the recovery offer typed "
    "`APPLICATION/OCTET-STREAM`, `application/octet-stream; charset=utf-8`, `image/png` or `application/foo+xml` (session 50 showed "
    "`application/octet-stream` only). Word-valid rejects all twelve.",
    "- The main document gets the recovery offer typed with the theme, glossary, header, footer, footnotes, endnotes, comments, "
    "settings, fontTable or numbering content type (session 50 showed the styles type only); word-valid rejects all ten.",
    "- A related settings part typed with the main document, numbering, header, fontTable, theme or comments type, a related numbering "
    "part typed with the main document, styles, header, fontTable or comments type, and the styles part typed with the main document, "
    "numbering, header, fontTable, theme or comments type all get the recovery offer; word-valid rejects all sixteen.",
    "- A related numbering part whose Override has `ContentType=\"\"` gets the recovery offer, as styles (session 49) and settings and "
    "fontTable (session 50) did. Word-valid accepts it: a false negative.",
    "",
    "| Run | Observed | Specimen | Shape | SHA-256 (first 16) | Word, run 1 | Word, run 2 | Outcome | word-valid at 0b26c414 | strict at 0b26c414 |",
    "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    *rows,
    "",
    "<details><summary>Raw records, session 53</summary>",
    "",
    "```jsonl",
    *raw,

    "",

### Session 54: 13:38Z–13:40Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at 0b26c414

The shapes three follow-ups need before they land: the broken relationship targets whose `rels-broken` verdict [#734](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/734) moves from the Target's spelling to the part it resolves to; the attached-toolbar spellings and the empty id of [#743](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/743) (the review of layers 151–155, findings 2, 3 and S1); and the four duplicate cells session 50 did not show ([#744](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/744), finding 4). Each chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; all 27 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen.

- A `customXml` relationship from the main document's relationships part to an absent package-root `customXml/item1.xml` gets the recovery offer however the Target spells it: `../customXml/item1.xml` (vectors.docx's shape, the calibration), `/customXml/item1.xml`, `..\customXml\item1.xml`, `../CUSTOMXML/%69tem1.xml`, and `../../customXml/item1.xml`, whose extra `..` stays at the package root as RFC 3986 removes dot segments. Word-valid at 0b26c414 rejects only the calibration and the last: three false negatives.
- An image relationship to an absent `media/_rels/x.png`, `notes.rels` or `word/../customXml/x.png` opens clean, as the broken `media/image9.png` calibration does, and so does a reached glossary's `customXml` relationship to an absent `../customXml/item1.xml` (which resolves to `word/customXml/item1.xml`). Word-valid at 0b26c414 rejects all four by their spelling: false positives.
- The Word-clean toolbar fixture (`tests/fixtures/working/package.word-attached-toolbar-utf8-repaired.docx`, re-zipped) opens clean unchanged, with its relationships part stored as `word/_rels/customizations.xml.RELS`, and with `wne:toolbarData r:id=""`. Word-valid rejects the `.RELS` spelling through `word-attached-toolbar-relationship`: a false positive. The Word-refused fixture (`tests/fixtures/broken/package.word-attached-toolbar-utf8.docx`) gets the recovery offer unchanged and with `word/customizations.xml` and its relationships part stored with `.XML` spellings; word-valid passes the `.XML` spelling: a false negative.
- Two fontTable or two webSettings relationships in `_rels/.rels`, beside the main document's own, open clean; two webSettings or two theme relationships in a reached glossary's relationships part get the recovery offer. Word-valid agrees on all four.

// Session 54 (2026-10-26): the shapes three follow-ups need before they land.
// - s54a/s54b (#734): a broken relationship Target the rels-broken verdict reads. Layer 158's lane decides it from the
//   resolved part (a relationships part, or a customXml part outside word/) instead of the Target's spelling, which
//   changes the verdict of spellings Word never saw: the injected ones (media/_rels/x.png, notes.rels,
//   word/../customXml/x.png), a reached glossary's ../customXml/ target, a target above the package root, and the
//   absolute, backslash and escaped spellings of the blocking ../customXml/item1.xml (vectors.docx's shape, the
//   calibration). A broken media target is the tolerated calibration.
// - s54c (#743): the attached-toolbar walk finds the part and its sidecar by literal name. The Word-clean and the
//   Word-refused toolbar fixtures, re-zipped unchanged (calibrations), the clean one with its sidecar spelled .RELS and
//   with an empty wne:toolbarData r:id, and the refused one with the part and sidecar spelled .XML.
// - s54d (#744): the four duplicate cells session 50 did not show: two fontTable and two webSettings relationships in
//   _rels/.rels, two webSettings and two theme relationships in a reached glossary's sidecar.
// Run from a worktree root as a copy: BUILD_DIR=<chunk>/src CHUNK=s54a pnpm exec tsx s54builder.tmp.mts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import JSZip from "jszip";
import { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } from "./tests/support/minimal-docx";
import { validate } from "./src/scripts/office/validate";

const W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main";
const REL = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships";
const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const SIDECAR = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const MAIN_TYPE = `${WML}.document.main+xml`;
const STYLES_TYPE = `${WML}.styles+xml`;
const P = MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>;
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n`;

/** A Word-clean fixture's theme part (Word 16.115 clean-open in the manifest). */
const THEME_XML = await (async () => {
    const zip = await JSZip.loadAsync(readFileSync("tests/fixtures/working/package.drawing-arc-radius-integer.docx"));
    const file = zip.file("word/theme/theme1.xml");
    if (!file) throw new Error("theme fixture lost word/theme/theme1.xml");
    return file.async("string");
})();

type Kind = "numbering" | "settings" | "fontTable" | "webSettings" | "theme";
/** The relationship segment, the part body and the content type of each kind (the bodies session 47 used). */
const KINDS: Record<Kind, { root: string; ct: string }> = {
    numbering: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:numbering xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.numbering+xml` },
    settings: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:settings xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.settings+xml` },
    fontTable: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:fonts xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.fontTable+xml` },
    webSettings: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:webSettings xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.webSettings+xml` },
    theme: { root: THEME_XML, ct: "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.theme+xml" },
};
/** Where a kind's parts live: `theme/theme1.xml` for the theme, `<kind>.xml` otherwise. */
const fileOf = (kind: Kind, n: 1 | 2) => (kind === "theme" ? `theme/theme${n}.xml` : `${kind}${n === 1 ? "" : "2"}.xml`);

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string, to: string) => {
    if (text.split(from).length !== 2) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};
const relationship = (id: string, segment: string, target: string) =>
    `<Relationship Id="${id}" Type="${REL}/${segment}" Target="${target}"/>`;
const relsPart = (body: string) =>
    `${XML_DECL}<Relationships xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships">${body}</Relationships>`;
const appendRels = (rels: string, extra: string) => replaceOnce(rels, "</Relationships>", `${extra}</Relationships>`);
const overrides = (ct: string, ...entries: Array<[string, string]>) =>
    replaceOnce(
        ct,
        "</Types>",
        `${entries.map(([part, type]) => `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`).join("")}</Types>`,
    );
const control = () => buildDocx({ ...P });

/** The minimal package plus `word/<file of kind>` related from the main document's sidecar as rId2. */
const withRelated = (kind: Kind, type = KINDS[kind].ct): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    [`word/${fileOf(kind, 1)}`]: KINDS[kind].root,
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rId2", kind, fileOf(kind, 1))),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, [`word/${fileOf(kind, 1)}`, type]),
});
/** {@link withRelated} with the Override of the related part (or of `part`) carrying `type`. */
const relatedTyped = (kind: Kind, type: string) => buildDocx(withRelated(kind, type));
const retyped = (part: string, own: string, type: string) =>
    buildDocx({
        ...P,
        [CT]: replaceOnce(
            P[CT]!,
            `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${own}"/>`,
            `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`,
        ),
    });
const mainTyped = (type: string) => retyped("word/document.xml", MAIN_TYPE, type);

/** Session 45's refused shape: two relationships of `kind` to two parts in the main document's sidecar. */
const dupInMainRels = (kind: Kind) => {
    const parts = withRelated(kind);
    return buildDocx({
        ...parts,
        [`word/${fileOf(kind, 2)}`]: KINDS[kind].root,
        [SIDECAR]: appendRels(parts[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rId3", kind, fileOf(kind, 2))),
        [CT]: overrides(parts[CT]!, [`word/${fileOf(kind, 2)}`, KINDS[kind].ct]),
    });
};
/** The main document's own `kind` relationship, and two more of `kind` in `_rels/.rels` (s49c's styles shape). */
const dupInPackageRels = (kind: Kind) => {
    const parts = withRelated(kind);
    return buildDocx({
        ...parts,
        [`word/${fileOf(kind, 2)}`]: KINDS[kind].root,
        "_rels/.rels": appendRels(
            P["_rels/.rels"]!,
            `${relationship("rId8", kind, `word/${fileOf(kind, 1)}`)}${relationship("rId9", kind, `word/${fileOf(kind, 2)}`)}`,
        ),
        [CT]: overrides(parts[CT]!, [`word/${fileOf(kind, 2)}`, KINDS[kind].ct]),
    });
};
const HEADER = `${XML_DECL}<w:hdr xmlns:w="${W}"><w:p><w:r><w:t>Header</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:hdr>`;
/** The main document's own `kind` relationship, and a referenced header whose sidecar holds two of `kind`. */
const dupInHeaderRels = (kind: Kind) => {
    const parts = withRelated(kind);
    return buildDocx({
        ...parts,
        [`word/${fileOf(kind, 2)}`]: KINDS[kind].root,
        "word/document.xml": replaceOnce(
            replaceOnce(P["word/document.xml"]!, `xmlns:w="${W}"`, `xmlns:w="${W}" xmlns:r="${REL}"`),
            "<w:sectPr>",
            `<w:sectPr><w:headerReference w:type="default" r:id="rIdH"/>`,
        ),
        "word/header9.xml": HEADER,
        "word/_rels/header9.xml.rels": relsPart(
            `${relationship("rId1", kind, fileOf(kind, 1))}${relationship("rId2", kind, fileOf(kind, 2))}`,
        ),
        [SIDECAR]: appendRels(parts[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdH", "header", "header9.xml")),
        [CT]: overrides(parts[CT]!, ["word/header9.xml", `${WML}.header+xml`], [`word/${fileOf(kind, 2)}`, KINDS[kind].ct]),
    });
};
const GLOSSARY =
    `${XML_DECL}<w:glossaryDocument xmlns:w="${W}"><w:docParts><w:docPart><w:docPartPr><w:name w:val="Part"/>` +
    `<w:category><w:name w:val="General"/><w:gallery w:val="placeholder"/></w:category><w:guid w:val="{6A9E2C40-3F1B-4C55-9D2E-7B1A0C9D4E11}"/></w:docPartPr>` +
    `<w:docPartBody><w:p><w:r><w:t>Part</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:docPartBody></w:docPart></w:docParts></w:glossaryDocument>`;
/** A reached glossary whose own sidecar holds two relationships of `kind` to two parts in its folder (s49c's shape). */
const dupInGlossaryRels = (kind: Kind) =>
    buildDocx({
        ...P,
        "word/glossary/document.xml": GLOSSARY,
        [`word/glossary/${fileOf(kind, 1)}`]: KINDS[kind].root,
        [`word/glossary/${fileOf(kind, 2)}`]: KINDS[kind].root,
        "word/glossary/_rels/document.xml.rels": relsPart(
            `${relationship("rId1", kind, fileOf(kind, 1))}${relationship("rId2", kind, fileOf(kind, 2))}`,
        ),
        [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdG", "glossaryDocument", "glossary/document.xml")),
        [CT]: overrides(
            P[CT]!,
            ["word/glossary/document.xml", `${WML}.document.glossary+xml`],
            [`word/glossary/${fileOf(kind, 1)}`, KINDS[kind].ct],
            [`word/glossary/${fileOf(kind, 2)}`, KINDS[kind].ct],
        ),
    });

type Row = [string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>];
const withControls = (chunk: string, rows: Row[]): Row[] => [
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal`, "control", control],
    ...rows,
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal-end`, "control", control],
];

/** The minimal package plus one relationship of `segment` from the main document's sidecar to an absent `target`. */
const brokenFromMain = (segment: string, target: string) =>
    buildDocx({ ...P, [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rId9", segment, target)) });
/** A reached glossary whose own sidecar relates `segment` to an absent `target` (s49c's glossary shape). */
const brokenFromGlossary = (segment: string, target: string) =>
    buildDocx({
        ...P,
        "word/glossary/document.xml": GLOSSARY,
        "word/glossary/_rels/document.xml.rels": relsPart(relationship("rId1", segment, target)),
        [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdG", "glossaryDocument", "glossary/document.xml")),
        [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, ["word/glossary/document.xml", `${WML}.document.glossary+xml`]),
    });

const CLEAN_TOOLBAR = "tests/fixtures/working/package.word-attached-toolbar-utf8-repaired.docx";
const BROKEN_TOOLBAR = "tests/fixtures/broken/package.word-attached-toolbar-utf8.docx";
/** `fixture` re-zipped with `edit` applied to its entries (renames, text replacements). */
const rezip = async (fixture: string, edit: (zip: JSZip) => Promise<void> = async () => {}) => {
    const zip = await JSZip.loadAsync(readFileSync(fixture));
    await edit(zip);
    return zip.generateAsync({ type: "uint8array", compression: "DEFLATE" });
};
const rename = async (zip: JSZip, from: string, to: string) => {
    const file = zip.file(from);
    if (!file) throw new Error(`no ${from}`);
    const bytes = await file.async("uint8array");
    zip.remove(from);
    zip.file(to, bytes);
};
const emptyToolbarId = async (zip: JSZip) => {
    const file = zip.file("word/customizations.xml");
    if (!file) throw new Error("no word/customizations.xml");
    const xml = await file.async("string");
    const ids = xml.match(/r:id="[^"]*"/g) ?? [];
    if (ids.length !== 1) throw new Error(`expected one r:id, found ${ids.length}`);
    zip.file("word/customizations.xml", xml.replace(ids[0]!, 'r:id=""'));
};

const chunks: Record<string, Row[]> = {

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = process.env.BUILD_DIR;
if (!dir) throw new Error("BUILD_DIR is required");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const verdict = async (profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
        try {
            const r = await validate(path.join(dir, file), { profile });
            return {
                valid: r.valid,
                errors: [...new Set(r.issues.filter((x) => x.severity === "error").map((x) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`))],
            };
        } catch (error) {
            return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
        }
    };
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        wordValid: await verdict("word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict("strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(path.join(dir, "..", "specimens.jsonl"), JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-54 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
CHUNKS = ("s54a", "s54b", "s54c", "s54d")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0]) if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": "control-minimal" in spec["name"],
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s54/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

def run_at(run, file):

        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)

    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"

        )

### Session 55: 14:37Z–14:51Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at 42600284

The shapes the review of layers 161–165 asked Word about: a header Word reads stored with no relationships part, whose references layer 161 handed to `rels-missing-sidecar` ([#751](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/751), finding 1), and a relationship whose TargetMode is spelled `external`, and a `c:chart` naming its relationship in both relationships namespaces ([#753](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/753), findings 6 and 7), with s55d and s55e added after the first three chunks to separate those two shapes from their confounders and to bound the TargetMode rule. Each chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; all 33 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen.

- A header the body references, stored as `word/header1.xml` with no relationships part, gets the recovery offer when it holds a `c:chart r:id="rId1"`, an `o:OLEObject r:id="rId1"`, or a `dgm:relIds` naming all four parts, as the same header does with a relationships part that lacks `rId1` (the calibration); with no `r:` reference it opens clean. Word-valid at 42600284 passes all three: false negatives.
- A relationship whose TargetMode is spelled `external` gets the recovery offer whether a `c:chart` names it, it is the diagramData relationship of session 46's word-clean-strict01 SmartArt, or it is an unreferenced hyperlink relationship in the main document's relationships part; spelled `Internal` or `External` the same packages open clean. Word reads the spelling, not the reference. The unreferenced hyperlink relationship also gets the recovery offer with TargetMode `external` in the package's `_rels/.rels`, and with `External ` (trailing space) or an empty TargetMode in the main document's relationships part; with `external` in a referenced header's own relationships part it opens clean, as with `External`. Word-valid at 42600284 passes all six refused shapes: false negatives.
- A `c:chart` carrying both `r:id` and the ISO Strict `rs:id` cannot be opened (open error, no recovery offer) whether one of the two is empty or both name the real chart relationship; `rs:id` alone in the Transitional document opens clean and draws the chart. Word refuses the second namespace, not the empty id. Word-valid at 42600284 passes all three: false negatives.

// Session 55 (2026-10-26): the shapes #751 and #753 ask Word about.
// - s55a (#751): a header the body references, stored as `word/header1.xml` with NO relationships part, holding a
//   `c:chart r:id`, an `o:OLEObject r:id` or a `dgm:relIds r:dm` that therefore names no relationship. Layer 161
//   hands such a part to `rels-missing-sidecar`, which the header/footer basename tolerance makes a warning, so
//   word-valid at 42600284 passes all three; at 0b26c414 `word-part-reference-relationship` rejected them. Word was
//   never shown the shape. Calibrations: the same header with its relationships part present but no `rId1`, and the
//   header with no relationships part and no `r:` reference. The `dgm:relIds` row names all four parts, as session 52
//   s52d learned the schema refuses `r:dm` alone; the image part ships only with the calibration whose sidecar names it.
// - s55b (#753): a `c:chart r:id` naming a real chart relationship whose TargetMode is spelled `Internal` or
//   `external` (OPC's ST_TargetMode is the exact enumeration Internal | External), and an empty id in one
//   relationships namespace beside the real id in the other, with the plain reference as calibration.
// - s55c (#753): session 46's word-clean-strict01 SmartArt with its diagramData relationship's TargetMode spelled
//   `Internal` or `external`, beside the unmodified package (session 52 s52d: clean).
// - s55d (calibrations for s55b and s55c): `c:chart` carrying both ids real, or only the Strict `rs:id`, separates the
//   empty id from the second relationships namespace; an unreferenced hyperlink relationship with TargetMode `external`
//   (and `External` as calibration) separates the spelling from the reference.
// - s55e (scope of the TargetMode spelling): an unreferenced hyperlink relationship with TargetMode `external` in the
//   package's `_rels/.rels` and in a referenced header's own relationships part (`External` as calibration), and the
//   spellings `External ` and `` in the main document's relationships part.
// Run from a worktree root as a copy: BUILD_DIR=<chunk>/src CHUNK=s55a pnpm exec tsx s55builder.tmp.mts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import JSZip from "jszip";
import { barChartXml, CHART_CONTENT_TYPE } from "./tests/support/chart-specimens";
import { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } from "./tests/support/minimal-docx";
import { validate } from "./src/scripts/office/validate";

const W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main";
const R = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships";
const RS = "http://purl.oclc.org/ooxml/officeDocument/relationships";
const C = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/chart";
const A = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/main";
const WP = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/wordprocessingDrawing";
const DGM = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/diagram";
const O = "urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:office";
const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const MAIN = "word/document.xml";
const SIDECAR = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const CHART = "word/charts/chart1.xml";
const P = MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>;
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n`;
const PNG = Uint8Array.from(
    Buffer.from("iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==", "base64"),
);
const DRAWING_NS = `xmlns:wp="${WP}" xmlns:a="${A}" xmlns:c="${C}" xmlns:dgm="${DGM}" xmlns:o="${O}" xmlns:r="${R}"`;

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string, to: string) => {
    if (text.split(from).length !== 2) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};
const relationship = (id: string, type: string, target: string, mode?: string) =>
    `<Relationship Id="${id}" Type="${type}" Target="${target}"${mode === undefined ? "" : ` TargetMode="${mode}"`}/>`;
const relsPart = (body: string) =>
    `${XML_DECL}<Relationships xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships">${body}</Relationships>`;
const appendRels = (rels: string, extra: string) => replaceOnce(rels, "</Relationships>", `${extra}</Relationships>`);
const withTypes = (types: string, defaults: Array<[string, string]>, overrides: Array<[string, string]>) =>
    replaceOnce(
        replaceOnce(
            types,
            '<Default Extension="rels"',
            `${defaults.map(([ext, type]) => `<Default Extension="${ext}" ContentType="${type}"/>`).join("")}<Default Extension="rels"`,
        ),
        "</Types>",
        `${overrides.map(([part, type]) => `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`).join("")}</Types>`,
    );

/** Session 52's drawings, each in its own paragraph; `ids` is the reference's id attribute(s), verbatim. */
const chartDrawing = (ids: string) =>
    '<w:p><w:r><w:drawing><wp:inline distT="0" distB="0" distL="0" distR="0"><wp:extent cx="5486400" cy="3200400"/>' +
    `<wp:effectExtent l="0" t="0" r="0" b="0"/><wp:docPr id="1" name="Chart 1"/><wp:cNvGraphicFramePr/><a:graphic><a:graphicData uri="${C}">` +
    `<c:chart ${ids}/></a:graphicData></a:graphic></wp:inline></w:drawing></w:r></w:p>`;
const diagramDrawing = (ids: string) =>
    '<w:p><w:r><w:drawing><wp:inline distT="0" distB="0" distL="0" distR="0"><wp:extent cx="952500" cy="952500"/>' +
    `<wp:effectExtent l="0" t="0" r="0" b="0"/><wp:docPr id="1" name="Diagram 1"/><a:graphic><a:graphicData uri="${DGM}">` +
    `<dgm:relIds ${ids}/></a:graphicData></a:graphic></wp:inline></w:drawing></w:r></w:p>`;
const oleObject = (ids: string) =>
    '<w:p><w:r><w:object><o:OLEObject Type="Embed" ProgID="Package" ShapeID="_x0000_i1025" DrawAspect="Icon" ObjectID="_1" ' +
    `${ids}/></w:object></w:r></w:p>`;
const control = () => buildDocx({ ...P });

/** A header the body references through `w:headerReference r:id="rIdH"`, stored as `word/header1.xml`, holding `body`. */
const referencedHeader = (body: string, sidecar?: string) =>
    buildDocx({
        ...P,
        ...(sidecar?.includes("media/image1.png") ? { "word/media/image1.png": PNG } : {}),
        "word/header1.xml": `${XML_DECL}<w:hdr xmlns:w="${W}" ${DRAWING_NS}>${body}</w:hdr>`,
        ...(sidecar === undefined ? {} : { "word/_rels/header1.xml.rels": sidecar }),
        [MAIN]: replaceOnce(
            replaceOnce(P[MAIN]!, `xmlns:w="${W}"`, `xmlns:w="${W}" xmlns:r="${R}"`),
            "<w:sectPr>",
            `<w:sectPr><w:headerReference w:type="default" r:id="rIdH"/>`,
        ),
        [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdH", `${R}/header`, "header1.xml")),
        [CT]: withTypes(P[CT]!, [["png", "image/png"]], [["word/header1.xml", `${WML}.header+xml`]]),
    });

/** The minimal package, `body` before the main document's `w:sectPr` (the Strict relationships prefix `rs` declared), and a real bar chart rId9 names with `mode`. */
const chartWith = (body: string, mode?: string) =>
    buildDocx({
        ...P,
        [CHART]: barChartXml(false),
        [MAIN]: replaceOnce(
            replaceOnce(P[MAIN]!, "<w:document ", `<w:document ${DRAWING_NS} xmlns:rs="${RS}" `),
            "<w:sectPr>",
            `${body}<w:sectPr>`,
        ),
        [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rId9", `${R}/chart`, "charts/chart1.xml", mode)),
        [CT]: withTypes(P[CT]!, [], [[CHART, CHART_CONTENT_TYPE]]),
    });

/** The minimal package with an unreferenced hyperlink relationship rId99 whose TargetMode is spelled `mode`. */
const unreferencedHyperlink = (mode: string) =>
    buildDocx({ ...P, [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rId99", `${R}/hyperlink`, "https://example.com/", mode)) });

const HYPERLINK = (mode: string) => relationship("rId99", `${R}/hyperlink`, "https://example.com/", mode);
const PACKAGE_RELS = "_rels/.rels";
/** The minimal package with the unreferenced hyperlink relationship in `_rels/.rels`. */
const packageHyperlink = (mode: string) => buildDocx({ ...P, [PACKAGE_RELS]: appendRels(P[PACKAGE_RELS]!, HYPERLINK(mode)) });
/** A referenced header whose own relationships part holds only the unreferenced hyperlink relationship. */
const headerHyperlink = (mode: string) => referencedHeader("<w:p><w:r><w:t>header</w:t></w:r></w:p>", relsPart(HYPERLINK(mode)));

/** Session 46's word-clean-strict01 package with its diagramData relationship rId35's TargetMode spelled `mode`. */
const STRICT01 = "tests/fixtures/working/word-clean-strict01.docx";
const DATA_REL =
    '<Relationship Id="rId35" Type="http://purl.oclc.org/ooxml/officeDocument/relationships/diagramData" Target="diagrams/data1.xml"/>';
const strict01 = async (mode?: string) => {
    const zip = await JSZip.loadAsync(readFileSync(STRICT01));
    const parts: Record<string, string | Uint8Array> = {};
    for (const [name, entry] of Object.entries(zip.files)) if (!entry.dir) parts[name] = await entry.async("uint8array");
    if (mode !== undefined) {
        const rels = Buffer.from(parts[SIDECAR] as Uint8Array).toString("utf8");
        parts[SIDECAR] = replaceOnce(
            rels,
            DATA_REL,
            DATA_REL.replace('Target="diagrams/data1.xml"/>', `Target="diagrams/data1.xml" TargetMode="${mode}"/>`),
        );
    }
    return buildDocx(parts);
};

const chunks: Record<string, Array<[string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>]>> = {

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = process.env.BUILD_DIR;
if (!dir) throw new Error("BUILD_DIR is required");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const verdict = async (profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
        try {
            const r = await validate(path.join(dir, file), { profile });
            return {
                valid: r.valid,
                errors: [...new Set(r.issues.filter((x) => x.severity === "error").map((x) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`))],
            };
        } catch (error) {
            return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
        }
    };
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        wordValid: await verdict("word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict("strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(path.join(dir, "..", "specimens.jsonl"), JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-55 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
CHUNKS = ("s55a", "s55b", "s55c", "s55d", "s55e")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0]) if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": "control-minimal" in spec["name"],
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s55/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

"""Render the session-55 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s55/section.md.

Reads the chunk's specimens.jsonl (validator columns at 42600284, written by the builder), both runs'
logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and s55/results.json from compare.py.
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
CHUNKS = ("s55a", "s55b", "s55c", "s55d", "s55e")
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s55/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


rows, raw, starts, ends = [], [], [], []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        starts.append(times[0])
        ends.append(times[1])
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        shape = s["issue"].replace("|", "\\|")
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {shape} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            raw.append(json.dumps({"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "sha256": s["sha256"],
                                   "observedAt": t.isoformat(), "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"],
                                   "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"], "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))

out = [
    f"### Session 55: {min(starts):%H:%M}Z–{max(ends):%H:%M}Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at 42600284",
    "",
    "The shapes the review of layers 161–165 asked Word about: a header Word reads stored with no relationships part, whose "
    "references layer 161 handed to `rels-missing-sidecar` ([#751](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/751), finding 1), "
    "and a relationship whose TargetMode is spelled `external`, and a `c:chart` naming its relationship in both relationships namespaces "
    "([#753](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/753), findings 6 and 7), with s55d and s55e added after the first three "
    "chunks to separate those two shapes from their confounders and to bound the TargetMode rule. Each chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, "
    "and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome "
    "is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; all 33 rows agree. The two times in "
    "Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen.",
    "",
    "- A header the body references, stored as `word/header1.xml` with no relationships part, gets the recovery offer when it holds a "
    "`c:chart r:id=\"rId1\"`, an `o:OLEObject r:id=\"rId1\"`, or a `dgm:relIds` naming all four parts, as the same header does with "
    "a relationships part that lacks `rId1` (the calibration); with no `r:` reference it opens clean. Word-valid at 42600284 passes all "
    "three: false negatives.",
    "- A relationship whose TargetMode is spelled `external` gets the recovery offer whether a `c:chart` names it, it is the diagramData "
    "relationship of session 46's word-clean-strict01 SmartArt, or it is an unreferenced hyperlink relationship in the main document's "
    "relationships part; spelled `Internal` or `External` the same packages open clean. Word reads the spelling, not the reference. "
    "The unreferenced hyperlink relationship also gets the recovery offer with TargetMode `external` in the package's `_rels/.rels`, and "
    "with `External ` (trailing space) or an empty TargetMode in the main document's relationships part; with `external` in a referenced "
    "header's own relationships part it opens clean, as with `External`. Word-valid at 42600284 passes all six refused shapes: false "
    "negatives.",
    "- A `c:chart` carrying both `r:id` and the ISO Strict `rs:id` cannot be opened (open error, no recovery offer) whether one of the two "
    "is empty or both name the real chart relationship; `rs:id` alone in the Transitional document opens clean and draws the chart. "
    "Word refuses the second namespace, not the empty id. Word-valid at 42600284 passes all three: false negatives.",
    "",
    "| Run | Observed | Specimen | Shape | SHA-256 (first 16) | Word, run 1 | Word, run 2 | Outcome | word-valid at 42600284 | strict at 42600284 |",
    "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",

### Session 56: 15:38Z–15:41Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at f033a3db

The content-type shapes the #739 lane changed or left without a Word row ([#739](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/739), [#760](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/760)): `word/styles.xml` typed with the footer content type, alone and with a second footer relationship to it that no section references or that the body references; and the same part typed with an inexact spelling of the styles type, alone and with a read footer relationship to it. The chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; all 7 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen.

- `word/styles.xml` typed `…footer+xml` gets the recovery offer reached by the main document's styles relationship alone (the session 49 class, the calibration), with a second footer relationship to it that no section references, and with that footer relationship referenced by the body. Word-valid at f033a3db rejects only the calibration: a matching footer reach exempted the styles reach's mismatch. Two false negatives, which #739's fix rejects.
- `word/styles.xml` typed `…styles+xml; charset=utf-8` gets the recovery offer alone (the calibration) and with a read footer relationship to it. Word-valid at f033a3db rejects only the calibration: the co-reach hides the inexact spelling. A false negative (#760).

`s56builder.mts`:

```ts
// Session 56 (2026-10-26): the content-type shapes lane F (#739) changed or left without a Word row.
// - s56a: word/styles.xml typed with the footer content type, alone (calibration), with a footer relationship the body
//   never references (no w:footerReference) also targeting it, and with a footer relationship the body references.
//   #739's fix stops a matching footer reach from exempting the styles reach's mismatch, so word-valid now rejects the
//   unused-footer row; Word was never shown it. Then word/styles.xml typed with an inexact spelling of the styles type
//   (`; charset=utf-8`) alone, and with a read footer relationship targeting it: lane F reports word-valid passes the
//   co-reach row, which no session showed.
// Run from a worktree root as a copy: BUILD_DIR=<chunk>/src CHUNK=s56a pnpm exec tsx s56builder.tmp.mts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } from "./tests/support/minimal-docx";
import { validate } from "./src/scripts/office/validate";

const W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main";
const REL = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships";
const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const SIDECAR = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const MAIN_TYPE = `${WML}.document.main+xml`;
const STYLES_TYPE = `${WML}.styles+xml`;
const P = MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>;
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n`;

type Kind = "numbering" | "settings" | "fontTable";
/** The relationship segment, the part body and the content type of each kind (the bodies session 47 used). */
const KINDS: Record<Kind, { root: string; ct: string }> = {
    numbering: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:numbering xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.numbering+xml` },
    settings: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:settings xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.settings+xml` },
    fontTable: { root: `${XML_DECL}<w:fonts xmlns:w="${W}"/>`, ct: `${WML}.fontTable+xml` },
};
/** The other mapped Word content types the rows type a part with. */
const TYPES = {
    main: MAIN_TYPE,
    styles: STYLES_TYPE,
    theme: "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.theme+xml",
    glossary: `${WML}.document.glossary+xml`,
    header: `${WML}.header+xml`,
    footer: `${WML}.footer+xml`,
    footnotes: `${WML}.footnotes+xml`,
    endnotes: `${WML}.endnotes+xml`,
    comments: `${WML}.comments+xml`,
    settings: KINDS.settings.ct,
    fontTable: KINDS.fontTable.ct,
    numbering: KINDS.numbering.ct,
};
const SPELLINGS: Array<[string, string]> = [
    ["octet-upper", "APPLICATION/OCTET-STREAM"],
    ["octet-charset", "application/octet-stream; charset=utf-8"],
    ["image-png", "image/png"],
    ["foo-xml", "application/foo+xml"],
];

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string, to: string) => {
    if (text.split(from).length !== 2) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};
const relationship = (id: string, segment: string, target: string) =>
    `<Relationship Id="${id}" Type="${REL}/${segment}" Target="${target}"/>`;
const appendRels = (rels: string, extra: string) => replaceOnce(rels, "</Relationships>", `${extra}</Relationships>`);
const overrides = (ct: string, ...entries: Array<[string, string]>) =>
    replaceOnce(
        ct,
        "</Types>",
        `${entries.map(([part, type]) => `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`).join("")}</Types>`,
    );
const retype = (ct: string, part: string, own: string, type: string) =>
    replaceOnce(ct, `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${own}"/>`, `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`);
const control = () => buildDocx({ ...P });

/** The minimal package plus `word/<kind>.xml` related from the main document's sidecar as rId2, typed `type`. */
const withRelated = (kind: Kind, type = KINDS[kind].ct): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    [`word/${kind}.xml`]: KINDS[kind].root,
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rId2", kind, `${kind}.xml`)),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, [`word/${kind}.xml`, type]),
});
const relatedTyped = (kind: Kind, type: string) => buildDocx(withRelated(kind, type));
const mainTyped = (type: string) => buildDocx({ ...P, [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/document.xml", MAIN_TYPE, type) });
const stylesTyped = (type: string) => buildDocx({ ...P, [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/styles.xml", STYLES_TYPE, type) });

/** `parts` plus a footer relationship (rIdF) to `target` (relative to word/) that the body's section references. */
const withReadFooter = (parts: Record<string, string>, target: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...parts,
    "word/document.xml": replaceOnce(
        replaceOnce(parts["word/document.xml"]!, `xmlns:w="${W}"`, `xmlns:w="${W}" xmlns:r="${REL}"`),
        "<w:sectPr>",
        `<w:sectPr><w:footerReference w:type="default" r:id="rIdF"/>`,
    ),
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(parts[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdF", "footer", target)),
});
const mainFooterCoReach = (type: string) =>
    buildDocx(withReadFooter({ ...P, [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/document.xml", MAIN_TYPE, type) }, "document.xml"));
const numberingFooterCoReach = (type: string) => buildDocx(withReadFooter(withRelated("numbering", type), "numbering.xml"));
const stylesFooterCoReach = (type: string) =>
    buildDocx(withReadFooter({ ...P, [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/styles.xml", STYLES_TYPE, type) }, "styles.xml"));
/** `parts` plus a footer relationship (rIdF) to `target` (relative to word/) that no section references. */
const withUnusedFooter = (parts: Record<string, string>, target: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...parts,
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(parts[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdF", "footer", target)),
});
const stylesRetyped = (type: string): Record<string, string> => ({ ...P, [CT]: retype(P[CT]!, "word/styles.xml", STYLES_TYPE, type) });
const STYLES_CHARSET = `${STYLES_TYPE}; charset=utf-8`;
type Row = [string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>];
const withControls = (chunk: string, rows: Row[]): Row[] => [
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal`, "control", control],
    ...rows,
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal-end`, "control", control],
];

const chunks: Record<string, Row[]> = {
    s56a: withControls("s56a", [
        [
            "styles-typed-footer-calibration",
            "calibration: word/styles.xml typed with the footer content type (the main document's styles relationship only)",
            () => buildDocx(stylesRetyped(TYPES.footer)),
        ],
        [
            "styles-typed-footer-unused-footer-rel",
            "#739: the same plus a footer relationship no section references, also targeting word/styles.xml",
            () => buildDocx(withUnusedFooter(stylesRetyped(TYPES.footer), "styles.xml")),
        ],
        [
            "styles-typed-footer-read-footer",
            "#739: the same with the body referencing that footer relationship",
            () => buildDocx(withReadFooter(stylesRetyped(TYPES.footer), "styles.xml")),
        ],
        [
            "styles-charset-calibration",
            "calibration: word/styles.xml typed styles+xml; charset=utf-8 (the main document's styles relationship only)",
            () => buildDocx(stylesRetyped(STYLES_CHARSET)),
        ],
        [
            "styles-charset-read-footer",
            "#739 residue: the same plus a footer relationship the body references, targeting word/styles.xml",
            () => buildDocx(withReadFooter(stylesRetyped(STYLES_CHARSET), "styles.xml")),
        ],
    ]),
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = process.env.BUILD_DIR;
if (!dir) throw new Error("BUILD_DIR is required");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const verdict = async (profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
        try {
            const r = await validate(path.join(dir, file), { profile });
            return {
                valid: r.valid,
                errors: [...new Set(r.issues.filter((x) => x.severity === "error").map((x) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`))],
            };
        } catch (error) {
            return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
        }
    };
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        wordValid: await verdict("word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict("strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(path.join(dir, "..", "specimens.jsonl"), JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}

`compare.py`:

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-56 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
CHUNKS = ("s56a",)
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0]) if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": "control-minimal" in spec["name"],
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s56/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

`section.py`:

`````python
"""Render the session-56 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s56/section.md.

Reads the chunk's specimens.jsonl (validator columns at f033a3db, written by the builder), both runs'
logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and s56/results.json from compare.py.
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/Users/arthrod/temp/T/docx-validate/.scratch/word-probes")
CHUNKS = ("s56a",)
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s56/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


rows, raw, starts, ends = [], [], [], []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        starts.append(times[0])
        ends.append(times[1])
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        shape = s["issue"].replace("|", "\\|")
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {shape} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]

                                   "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"], "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))
