const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = process.env.BUILD_DIR;
if (!dir) throw new Error("BUILD_DIR is required");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "..", "specimens.jsonl"), "");
for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const verdict = async (profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
        try {
            const r = await validate(path.join(dir, file), { profile });
            return {
                valid: r.valid,
                errors: [...new Set(r.issues.filter((x) => x.severity === "error").map((x) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`))],
            };
        } catch (error) {
            return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
        }
    };
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        validatorRevision: REVISION,
        wordValid: await verdict("word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict("strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(path.join(dir, "..", "specimens.jsonl"), JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}

"""Join both passes of the session-66 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s67a", "s67b")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0]) if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": "control-minimal" in spec["name"],
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s67/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

"""Render the session-67 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s67/section.md.

Reads each chunk's specimens.jsonl (written by the builder, each row carrying the validator revision it was judged at),
both runs' logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and the results.json compare.py writes. The validator label comes from
the rows' `validatorRevision`, never from this script (CodeRabbit on #796).
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s67a", "s67b")
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s67/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    # A builder records valid: null when validate() threw; render that as the exception, not as a rejection.
    if v["valid"] is None:
        return "threw: " + ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in v["errors"])
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


rows, raw, starts, ends, revisions = [], [], [], [], set()
agreed = 0
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        revisions.add(s.get("validatorRevision", "unknown"))
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        starts.append(times[0])
        ends.append(times[1])
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        agreed += result["agreed"]
        shape = s["issue"].replace("|", "\\|")
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {shape} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            raw.append(json.dumps({"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "sha256": s["sha256"],
                                   "validatorRevision": s.get("validatorRevision"), "observedAt": t.isoformat(),
                                   "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"], "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"],
                                   "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))

assert len(revisions) == 1, revisions
rev = next(iter(revisions))
at = rev[:8] if rev != "unknown" else "an unrecorded revision"
out = [
    f"### Session 67: {min(starts):%H:%M}Z–{max(ends):%H:%M}Z on 2026-10-26, validator columns at {at}",
    "",
    "The scope of [#850](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/850) and [#851](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/851). Two chunks, each "
    "opening and closing with the minimal control. Each ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each "
    "run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the "
    "manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; "
    f"{agreed} of {len(rows)} rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the "
    f"builder's description of the specimen. The builder recorded the validator revision in every row (`{rev}`).",
    "",
    "- **Parts both story roots read (s67a, #850).** Session 66's shared comments part, related and referenced by both the "
    "main document and a reached glossary, is refused again. Related by both but referenced by only one of them, or by neither, "
    "it opens clean, so the refusal needs both roots to use the part. A `word/footnotes.xml` that the main document relates "
    "and the glossary relates as `../footnotes.xml`, each referencing footnote 1, is refused too, and so is its endnotes twin; "
    "referenced by the body only, the shared footnotes part opens clean. Word-valid accepts all seven rows: three false "
    "negatives.",
    "- **Text directly inside `mc:AlternateContent` (s67b, #851).** In a used `word/comments.xml` typed comments whose stored "
    "root is s63b's AlternateContent, text before the Choice, text after the Fallback, text after a Choice with no Fallback, "
    "and text between two Choices (the second requiring a namespace Word does not understand) each get the recovery offer; "
    "the no-Fallback and two-Choice roots without the text open clean here, as s63b's root did in session 63, and so does a "
    "newline and spaces between the Choice and the Fallback. In the main "
    "document, a run-level AlternateContent with text between its Choice and its Fallback is refused, and without the text "
    "it opens clean. Word-valid accepts every row: five false negatives.",
    "",
    f"| Run | Observed | Specimen | Shape | SHA-256 (first 16) | Word, run 1 | Word, run 2 | Outcome | word-valid at {at} | strict at {at} |",
    "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    *rows,
    "",
    "<details><summary>Raw records, session 67</summary>",
    "",
    "```jsonl",
    *raw,
    "```",
    "",
    "</details>",
    "",
    "<details><summary>Session 67 builder, cross-check and section scripts</summary>",
    "",
    "Staging the second run and reading the logs used session 41's `stage_pass2.py` and `logcheck.py`, above, unchanged.",
    "",
]
for name, path, lang in (("s67builder.mts", ROOT / "s67builder.mts", "ts"), ("compare.py", ROOT / "s67/compare.py", "python"),
                         ("section.py", ROOT / "s67/section.py", "python")):
    out += [f"`{name}`:", "", f"````{lang}", path.read_text().rstrip("\n"), "````", ""]
out += ["</details>", ""]
(ROOT / "s67/section.md").write_text("\n".join(out))
print(len(rows), "rows,", len(raw), "raw records,", agreed, "agreed")

<details><summary>Session 68 builder, cross-check and section scripts</summary>

Staging the second run and reading the logs used session 41's `stage_pass2.py` and `logcheck.py`, above, unchanged.

`s68builder.mts`:

```ts
// Session 68: a two-run re-probe of session 39's three chunks (#661, #662), byte for byte, with the controls named so
// the driver's name-ordered queue opens one first and one last in every chunk. Session 39 ran each chunk once, before
// the two-runs-with-logs rule, and queued its controls last (#671).
// Every row records the validator revision it was judged at (`validatorRevision`); the verdict helper is s67builder.mts's.
// The builder empties the chunk's specimens.jsonl once before its row loop (promised on #825).
// Run from a worktree root: CHUNK=s68a pnpm exec node --import tsx <this file>
// (the imports are absolute, so the file needs no copy into the worktree; `git rev-parse` reads the cwd's worktree).
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const ROOT = path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);
const { validate } = await import(path.join(process.cwd(), "src/scripts/office/validate.ts"));
const REVISION = execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();

// Each session 68 chunk repeats one session 39 chunk.
const SOURCES: Record<string, string> = { s68a: "s39a", s68b: "s39b", s68c: "s39c" };

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const source = SOURCES[chunk];
if (!source) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(SOURCES).join(", ")}`);
const dir = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "src");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
const jsonl = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "specimens.jsonl");
writeFileSync(jsonl, "");

type SourceRow = { name: string; issue: string; file: string; sha256: string };
const sourceRows: SourceRow[] = readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, source, "specimens.jsonl"), "utf8")
    .trim()
    .split("\n")
    .map((line) => JSON.parse(line));
const control = sourceRows.find((row) => row.name === `${source}-control-minimal`);
if (!control) throw new Error(`${source} has no ${source}-control-minimal row`);
const specimens = sourceRows.filter((row) => row.issue !== "control");
if (specimens.length !== 6) throw new Error(`${source}: expected 6 specimens, found ${specimens.length}`);

// [name, issue, the session 39 row whose bytes it copies]
const rows: Array<[string, string, SourceRow]> = [
    [`00-${chunk}-control-first`, "control", control],
    ...specimens.map((row): [string, string, SourceRow] => [row.name, `repeat of ${source}: ${row.issue}`, row]),
    [`zz-${chunk}-control-last`, "control", control],
];

const verdict = async (file: string, profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
    try {
        const r = await validate(file, { profile });
        return {
            valid: r.valid,
            errors: [
                ...new Set(
                    r.issues
                        .filter((x: { severity: string }) => x.severity === "error")
                        .map((x: { code: string; path?: string }) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`),
                ),
            ],
        };
    } catch (error) {
        return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
    }
};

for (const [name, issue, from] of rows) {
    const bytes = readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, source, "src", from.file));
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    if (sha256 !== from.sha256) throw new Error(`${from.file}: stored bytes ${sha256} differ from session 39's ${from.sha256}`);
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const target = path.join(dir, file);
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: false,
        copiedFrom: `${source}/src/${from.file}`,
        validatorRevision: REVISION,
        wordValid: await verdict(target, "word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict(target, "strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(jsonl, JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `copied ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}
```

`compare.py`:

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-68 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s68a", "s68b", "s68c")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0]) if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": spec["issue"] == "control",
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s68/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

`section.py`:

`````python
"""Render the session-68 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s68/section.md.

Reads each chunk's specimens.jsonl (written by the builder, each row carrying the validator revision it was judged at),
both runs' logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and the results.json compare.py writes. The validator label comes from
the rows' `validatorRevision`, never from this script (CodeRabbit on #796).
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s68a", "s68b", "s68c")
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s68/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    # A builder records valid: null when validate() threw; render that as the exception, not as a rejection.
    if v["valid"] is None:
        return "threw: " + ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in v["errors"])
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


rows, raw, starts, ends, revisions = [], [], [], [], set()
agreed = 0
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        revisions.add(s.get("validatorRevision", "unknown"))
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        starts.append(times[0])
        ends.append(times[1])
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        agreed += result["agreed"]
        shape = s["issue"].replace("|", "\\|")
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {shape} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            raw.append(json.dumps({"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "sha256": s["sha256"],
                                   "validatorRevision": s.get("validatorRevision"), "observedAt": t.isoformat(),
                                   "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"], "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"],
                                   "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))

assert len(revisions) == 1, revisions
rev = next(iter(revisions))
at = rev[:8] if rev != "unknown" else "an unrecorded revision"

# Where each run opened its controls, from the driver's manifests (in open order, #671): the narrative states it, so
# check it here rather than trust the names' sort order.
for label in CHUNKS:
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        opened = [json.loads(l)["original_filename"] for l in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
        assert len(opened) == 8 and opened[0] == f"00-{label}-control-first.docx" and opened[-1] == f"zz-{label}-control-last.docx", (run, opened)
# The narrative's claims about outcomes, checked against results.json.
for (label, file), r in results.items():
    if r["control"] or label != "s68c":
        assert r["outcome"] == "clean-open", (label, file, r["outcome"])
    else:
        assert r["outcome"] == "unreadable-content-warning", (label, file, r["outcome"])
    assert r["validatorMatchesWord"], (label, file)
assert agreed == len(rows) == 24, (agreed, len(rows))
day = f"{min(starts):%Y-%m-%d}"
assert day == f"{max(ends):%Y-%m-%d}", (min(starts), max(ends))
out = [
    f"### Session 68: {min(starts):%H:%M}Z–{max(ends):%H:%M}Z on {day}, validator columns at {at}",
    "",
    "A two-run repeat of session 39 ([#661](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/661), "
    "[#662](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/662)). Session 39 ran each chunk once, before the "
    "two-runs-with-logs rule, and its controls were queued last in every chunk ([#671](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/671)). "
    "Here each chunk holds session 39's six specimens, copied byte for byte (the builder checks every SHA-256 against "
    "session 39's row), and its minimal control twice, named so the driver's name-ordered queue opens one copy first and "
    "the other last; every run's manifest shows the controls opened 1st and 8th of 8. Each chunk ran twice, as two separate "
    "driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's "
    "`logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, "
    f"and `unknown` otherwise; {agreed} of {len(rows)} rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and "
    "second runs. Shape repeats session 39's description. The builder recorded the validator revision in every row "
    f"(`{rev}`).",
    "",
    "- **Chart sources (s68a, #661).** The six unreferenced chart shapes, clean in session 39, open clean in both runs: "
    "a chart related from a referenced header's sidecar, from a reached glossary's footnotes part's sidecar and from the "
    "glossary document's sidecar, a chart whose only drawing sits in an unselected Fallback, a chart related twice and "
    "named by neither, and a chart related through an equivalent target spelling.",
    "- **Package-root wrappers (s68b, #662).** The six compound `_rels/.rels` root wrappers, clean in session 39, open "
    "clean in both runs.",
    "- **Referenced chart twins (s68c, #661).** Each of the six referenced twins gets the recovery offer in both runs, as "
    "in session 39.",
    "",
    "Session 39's verdicts stand, now from two runs whose controls bracket the specimens. Word-valid matches Word on all "
    "24 rows.",
    "",
    f"| Run | Observed | Specimen | Shape | SHA-256 (first 16) | Word, run 1 | Word, run 2 | Outcome | word-valid at {at} | strict at {at} |",
    "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    *rows,
    "",
    "<details><summary>Raw records, session 68</summary>",
    "",
    "```jsonl",
    *raw,
    "```",
    "",
    "</details>",
    "",
    "<details><summary>Session 68 builder, cross-check and section scripts</summary>",
    "",
    "Staging the second run and reading the logs used session 41's `stage_pass2.py` and `logcheck.py`, above, unchanged.",
    "",
]
for name, path, lang in (("s68builder.mts", ROOT / "s68builder.mts", "ts"), ("compare.py", ROOT / "s68/compare.py", "python"),
                         ("section.py", ROOT / "s68/section.py", "python")):
    out += [f"`{name}`:", "", f"````{lang}", path.read_text().rstrip("\n"), "````", ""]
out += ["</details>", ""]
(ROOT / "s68/section.md").write_text("\n".join(out))
print(len(rows), "rows,", len(raw), "raw records,", agreed, "agreed")
`````

### Session 69: 05:01Z–05:01Z on 2026-10-27, validator columns at bc09dc1d

The open question of [#896](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/896): whether a comments part that no relationship names defines the comment the body references. At this revision the comment checks fell back to `word/comments.xml` by name whenever no relationship of the main document named a comments part. Session 61 refused the notes twin. One chunk, with the minimal control twice. It ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; 8 of 8 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen. The builder recorded the validator revision in every row (`bc09dc1dc98f69fcf522dd2a9b2e883afea5a1cd`).

The driver opens files in name order, and the control names sort last, so both runs opened the two controls 7th and 8th, after every specimen, not one first and one last as in session 68. The two calibrations opened 2nd and 6th, on either side of the two refused rows (3rd and 5th), and opened clean in both runs, so Word opened packages clean before and after each refusal.

- **(a), (b).** A body `w:commentReference` to comment 0, which only a `word/comments.xml` typed comments by its Override but named by no relationship defines, gets the recovery offer, both with no `word/_rels/document.xml.rels` and beside one relating only `styles.xml`. Word-valid at bc09dc1d accepts both: two false negatives, from the by-name fallback.
- **(c) and the no-sidecar calibration.** The same package with a comments relationship naming the part opens clean, and so does the minimal package with no main-document relationships part and no comments.
- **(d).** Row (b) with the range markers only, no `w:commentReference`, opens clean. Range markers naming no comment stay word-valid warnings (#784), so this row is consistent with Word reading no comments part.
- **#895.** The no-relationships tree after layer 242's `addComment` for comment 0, which creates `word/_rels/document.xml.rels` and relates and types its four comment parts, opens clean with the body then marked.

Word defines comments only from the part a `comments` relationship names, as session 61 showed for notes. Word-valid at bc09dc1d matches Word on 6 of 8 rows.

```ts
// Session 69 (2026-10-27): does Word read a comments part no relationship names (#896)?
// The comment checks fall back to word/comments.xml by name when no relationship of the main document names a comments
// part, so a body w:commentReference to a comment only that part defines draws no comment-marker-missing. Session 61
// refused the notes twin (a note only an unrelated word/footnotes.xml defines). This chunk asks the same of comments,
// with and without a main-document relationships part, and checks the part #895's addComment fix now creates.
// Every row records the validator revision it was judged at (`validatorRevision`); the verdict helper is s67builder.mts's.
// The builder empties the chunk's specimens.jsonl once before its row loop (promised on #825).
// Run from a worktree root: CHUNK=s69a pnpm exec node --import tsx <this file>
// (the imports are absolute, so the file needs no copy into the worktree; `git rev-parse` reads the cwd's worktree).
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { promises as fs } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const ROOT = path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);
const WT = process.cwd();
const { validate } = await import(path.join(WT, "src/scripts/office/validate.ts"));
const { addComment } = await import(path.join(WT, "src/scripts/comment.ts"));
const { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } = await import(path.join(WT, "tests/support/minimal-docx.ts"));
const REVISION = execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();

const W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main";
const R = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships";
const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const MAIN = "word/document.xml";
const SIDECAR = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const P = MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>;
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n`;
const HELLO = "<w:r><w:t>Hello</w:t></w:r>";

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string, to: string) => {
    if (text.split(from).length !== 2) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};
const relationship = (id: string, segment: string, target: string) =>
    `<Relationship Id="${id}" Type="${R}/${segment}" Target="${target}"/>`;
const appendRels = (rels: string, extra: string) => replaceOnce(rels, "</Relationships>", `${extra}</Relationships>`);
const overrides = (ct: string, ...entries: Array<[string, string]>) =>
    replaceOnce(
        ct,
        "</Types>",
        `${entries.map(([part, type]) => `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`).join("")}</Types>`,
    );

/** The main document with comment 0's range around "Hello", and its w:commentReference when `reference`. */
const marked = (main: string, reference: boolean) =>
    replaceOnce(
        main,
        HELLO,
        `<w:commentRangeStart w:id="0"/>${HELLO}<w:commentRangeEnd w:id="0"/>${reference ? `<w:r><w:commentReference w:id="0"/></w:r>` : ""}`,
    );
const COMMENTS_XML = `${XML_DECL}<w:comments xmlns:w="${W}"><w:comment w:id="0" w:author="a" w:initials="a"><w:p><w:r><w:t>Comment</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:comment></w:comments>`;

/** The minimal parts with no main-document relationships part; styles.xml and its Override go too, so nothing is left unrelated. */
const noSidecar = (): Record<string, string> => {
    const next: Record<string, string> = {
        ...P,
        [CT]: replaceOnce(P[CT]!, `<Override PartName="/word/styles.xml" ContentType="${WML}.styles+xml"/>`, ""),
    };
    delete next[SIDECAR];
    delete next["word/styles.xml"];
    return next;
};
/** `parts` with word/comments.xml (comment 0, typed comments), related by the main document when `related`, and the body marked. */
const withComments = (parts: Record<string, string>, related: boolean, reference: boolean): Record<string, string> => {
    const next: Record<string, string> = {
        ...parts,
        "word/comments.xml": COMMENTS_XML,
        [CT]: overrides(parts[CT]!, ["word/comments.xml", `${WML}.comments+xml`]),
        [MAIN]: marked(parts[MAIN]!, reference),
    };
    if (related) next[SIDECAR] = appendRels(parts[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdC", "comments", "comments.xml"));
    return next;
};

/** The parts as `addComment` leaves them for a first comment on the no-relationships tree, with the body then marked (#895). */
const viaAddComment = async (chunk: string): Promise<Record<string, string>> => {
    const work = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "work");
    rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true });
    for (const [name, text] of Object.entries(noSidecar())) {
        mkdirSync(path.dirname(path.join(work, name)), { recursive: true });
        writeFileSync(path.join(work, name), text);
    }
    const result = await addComment({
        unpackedDir: work,
        commentId: 0,
        text: "Comment",
        author: "a",
        initials: "a",
        date: new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 27, 0, 0, 0)),
    });
    if (!result.message.startsWith("Added comment 0")) throw new Error(`addComment: ${result.message}`);
    const parts: Record<string, string> = {};
    const walk = async (dir: string): Promise<void> => {
        for (const entry of await fs.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
            const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);
            if (entry.isDirectory()) await walk(full);
            else parts[path.relative(work, full)] = await fs.readFile(full, "utf8");
        }
    };
    await walk(work);
    parts[MAIN] = marked(parts[MAIN]!, true);
    return parts;
};

type Row = [string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>];
const control = () => buildDocx({ ...P });
const withControls = (chunk: string, rows: Row[]): Row[] => [
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal`, "control", control],
    ...rows,
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal-end`, "control", control],
];

const chunks: Record<string, Row[]> = {
    s69a: withControls("s69a", [
        [
            "no-sidecar-calibration",
            "calibration: the minimal package with no word/_rels/document.xml.rels (styles.xml and its Override removed too); no comments",
            () => buildDocx(noSidecar()),
        ],
        [
            "comments-unrelated-no-sidecar",
            "(a) no word/_rels/document.xml.rels; word/comments.xml defines comment 0 (typed comments); the body marks its range and references it",
            () => buildDocx(withComments(noSidecar(), false, true)),
        ],
        [
            "comments-unrelated-sidecar",
            "(b) word/_rels/document.xml.rels relates only styles.xml; word/comments.xml defines comment 0 (typed comments); the body marks its range and references it",
            () => buildDocx(withComments({ ...P }, false, true)),
        ],
        [
            "comments-related-calibration",
            "(c) calibration: the same package with a comments relationship naming word/comments.xml",
            () => buildDocx(withComments({ ...P }, true, true)),
        ],
        [
            "comments-unrelated-range-only",
            "(d) row (b) with the range markers only, no w:commentReference",
            () => buildDocx(withComments({ ...P }, false, false)),
        ],
        [
            "addcomment-created-sidecar",
            "#895: the no-relationships tree after layer 242's addComment for comment 0 (it creates word/_rels/document.xml.rels and its four comment parts), then the body marked",
            async () => buildDocx(await viaAddComment("s69a")),
        ],
    ]),
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "src");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
const jsonl = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "specimens.jsonl");
writeFileSync(jsonl, "");

const verdict = async (file: string, profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
    try {
        const r = await validate(file, { profile });
        return {
            valid: r.valid,
            errors: [
                ...new Set(
                    r.issues
                        .filter((x: { severity: string }) => x.severity === "error")
                        .map((x: { code: string; path?: string }) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`),
                ),
            ],
        };
    } catch (error) {
        return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
    }
};

for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const target = path.join(dir, file);
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        validatorRevision: REVISION,
        wordValid: await verdict(target, "word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict(target, "strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(jsonl, JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}

`compare.py`:

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-69 chunk: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s69a",)
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0], "unknown") if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": spec["issue"] == "control",
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s69/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

`````python
"""Render the session-69 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s69/section.md.

Reads each chunk's specimens.jsonl (written by the builder, each row carrying the validator revision it was judged at),
both runs' logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and the results.json compare.py writes. The validator label comes from
the rows' `validatorRevision`, never from this script (CodeRabbit on #796).
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s69a",)
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s69/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    # A builder records valid: null when validate() threw; render that as the exception, not as a rejection.
    if v["valid"] is None:
        return "threw: " + ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in v["errors"])
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


rows, raw, starts, ends, revisions = [], [], [], [], set()
agreed = 0
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        revisions.add(s.get("validatorRevision", "unknown"))
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        starts.append(times[0])
        ends.append(times[1])
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        agreed += result["agreed"]
        shape = s["issue"].replace("|", "\\|")
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {shape} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            raw.append(json.dumps({"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "sha256": s["sha256"],
                                   "validatorRevision": s.get("validatorRevision"), "observedAt": t.isoformat(),
                                   "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"], "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"],
                                   "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))

assert len(revisions) == 1, revisions
rev = next(iter(revisions))
at = rev[:8] if rev != "unknown" else "an unrecorded revision"

REFUSED = ("comments-unrelated-no-sidecar.docx", "comments-unrelated-sidecar.docx")
# Where each run opened each row, from the driver's manifests (in open order, #671): the narrative states it, so check it
# here rather than trust the names' sort order. The control names sort last, so both controls opened after every specimen.
for label in CHUNKS:
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        opened = [json.loads(l)["original_filename"] for l in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
        assert len(opened) == 8, (run, opened)
        assert opened[6:] == [f"{label}-control-minimal-end.docx", f"{label}-control-minimal.docx"], (run, opened)
        assert opened[1] == "comments-related-calibration.docx" and opened[5] == "no-sidecar-calibration.docx", (run, opened)
        assert (opened[2], opened[4]) == REFUSED, (run, opened)
# The narrative's claims about outcomes, checked against results.json.
for (label, file), r in results.items():
    if file in REFUSED:
        assert r["outcome"] == "unreadable-content-warning" and r["wordValid"] is True and not r["validatorMatchesWord"], (file, r)
    else:
        assert r["outcome"] == "clean-open" and r["validatorMatchesWord"], (file, r)
assert agreed == len(rows) == 8, (agreed, len(rows))
day = f"{min(starts):%Y-%m-%d}"
assert day == f"{max(ends):%Y-%m-%d}", (min(starts), max(ends))
out = [
    f"### Session 69: {min(starts):%H:%M}Z–{max(ends):%H:%M}Z on {day}, validator columns at {at}",
    "",
    "The open question of [#896](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/896): whether a comments part that "
    "no relationship names defines the comment the body references. At this revision the comment checks fell back to "
    "`word/comments.xml` by name whenever no relationship of the main document named a comments part. Session 61 refused "
    "the notes twin. One chunk, with the minimal control twice. It ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical "
    "copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by "
    f"`wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` "
    f"otherwise; {agreed} of {len(rows)} rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. "
    f"Shape is the builder's description of the specimen. The builder recorded the validator revision in every row (`{rev}`).",
    "",
    "The driver opens files in name order, and the control names sort last, so both runs opened the two controls 7th and "
    "8th, after every specimen, not one first and one last as in session 68. The two calibrations opened 2nd and 6th, on "
    "either side of the two refused rows (3rd and 5th), and opened clean in both runs, so Word opened packages clean before "
    "and after each refusal.",
    "",
    "- **(a), (b).** A body `w:commentReference` to comment 0, which only a `word/comments.xml` typed comments by its "
    "Override but named by no relationship defines, gets the recovery offer, both with no `word/_rels/document.xml.rels` "
    f"and beside one relating only `styles.xml`. Word-valid at {at} accepts both: two false negatives, from the by-name "

    "- **#895.** The no-relationships tree after layer 242's `addComment` for comment 0, which creates "

    "",

    "",
    f"| Run | Observed | Specimen | Shape | SHA-256 (first 16) | Word, run 1 | Word, run 2 | Outcome | word-valid at {at} | strict at {at} |",
    "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    *rows,

for name, path, lang in (("s69builder.mts", ROOT / "s69builder.mts", "ts"), ("compare.py", ROOT / "s69/compare.py", "python"),

### Session 70: 21:41Z–21:47Z on 2026-10-27, validator columns at f2fe8fe3

The open question of [#962](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/962): how Word resolves a relationship target with an empty segment or a final dot segment. At this revision `relationshipTargetPartName` resolved a target as `path.posix.join` does, which collapses an empty segment and drops the final `/` that RFC 3986's remove_dot_segments leaves after a final `.` or `..` segment, so `word/main.xml/.` and `word/main.xml/x/..` named `word/main.xml`. Three chunks: s70a asks with the `officeDocument` target of a main document stored as `word/main.xml`, s70b with a `footnotes` target whose note 1 the body references (a note no part defines dangles, and Word offers recovery for it, session 61), and s70c, added after the first two ran, with the other spellings whose RFC 3986 path ends in `/`. Each chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; 18 of 18 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen. The builder recorded the validator revision in every row (`f2fe8fe3c7495bdbccb69cb6c722dc55fd4de90d`).

The driver opens files in name order, and the control names sort last, so in every run both minimal controls opened after every specimen, and clean. Each run also opened a row clean after its refused rows: s70a's calibration opened 5th, after the refused 2nd and 4th; s70b's opened 3rd, after the refused 2nd; and s70c's inner-dot calibration opened 2nd, between the refused 1st and 3rd. Every clean row's PDF holds the text the specimen stores: `Hello` for the main document, and `Hello1 Note` (footnote 1) for the notes rows (`pdftotext`, both runs).

- **An empty segment collapses.** `word//main.xml`, the package-absolute `/word//main.xml`, and the footnotes target `notes//footnotes.xml` open clean, with the main document and the note rendered, as the plain calibrations do: Word reads the part through the target, as `path.posix.join` collapses it, where RFC 3986 would keep the empty segment.
- **An inner `.` resolves.** `word/./main.xml` opens clean with the main document rendered.

`s70builder.mts`:

```ts
// Session 70 (2026-10-27): does Word collapse an empty segment and a final `/.` in a relationship target (#962)?
// relationshipTargetPartName resolves a target with path.posix.join, which collapses `word//main.xml` to `word/main.xml`
// and drops a final `/.`, so `word/main.xml/.` names `word/main.xml` too; RFC 3986's remove_dot_segments keeps the empty
// segment and leaves `word/main.xml/`, which names no part. s70a asks Word with the officeDocument target of a main
// document stored as word/main.xml (relative and package-absolute spellings), s70b with a footnotes target whose note
// the body references: if Word reads no notes part through the target, the reference dangles and Word offers recovery
// (session 61), so a clean open shows the target named the part.
// Every row records the validator revision it was judged at (`validatorRevision`); the verdict helper is s67builder.mts's.
// The builder empties the chunk's specimens.jsonl once before its row loop (promised on #825).
// Run from a worktree root: CHUNK=s70a pnpm exec node --import tsx <this file>
// (the imports are absolute, so the file needs no copy into the worktree; `git rev-parse` reads the cwd's worktree).
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const ROOT = path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);
const WT = process.cwd();
const { validate } = await import(path.join(WT, "src/scripts/office/validate.ts"));
const { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } = await import(path.join(WT, "tests/support/minimal-docx.ts"));
const REVISION = execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();

const W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main";
const R = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships";
const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const MAIN = "word/document.xml";
const SIDECAR = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const P = MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>;
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n`;

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string, to: string) => {
    if (text.split(from).length !== 2) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};
const relationship = (id: string, segment: string, target: string) =>
    `<Relationship Id="${id}" Type="${R}/${segment}" Target="${target}"/>`;
const appendRels = (rels: string, extra: string) => replaceOnce(rels, "</Relationships>", `${extra}</Relationships>`);
const overrides = (ct: string, ...entries: Array<[string, string]>) =>
    replaceOnce(
        ct,
        "</Types>",
        `${entries.map(([part, type]) => `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`).join("")}</Types>`,
    );

/** The minimal parts with the main document stored as word/main.xml (its sidecar renamed, its Override moved) and named by the officeDocument target `target`. */
const mainAt = (target: string): Record<string, string> => {
    const next: Record<string, string> = { ...P, "word/main.xml": P[MAIN]!, "word/_rels/main.xml.rels": P[SIDECAR]! };
    delete next[MAIN];
    delete next[SIDECAR];
    next["_rels/.rels"] = replaceOnce(P["_rels/.rels"]!, 'Target="word/document.xml"', `Target="${target}"`);
    next[CT] = replaceOnce(P[CT]!, 'PartName="/word/document.xml"', 'PartName="/word/main.xml"');
    return next;
};

/** The minimal parts with footnote 1 stored in word/notes/footnotes.xml (typed footnotes), named by the main document's footnotes target `target`; the body references footnote 1. */
const notesAt = (target: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    [MAIN]: replaceOnce(P[MAIN]!, "</w:r></w:p>", `</w:r><w:r><w:footnoteReference w:id="1"/></w:r></w:p>`),
    "word/notes/footnotes.xml": `${XML_DECL}<w:footnotes xmlns:w="${W}"><w:footnote w:id="1"><w:p><w:r><w:t>Note</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:footnote></w:footnotes>`,
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdN", "footnotes", target)),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, ["word/notes/footnotes.xml", `${WML}.footnotes+xml`]),
});

type Row = [string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>];
const control = () => buildDocx({ ...P });
const withControls = (chunk: string, rows: Row[]): Row[] => [
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal`, "control", control],
    ...rows,
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal-end`, "control", control],
];

const chunks: Record<string, Row[]> = {
    s70a: withControls("s70a", [
        [
            "main-plain-calibration",
            "calibration: the main document stored as word/main.xml, named by the officeDocument target word/main.xml",
            () => buildDocx(mainAt("word/main.xml")),
        ],
        [
            "main-empty-segment",
            "#962: the same, named by word//main.xml (path.posix.join: word/main.xml; RFC 3986: word//main.xml, no part)",
            () => buildDocx(mainAt("word//main.xml")),
        ],
        ["main-absolute-empty-segment", "#962: the same, named by /word//main.xml", () => buildDocx(mainAt("/word//main.xml"))],
        [
            "main-final-dot",
            "#962: the same, named by word/main.xml/. (path.posix.join: word/main.xml; RFC 3986: word/main.xml/, no part)",
            () => buildDocx(mainAt("word/main.xml/.")),
        ],
        ["main-absolute-final-dot", "#962: the same, named by /word/main.xml/.", () => buildDocx(mainAt("/word/main.xml/."))],
    ]),
    s70b: withControls("s70b", [
        [
            "notes-plain-calibration",
            "calibration: footnote 1 in word/notes/footnotes.xml, named by the footnotes target notes/footnotes.xml; the body references footnote 1",
            () => buildDocx(notesAt("notes/footnotes.xml")),
        ],
        [
            "notes-empty-segment",
            "#962: the same, named by notes//footnotes.xml (path.posix.join: word/notes/footnotes.xml; RFC 3986: word/notes//footnotes.xml, no part)",
            () => buildDocx(notesAt("notes//footnotes.xml")),
        ],
        [
            "notes-final-dot",
            "#962: the same, named by notes/footnotes.xml/. (path.posix.join: word/notes/footnotes.xml; RFC 3986: word/notes/footnotes.xml/, no part)",
            () => buildDocx(notesAt("notes/footnotes.xml/.")),
        ],
    ]),
    // Added after s70a/s70b showed Word refusing a final `/.`: the other spellings whose RFC 3986 path ends in `/`.
    s70c: withControls("s70c", [
        [
            "main-inner-dot-calibration",
            "calibration: the main document stored as word/main.xml, named by word/./main.xml (path.posix.join and RFC 3986 alike: word/main.xml)",
            () => buildDocx(mainAt("word/./main.xml")),
        ],
        [
            "main-final-dotdot",
            "#962: the same, named by word/main.xml/x/.. (path.posix.join: word/main.xml; RFC 3986: word/main.xml/, no part)",
            () => buildDocx(mainAt("word/main.xml/x/..")),
        ],
        [
            "main-trailing-slash",
            "#962: the same, named by word/main.xml/ (path.posix.join and RFC 3986 alike: word/main.xml/, no part)",
            () => buildDocx(mainAt("word/main.xml/")),
        ],
        [
            "notes-final-dotdot",
            "#962: footnote 1 in word/notes/footnotes.xml, named by the footnotes target notes/footnotes.xml/x/.. (path.posix.join: word/notes/footnotes.xml; RFC 3986: word/notes/footnotes.xml/, no part); the body references footnote 1",
            () => buildDocx(notesAt("notes/footnotes.xml/x/..")),
        ],
    ]),
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "src");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
const jsonl = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "specimens.jsonl");
writeFileSync(jsonl, "");

const verdict = async (file: string, profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
    try {
        const r = await validate(file, { profile });
        return {
            valid: r.valid,
            errors: [
                ...new Set(
                    r.issues
                        .filter((x: { severity: string }) => x.severity === "error")
                        .map((x: { code: string; path?: string }) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`),
                ),
            ],
        };
    } catch (error) {
        return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
    }
};

for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const target = path.join(dir, file);
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        validatorRevision: REVISION,
        wordValid: await verdict(target, "word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict(target, "strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(jsonl, JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}
```

`compare.py`:

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-70 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s70a", "s70b", "s70c")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0], "unknown") if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": spec["issue"] == "control",
                     "validatorMatchesWord": (all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True)})
(ROOT / "s70/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

`section.py`:

`````python
"""Render the session-70 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s70/section.md.

Reads each chunk's specimens.jsonl (written by the builder, each row carrying the validator revision it was judged at),
both runs' logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and the results.json compare.py writes. The validator label comes from
the rows' `validatorRevision`, never from this script (CodeRabbit on #796). The text Word rendered is read from its own
PDFs with pdftotext, so the narrative's "rendered" claims are checked here.
"""
import json
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s70a", "s70b", "s70c")
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s70/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    # A builder records valid: null when validate() threw; render that as the exception, not as a rejection.
    if v["valid"] is None:
        return "threw: " + ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in v["errors"])
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def run_at(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(row["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    raise KeyError(file)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


def rendered(run, file):
    pdf = run / "pdf" / (Path(file).stem + "_byword.pdf")
    return " ".join(subprocess.run(["pdftotext", str(pdf), "-"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split())


rows, raw, starts, ends, revisions = [], [], [], [], set()
agreed = 0
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        revisions.add(s.get("validatorRevision", "unknown"))
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        starts.append(times[0])
        ends.append(times[1])
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        agreed += result["agreed"]
        shape = s["issue"].replace("|", "\\|")
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {shape} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            raw.append(json.dumps({"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "sha256": s["sha256"],
                                   "validatorRevision": s.get("validatorRevision"), "observedAt": t.isoformat(),
                                   "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"], "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"],
                                   "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}, ensure_ascii=False))

assert len(revisions) == 1, revisions
rev = next(iter(revisions))
at = rev[:8] if rev != "unknown" else "an unrecorded revision"

REFUSED = {"main-final-dot.docx", "main-absolute-final-dot.docx", "notes-final-dot.docx", "main-final-dotdot.docx",
           "main-trailing-slash.docx", "notes-final-dotdot.docx"}
ACCEPTED_BY_VALIDATOR = REFUSED - {"main-trailing-slash.docx"}
# The narrative's claims about outcomes, checked against results.json.
for (label, file), r in results.items():
    if file in REFUSED:
        assert r["outcome"] == "unreadable-content-warning", (file, r)
        assert r["wordValid"] is (file in ACCEPTED_BY_VALIDATOR), (file, r)
        assert r["validatorMatchesWord"] is (file not in ACCEPTED_BY_VALIDATOR), (file, r)
    else:
        assert r["outcome"] == "clean-open" and r["validatorMatchesWord"], (file, r)
assert agreed == len(rows) == 18, (agreed, len(rows))
# Where each run opened each row, from the driver's manifests (in open order, #671): the control names sort last, so both
# controls opened after every specimen in every run, and each run opened a row clean after its refused rows.
ORDER = {

        assert opened == ORDER[label], (run, opened)
# The text Word rendered in each clean row, both runs: the main document's "Hello", and footnote 1 ("1 Note") after it.
for label in CHUNKS:

            if file in REFUSED:
                continue
            text = rendered(run, file)
            expected = "Hello1 Note" if file.startswith("notes-") else "Hello"
            assert text == expected, (run, file, text)
day = f"{min(starts):%Y-%m-%d}"
assert day == f"{max(ends):%Y-%m-%d}", (min(starts), max(ends))

    "between the refused 1st and 3rd. Every clean row's PDF holds the text the specimen stores: `Hello` for the main "

    "`notes//footnotes.xml` open clean, with the main document and the note rendered, as the plain calibrations do: Word "

    "- **An inner `.` resolves.** `word/./main.xml` opens clean with the main document rendered.",

### Session 71: 22:06Z–22:08Z on 2026-10-27, validator columns at 80fb0996

The open question of [#975](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/975): whether Word refuses a relationship target ending in a final `.` or `..` segment for relationship types other than the two session 70 probed (`officeDocument`, `footnotes`). At this revision the read model reads such a target as a folder (#962), but the file-reference walks (`rels-broken`, `rels-target-missing`) resolve a file-system path first, which drops the final `/`, so they find the part. Two chunks: s71a relates `customXml/item1.xml` from the main document's relationships part (session 54 refused that relationship when the part is absent), and s71b names a styles part whose document defaults turn on caps, so the PDF reads `HELLO` only when Word applied it, and a default header holding `Head` that the section references. Each chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; 11 of 11 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen. The builder recorded the validator revision in every row (`80fb0996534e173c461cc91a07f4cc439e94c593`).

The driver opens files in name order. In s71a both minimal controls opened after every specimen, and clean. In s71b they opened 3rd and 4th, clean, after the refused header row, and the styles calibration opened clean 5th, before the refused styles row. Every clean row's PDF holds the text the specimen stores: `Hello` for the controls and the customXml calibration, `HELLO` for the styles calibration, so Word applied its caps, and `Head Hello` for the header calibration (`pdftotext`, both runs).

- **customXml.** `../customXml/item1.xml/.` and `../customXml/item1.xml/x/..` from `word/` get the recovery offer, while `../customXml/item1.xml` beside the same stored part opens clean.
- **styles.** `styles.xml/.` gets the recovery offer, while `styles.xml` opens clean with its caps applied.
- **header.** `header1.xml/.` gets the recovery offer, while `header1.xml` opens clean with `Head` rendered.

Every relationship type probed so far reads a final `.` or `..` segment as RFC 3986 does: the target names a folder, and Word refuses the package. Word-valid at 80fb0996 accepts the four folder rows, four false negatives from the file-reference walks' dropped `/`, and matches Word on 7 of 11 rows.

`s71builder.mts`:

```ts
// Session 71 (2026-10-27): does Word read a part through a styles, header or customXml target ending in a final `.` or
// `..` segment (#975)? Session 70 (#962) showed Word refusing such an officeDocument or footnotes target: the RFC 3986
// path names a folder. The file-reference walks (rels-broken) still resolve a file-system path and drop the final `/`.
// s71a: a customXml part stored at customXml/item1.xml, related from the main document's sidecar (session 54 refused the
// absent part); s71b: a styles part whose docDefaults turn on caps, so the PDF reads HELLO when Word applied it and Hello
// when it did not, and a default header holding "Head", named by its target.
// Every row records the validator revision it was judged at (`validatorRevision`); the verdict helper is s67builder.mts's.
// The builder empties the chunk's specimens.jsonl once before its row loop (promised on #825).
// Run from a worktree root: CHUNK=s71a pnpm exec node --import tsx <this file>
// (the imports are absolute, so the file needs no copy into the worktree; `git rev-parse` reads the cwd's worktree).
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const ROOT = path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);
const WT = process.cwd();
const { validate } = await import(path.join(WT, "src/scripts/office/validate.ts"));
const { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } = await import(path.join(WT, "tests/support/minimal-docx.ts"));
const REVISION = execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();

const W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main";
const R = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships";
const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const MAIN = "word/document.xml";
const SIDECAR = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const P = MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>;
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n`;

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string, to: string) => {
    if (text.split(from).length !== 2) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};
const relationship = (id: string, segment: string, target: string) =>
    `<Relationship Id="${id}" Type="${R}/${segment}" Target="${target}"/>`;
const appendRels = (rels: string, extra: string) => replaceOnce(rels, "</Relationships>", `${extra}</Relationships>`);
const overrides = (ct: string, ...entries: Array<[string, string]>) =>
    replaceOnce(
        ct,
        "</Types>",
        `${entries.map(([part, type]) => `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/>`).join("")}</Types>`,
    );

const CUSTOM_XML = `${XML_DECL}<root xmlns="urn:s71"/>`;
/** The minimal parts with customXml/item1.xml stored and related from the main document's sidecar by `target`. */
const customXmlAt = (target: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    "customXml/item1.xml": CUSTOM_XML,
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdX", "customXml", target)),
});
/** The minimal parts with caps turned on in styles.xml's docDefaults, named by the styles target `target`. */
const capsStylesAt = (target: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    "word/styles.xml": replaceOnce(
        P["word/styles.xml"]!,
        "<w:rPrDefault><w:rPr/></w:rPrDefault>",
        "<w:rPrDefault><w:rPr><w:caps/></w:rPr></w:rPrDefault>",
    ),
    [SIDECAR]: replaceOnce(P[SIDECAR]!, 'Target="styles.xml"', `Target="${target}"`),
});
/** The minimal parts with a default header word/header1.xml holding "Head", referenced from the section and named by `target`. */
const headerAt = (target: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    [MAIN]: replaceOnce(
        replaceOnce(P[MAIN]!, `xmlns:w="${W}"`, `xmlns:w="${W}" xmlns:r="${R}"`),
        "<w:sectPr>",
        '<w:sectPr><w:headerReference w:type="default" r:id="rIdH"/>',
    ),
    "word/header1.xml": `${XML_DECL}<w:hdr xmlns:w="${W}"><w:p><w:r><w:t>Head</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:hdr>`,
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdH", "header", target)),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, ["word/header1.xml", `${WML}.header+xml`]),
});

type Row = [string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>];
const control = () => buildDocx({ ...P });
const withControls = (chunk: string, rows: Row[]): Row[] => [
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal`, "control", control],
    ...rows,
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal-end`, "control", control],
];

const chunks: Record<string, Row[]> = {
    s71a: withControls("s71a", [
        [
            "customxml-calibration",
            "calibration: customXml/item1.xml stored and related from the main document's sidecar by ../customXml/item1.xml",
            () => buildDocx(customXmlAt("../customXml/item1.xml")),
        ],
        [
            "customxml-final-dot",
            "#975: the same, related by ../customXml/item1.xml/. (RFC 3986: customXml/item1.xml/, a folder)",
            () => buildDocx(customXmlAt("../customXml/item1.xml/.")),
        ],
        [
            "customxml-final-dotdot",
            "#975: the same, related by ../customXml/item1.xml/x/.. (RFC 3986: customXml/item1.xml/, a folder)",
            () => buildDocx(customXmlAt("../customXml/item1.xml/x/..")),
        ],
    ]),
    s71b: withControls("s71b", [
        [
            "styles-caps-calibration",
            "calibration: styles.xml's docDefaults turn on caps; the styles target is styles.xml (Word applied it if the PDF reads HELLO)",
            () => buildDocx(capsStylesAt("styles.xml")),
        ],
        [
            "styles-caps-final-dot",
            "#975: the same, named by styles.xml/. (RFC 3986: word/styles.xml/, a folder)",
            () => buildDocx(capsStylesAt("styles.xml/.")),
        ],
        [
            "header-calibration",
            "calibration: a default header word/header1.xml holding Head, referenced from the section, named by header1.xml",
            () => buildDocx(headerAt("header1.xml")),
        ],
        [
            "header-final-dot",
            "#975: the same, named by header1.xml/. (RFC 3986: word/header1.xml/, a folder)",
            () => buildDocx(headerAt("header1.xml/.")),
        ],
    ]),
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "src");
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
const jsonl = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "specimens.jsonl");
writeFileSync(jsonl, "");

const verdict = async (file: string, profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
    try {
        const r = await validate(file, { profile });
        return {
            valid: r.valid,
            errors: [
                ...new Set(
                    r.issues
                        .filter((x: { severity: string }) => x.severity === "error")
                        .map((x: { code: string; path?: string }) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`),
                ),
            ],
        };
    } catch (error) {
        return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
    }
};

for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const target = path.join(dir, file);
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        validatorRevision: REVISION,
        wordValid: await verdict(target, "word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict(target, "strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(jsonl, JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}
