```ts
// Session 82 (2026-10-28): which parts Word judges a hyperlink's relationship in (#1106).
// `word-hyperlink-relationship` walks `ctx.storyParts()`, the parts named like a story wherever stored, not the parts Word
// reads. Session 28 (s28a) showed Word refuse a `w:hyperlink` whose relationship has the Type `…/relationships/HYPERLINK`
// in word/document.xml and open the exact Transitional Type clean. Each row here puts that shape (refused Type, TargetMode
// External, a URL target) in one placement, beside its calibration with the exact Type:
// s82a: the main document stored as word/document.xml (s28a repeated), the main document stored as word/main.xml, a used
// header stored as word/header1.xml, and a used header stored as word/hdr.xml.
// s82b: an unrelated word/header9.xml typed header by its Override (no relationship names it), a glossary stored as
// word/glossary/document.xml that no relationship reaches, and the same glossary reached by the main document's
// glossaryDocument relationship.
// Every row records the validator revision it was judged at (`validatorRevision`); the verdict helper and the glossary are
// s81builder.mts's.
// The builder empties the chunk's specimens.jsonl once before its row loop (promised on #825), and its src (#985).
// Run from a worktree root: CHUNK=s82a pnpm exec node --import tsx <this file>
// (the imports are absolute, so the file needs no copy into the worktree; `git rev-parse` reads the cwd's worktree).
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const ROOT = path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);
const WT = process.cwd();
const { validate } = await import(path.join(WT, "src/scripts/office/validate.ts"));
const { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } = await import(path.join(WT, "tests/support/minimal-docx.ts"));
const REVISION = execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();

const W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main";
const R = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships";
const PR = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const SIDECAR = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const P = MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>;
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n`;

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string, to: string) => {
    if (text.split(from).length !== 2) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};
const relationship = (id: string, segment: string, target: string) =>
    `<Relationship Id="${id}" Type="${R}/${segment}" Target="${target}"/>`;
const appendRels = (rels: string, extra: string) => replaceOnce(rels, "</Relationships>", `${extra}</Relationships>`);
const relsPart = (body: string) => `${XML_DECL}<Relationships xmlns="${PR}">${body}</Relationships>`;

const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const MAIN = P["word/document.xml"]!;
const overrides = (ct: string, ...pairs: [string, string][]) =>
    pairs.reduce(
        (types, [part, type]) => replaceOnce(types, "</Types>", `<Override PartName="/${part}" ContentType="${type}"/></Types>`),
        ct,
    );
const withR = (doc: string) => replaceOnce(doc, `<w:document xmlns:w="${W}"`, `<w:document xmlns:w="${W}" xmlns:r="${R}"`);

/** Session 28's refused Type, and the exact Transitional Type its calibration uses. */
const REFUSED = "HYPERLINK";
const EXACT = "hyperlink";
/** The hyperlink relationship rIdL of Type segment `segment`, External, to a URL. */
const linkRelationship = (segment: string) =>
    `<Relationship Id="rIdL" Type="${R}/${segment}" Target="https://example.com/" TargetMode="External"/>`;
const LINK_PARAGRAPH = '<w:p><w:hyperlink r:id="rIdL"><w:r><w:t>Link</w:t></w:r></w:hyperlink></w:p>';

/** The main document stored at `mainPart` holding the hyperlink, its sidecar relating the styles part and rIdL. */
const mainWithLink = (mainPart: string, segment: string): Record<string, string> => {
    const parts: Record<string, string> = { ...P };
    const doc = replaceOnce(withR(MAIN), "<w:sectPr>", `${LINK_PARAGRAPH}<w:sectPr>`);
    const sidecar = appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, linkRelationship(segment));
    if (mainPart === "word/document.xml") return { ...parts, "word/document.xml": doc, [SIDECAR]: sidecar };
    delete parts["word/document.xml"];
    delete parts[SIDECAR];
    const name = path.posix.basename(mainPart);
    return {
        ...parts,
        [mainPart]: doc,
        [`word/_rels/${name}.rels`]: sidecar,
        "_rels/.rels": replaceOnce(P["_rels/.rels"]!, 'Target="word/document.xml"', `Target="${mainPart}"`),
        [CT]: replaceOnce(P[CT]!, 'PartName="/word/document.xml"', `PartName="/${mainPart}"`),
    };
};

const HEADER_WITH_LINK = `${XML_DECL}<w:hdr xmlns:w="${W}" xmlns:r="${R}">${LINK_PARAGRAPH}</w:hdr>`;
/** A header stored at word/`headerName` holding the hyperlink, its sidecar relating rIdL, referenced by the section. */
const usedHeaderWithLink = (headerName: string, segment: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    "word/document.xml": replaceOnce(withR(MAIN), "<w:sectPr>", '<w:sectPr><w:headerReference w:type="default" r:id="rIdH"/>'),
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdH", "header", headerName)),
    [`word/${headerName}`]: HEADER_WITH_LINK,
    [`word/_rels/${headerName}.rels`]: relsPart(linkRelationship(segment)),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, [`word/${headerName}`, `${WML}.header+xml`]),
});
/** The same header stored as word/header9.xml and typed header, which no relationship names. */
const unrelatedHeaderWithLink = (segment: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    "word/header9.xml": HEADER_WITH_LINK,
    "word/_rels/header9.xml.rels": relsPart(linkRelationship(segment)),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, ["word/header9.xml", `${WML}.header+xml`]),
});

const glossaryWithLink =
    `${XML_DECL}<w:glossaryDocument xmlns:w="${W}" xmlns:r="${R}"><w:docParts><w:docPart><w:docPartPr><w:name w:val="Part"/>` +
    `<w:category><w:name w:val="General"/><w:gallery w:val="placeholder"/></w:category><w:guid w:val="{6A9E2C40-3F1B-4C55-9D2E-7B1A0C9D4E11}"/></w:docPartPr>` +
    `<w:docPartBody>${LINK_PARAGRAPH}</w:docPartBody></w:docPart></w:docParts></w:glossaryDocument>`;
/** A glossary stored as word/glossary/document.xml holding the hyperlink; the main document relates it when `reached`. */
const glossaryLink = (reached: boolean, segment: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    "word/glossary/document.xml": glossaryWithLink,
    "word/glossary/_rels/document.xml.rels": relsPart(linkRelationship(segment)),
    ...(reached ? { [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdG", "glossaryDocument", "glossary/document.xml")) } : {}),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, ["word/glossary/document.xml", `${WML}.document.glossary+xml`]),
});

/** A header stored as word/header1.xml holding the hyperlink, which the main document relates but no section references. */
const unusedHeaderWithLink = (segment: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdH", "header", "header1.xml")),
    "word/header1.xml": HEADER_WITH_LINK,
    "word/_rels/header1.xml.rels": relsPart(linkRelationship(segment)),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, ["word/header1.xml", `${WML}.header+xml`]),
});
const FOOTNOTES_WITH_LINK = `${XML_DECL}<w:footnotes xmlns:w="${W}" xmlns:r="${R}"><w:footnote w:id="1">${LINK_PARAGRAPH}</w:footnote></w:footnotes>`;
/** word/footnotes.xml whose footnote 1 holds the hyperlink, related by the main document, which references it when `used`. */
const footnotesWithLink = (used: boolean, segment: string): Record<string, string> => ({
    ...P,
    ...(used
        ? {
              "word/document.xml": replaceOnce(
                  MAIN,
                  "<w:r><w:t>Hello</w:t></w:r>",
                  '<w:r><w:t>Hello</w:t></w:r><w:r><w:footnoteReference w:id="1"/></w:r>',
              ),
          }
        : {}),
    [SIDECAR]: appendRels(P[SIDECAR]!, relationship("rIdN", "footnotes", "footnotes.xml")),
    "word/footnotes.xml": FOOTNOTES_WITH_LINK,
    "word/_rels/footnotes.xml.rels": relsPart(linkRelationship(segment)),
    [CT]: overrides(P[CT]!, ["word/footnotes.xml", `${WML}.footnotes+xml`]),
});

type Row = [string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>];
const control = () => buildDocx({ ...P });
const withControls = (chunk: string, rows: Row[]): Row[] => [
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal`, "control", control],
    ...rows,
    [`${chunk}-control-minimal-end`, "control", control],
];

const chunks: Record<string, Row[]> = {
    s82a: withControls("s82a", [
        [
            "main-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: s28a repeated, a hyperlink in word/document.xml whose relationship has the Type …/HYPERLINK",
            () => buildDocx(mainWithLink("word/document.xml", REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "main-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(mainWithLink("word/document.xml", EXACT)),
        ],
        [
            "renamed-main-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: the same hyperlink in a main document stored as word/main.xml",
            () => buildDocx(mainWithLink("word/main.xml", REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "renamed-main-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(mainWithLink("word/main.xml", EXACT)),
        ],
        [
            "header1-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: the same hyperlink in a used header stored as word/header1.xml",
            () => buildDocx(usedHeaderWithLink("header1.xml", REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "header1-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(usedHeaderWithLink("header1.xml", EXACT)),
        ],
        [
            "renamed-header-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: the same hyperlink in a used header stored as word/hdr.xml",
            () => buildDocx(usedHeaderWithLink("hdr.xml", REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "renamed-header-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(usedHeaderWithLink("hdr.xml", EXACT)),
        ],
    ]),
    s82b: withControls("s82b", [
        [
            "unrelated-header9-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: the same hyperlink in word/header9.xml, typed header, which no relationship names",
            () => buildDocx(unrelatedHeaderWithLink(REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "unrelated-header9-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(unrelatedHeaderWithLink(EXACT)),
        ],
        [
            "unreached-glossary-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: the same hyperlink in word/glossary/document.xml, which no relationship reaches",
            () => buildDocx(glossaryLink(false, REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "unreached-glossary-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(glossaryLink(false, EXACT)),
        ],
        [
            "reached-glossary-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: the same hyperlink in a glossary the main document relates",
            () => buildDocx(glossaryLink(true, REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "reached-glossary-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(glossaryLink(true, EXACT)),
        ],
    ]),
    // s82c: the stories the read model leaves out because their root does not use them, beside a used notes part.
    s82c: withControls("s82c", [
        [
            "unused-header1-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: the same hyperlink in word/header1.xml, which the main document relates but no section references",
            () => buildDocx(unusedHeaderWithLink(REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "unused-header1-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(unusedHeaderWithLink(EXACT)),
        ],
        [
            "unused-footnotes-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: the same hyperlink in footnote 1 of word/footnotes.xml, which the main document relates but does not reference",
            () => buildDocx(footnotesWithLink(false, REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "unused-footnotes-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(footnotesWithLink(false, EXACT)),
        ],
        [
            "used-footnotes-link-refused-type",
            "#1106: the same, the body referencing footnote 1",
            () => buildDocx(footnotesWithLink(true, REFUSED)),
        ],
        [
            "used-footnotes-link-calibration",
            "calibration: the same with the exact hyperlink Type",
            () => buildDocx(footnotesWithLink(true, EXACT)),
        ],
    ]),
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "src");
// A rerun starts from an empty src, so a removed or renamed row leaves no stale specimen for the staging and log-check
// scripts to pick up (CodeRabbit on #985).
rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
const jsonl = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "specimens.jsonl");
writeFileSync(jsonl, "");

const verdict = async (file: string, profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
    try {
        const r = await validate(file, { profile });
        return {
            valid: r.valid,
            errors: [
                ...new Set(
                    r.issues
                        .filter((x: { severity: string }) => x.severity === "error")
                        .map((x: { code: string; path?: string }) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`),
                ),
            ],
        };
    } catch (error) {
        return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
    }
};

for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const target = path.join(dir, file);
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        validatorRevision: REVISION,
        wordValid: await verdict(target, "word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict(target, "strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(jsonl, JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid} ${row.strict.errors.join(",")}`,
    );
}
```

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-82 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s82a", "s82b", "s82c")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0], "unknown") if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": spec["issue"] == "control",
                     # A match needs agreed readings: an unknown row matches nothing (CodeRabbit on #985).
                     "validatorMatchesWord": agreed and ((all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True))})
(ROOT / "s82/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

`section.py`:

"""Render the session-82 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s82/section.md.

Reads each chunk's specimens.jsonl (written by the builder, each row carrying the validator revision it was judged at),
both runs' logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and the results.json compare.py writes. The validator label comes from
the rows' `validatorRevision`, never from this script (CodeRabbit on #796). The text Word rendered is read from its own
PDFs with pdftotext, so the narrative's "rendered" claims are checked here.
"""
import json
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s82a", "s82b", "s82c")
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s82/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    # A builder records valid: null when validate() threw; render that as the exception, not as a rejection.
    if v["valid"] is None:
        return "threw: " + ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in v["errors"])
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e.split('@')[0]}`" for e in v["errors"])


def manifest(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return row
    raise KeyError(file)


def run_at(run, file):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(manifest(run, file)["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


def rendered(run, file):
    pdf = run / "pdf" / (Path(file).stem + "_byword.pdf")
    if not pdf.exists():
        return None
    return " ".join(subprocess.run(["pdftotext", str(pdf), "-"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split())


rows, raw, starts, ends, revisions = [], [], [], [], set()
agreed = 0
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        revisions.add(s.get("validatorRevision", "unknown"))
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]
        starts.append(times[0])
        ends.append(times[1])
        result = results[(label, s["file"])]
        agreed += result["agreed"]
        shape = s["issue"].replace("|", "\\|")
        rows.append(
            f"| `{label}` | {times[0]:%H:%M:%S}Z, {times[1]:%H:%M:%S}Z | `{s['name']}` | {shape} | `{s['sha256'][:16]}` | "
            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):
            row = c[s["file"]]
            record = {"run": label, "pass": n, "name": s["name"], "sha256": s["sha256"],
                      "validatorRevision": s.get("validatorRevision"), "observedAt": t.isoformat(),
                      "staged": row["staged"], "logVerdict": row["logVerdict"], "tableVerdict": row["outcomesVerdict"],
                      "pdf": row["pdf"], "evidence": row["evidence"]}
            error = manifest(r, s["file"]).get("error")
            if error:
                record["error"] = error
            raw.append(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False))

assert len(revisions) == 1, revisions
rev = next(iter(revisions))
at = rev[:8] if rev != "unknown" else "an unrecorded revision"

OVERREACH = {"unrelated-header9-link-refused-type.docx", "unreached-glossary-link-refused-type.docx",
             "unused-header1-link-refused-type.docx", "unused-footnotes-link-refused-type.docx"}
# The narrative's claims about outcomes, checked against results.json: every row's four readings agree, the refused

for (label, file), r in results.items():

    assert set(r["readings"]) == ({"repair-warning"} if file in REFUSED else {"clean-open"}), (label, file, r)
    assert r["wordValid"] is ((file not in REFUSED or file in MISSED) and file not in OVERREACH), (label, file, r)
    assert r["validatorMatchesWord"] is (file not in MISSED | OVERREACH), (label, file, r)
assert agreed == len(rows) == 26, (agreed, len(rows))
# The driver opens files in name order (#671).
for label in CHUNKS:
    files = sorted(json.loads(l)["file"] for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines())
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        opened = [json.loads(l)["original_filename"] for l in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
        assert opened == files, (run, opened)
# The text Word rendered in each clean row, both runs: the hyperlink's "Link" after "Hello" in a main document, before

### Session 83: 13:05Z–13:09Z on 2026-10-28, validator columns at 568d746a

Whether Word judges [#1113](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/1113)'s Word-blocking rules in the parts it reads, as session 82 found for the hyperlink relationship. Twenty check files, holding 26 Word rules, judge the parts named like a story wherever stored (`STORY_PART`), not the parts Word reads. Eleven of those rules, in eight of the files, have a Word-refused fixture whose finding is only in `word/document.xml` and a clean twin (session 41's pairs; the `-shape` pair for `word-textbox-deleted-text`, whose plain fixture holds its defect in a footer). Each pair gives three rows: `-main` is the broken fixture with its main document stored as `word/main.xml`, with `_rels/.rels`, the content-types Override and the part's own relationships following the name; `-main-calibration` is the clean twin renamed the same way; `-unrelated-header` is the clean twin plus `word/header83.xml`, typed header by its Override, which no relationship names, holding the broken fixture's body under a `w:hdr` root with its `w:sectPr` removed, and the broken main document's relationships as its own. Chunk s83a holds `word-row-without-cell`, `word-cell-ends-with-table` and `word-drawing-arc-radius`; s83b `word-drawing-extent-negative`, `word-empty-drawing` and `word-anchor-missing-attribute`; s83c `word-text-contains-paragraph`, `word-textbox-deleted-text` and `word-move-from-deleted-text`; s83d `word-sdt-id-empty` and `word-choice-requires-undeclared`. Each chunk ends with a minimal control. Each chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; 37 of 37 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen. The builder recorded the validator revision in every row (`568d746adf4aaa478735b82672c3bbd66c858355`). The strict column leaves out the `rels-unreferenced`, `paraid-missing-element`, `xsd-summary` and `xsd-error` findings and names every other strict error, so beside the probed rule it also names fixture findings such as `textid-missing-element` and `style-default-missing` (#1124).

Every calibration and control opened clean. Each unrelated header's PDF holds exactly its calibration's text in both runs (`pdftotext`; the `word-empty-drawing` and `word-choice-requires-undeclared` twins render no text), and each control's holds `Hello`. No refused row left a PDF.

- **Word judges the eleven shapes in a main document whatever its name.** It refused all eleven renamed main documents, as it did in `word/document.xml` (session 41): an open error for 7 (`word-row-without-cell`, `word-drawing-arc-radius`, `word-drawing-extent-negative`, `word-empty-drawing`, `word-anchor-missing-attribute`, `word-text-contains-paragraph`, `word-sdt-id-empty`) and an offer to recover unreadable content for 4 (`word-cell-ends-with-table`, `word-textbox-deleted-text`, `word-move-from-deleted-text`, `word-choice-requires-undeclared`).
- **It does not judge them in a part it does not read.** It opened every shape clean in the unrelated `word/header83.xml`, as the read model says it reads no part that no relationship names (#726).

Word-valid at 568d746a judged by name, so it matches Word on 16 of 37 rows: it passes ten of the renamed main documents and rejects all eleven unrelated headers. It rejects the renamed `word-choice-requires-undeclared` row only through `mce-malformed`, which judges every part: that rule also rejects the unrelated header Word opened clean. [#1113](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/1113) moves the rules onto the read model.

`s83builder.mts`:

```ts
// Session 83 (2026-10-28): which parts Word judges the by-name story rules' shapes in (#1113).
// Twenty check files walk `ctx.storyParts()`, the parts named like a story wherever stored, not the parts Word reads.
// Session 82 (#1106) showed the cost for `word-hyperlink-relationship`: Word refused its shape in a main document stored
// as word/main.xml and opened it clean in an unrelated word/header9.xml. This session asks the same of the Word-blocking
// rules whose refused shape session 41 attributes to one fixture pair (a broken fixture Word refused, a twin it opened
// clean). For each pair, three rows:
// - `<rule>-main`: the broken fixture with its main document stored as word/main.xml (_rels/.rels, the content-types
//   Override and the sidecar's name follow), whose shape the by-name list does not judge;
// - `<rule>-main-calibration`: the clean twin renamed the same way;
// - `<rule>-unrelated-header`: the clean twin plus word/header83.xml (session 82 used header9, which one fixture
//   stores), typed header by its Override, which no relationship names,
//   holding the broken main document's body (its w:sectPr elements dropped) under a w:hdr root with the document root's
//   attributes, and a copy of the broken main document's relationships as its sidecar. The by-name list judges it.
// Each pair's broken fixture must hold the rule's finding in word/document.xml (the builder checks it), so session 41's
// word-textbox-deleted-text pair is its `-shape` one: the plain fixture's defect sits in footer1.xml.
// Every row records the validator revision it was judged at (`validatorRevision`); the verdict helper is s82builder.mts's.
// The builder empties the chunk's specimens.jsonl once before its row loop (promised on #825), and its src (#985).
// Run from a worktree root: CHUNK=s83a pnpm exec node --import tsx <this file>
// (the imports are absolute, so the file needs no copy into the worktree; `git rev-parse` reads the cwd's worktree).
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const ROOT = path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);
const WT = process.cwd();
const { validate } = await import(path.join(WT, "src/scripts/office/validate.ts"));
const { parseXml } = await import(path.join(WT, "src/lib/xml-helpers.ts"));
const { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } = await import(path.join(WT, "tests/support/minimal-docx.ts"));
const JSZip = createRequire(path.join(WT, "package.json"))("jszip");
const REVISION = execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();
const FIXTURES = path.join(WT, "tests/fixtures");

const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const MAIN = "word/document.xml";
const MAIN_RELS = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\r\n`;

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string | RegExp, to: string) => {
    const count = typeof from === "string" ? text.split(from).length - 1 : (text.match(new RegExp(from.source, "g")) ?? []).length;
    if (count !== 1) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}, found ${count}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};

type Parts = Map<string, Uint8Array>;
const utf8 = new TextDecoder("utf-8");
const encoder = new TextEncoder();
const textOf = (parts: Parts, name: string) => {
    const bytes = parts.get(name);
    if (!bytes) throw new Error(`no ${name}`);
    const text = utf8.decode(bytes);
    return text.charCodeAt(0) === 0xfeff ? text.slice(1) : text;
};

/** The fixture's parts in stored order. */
const load = async (rel: string): Promise<Parts> => {
    const zip = await JSZip.loadAsync(readFileSync(path.join(FIXTURES, rel)));
    const parts: Parts = new Map();
    for (const name of Object.keys(zip.files)) {
        if (!zip.files[name].dir) parts.set(name, await zip.files[name].async("uint8array"));
    }
    return parts;
};
const pack = async (parts: Parts): Promise<Uint8Array> => {
    const zip = new JSZip();
    for (const [name, bytes] of parts) zip.file(name, bytes, { compression: "DEFLATE" });
    return zip.generateAsync({ type: "uint8array", compression: "DEFLATE" });
};

/** The package with its main document stored as word/main.xml; every name that points at it follows. */
const renameMain = (parts: Parts): Parts => {
    if (!parts.has(MAIN)) throw new Error("no word/document.xml");
    const out: Parts = new Map();
    for (const [name, bytes] of parts) {
        if (name === MAIN) out.set("word/main.xml", bytes);
        else if (name === MAIN_RELS) out.set("word/_rels/main.xml.rels", bytes);
        else if (name === "_rels/.rels")
            out.set(
                name,
                encoder.encode(replaceOnce(textOf(parts, name), /Target="(\/?)word\/document\.xml"/, 'Target="$1word/main.xml"')),
            );
        else if (name === CT)
            out.set(name, encoder.encode(replaceOnce(textOf(parts, name), 'PartName="/word/document.xml"', 'PartName="/word/main.xml"')));
        else out.set(name, bytes);
    }
    return out;
};

/** `text` without its outermost `<tag>` elements, nested ones (a w:sectPr inside a w:sectPrChange) counted, not matched. */
const withoutElements = (text: string, tag: string): string => {
    const token = new RegExp(`<${tag}\\b[^>]*?(/?)>|</${tag}>`, "g");
    let out = "";
    let depth = 0;
    let start = 0;
    let cut = 0;
    for (let match = token.exec(text); match; match = token.exec(text)) {
        const closing = match[0].startsWith("</");
        const selfClosing = !closing && match[1] === "/";
        if (depth === 0 && !closing) {
            out += text.slice(cut, match.index);
            start = match.index;
            if (selfClosing) {
                cut = token.lastIndex;
                continue;
            }
            depth = 1;
        } else if (closing) {
            depth -= 1;
            if (depth < 0) throw new Error(`unbalanced </${tag}>`);
            if (depth === 0) cut = token.lastIndex;
        } else if (!selfClosing) {
            depth += 1;
        }
    }
    if (depth !== 0) throw new Error(`unclosed <${tag}> at ${start}`);
    return out + text.slice(cut);
};

/** `broken`'s main-document body as a header part: the w:document root's attributes on w:hdr, its w:sectPr elements dropped. */
const bodyAsHeader = (doc: string): string => {
    const attributes = doc.match(/<w:document\b([^>]*)>/)?.[1];
    const body = doc.match(/<w:body>([\s\S]*)<\/w:body>/)?.[1];
    if (attributes === undefined || body === undefined) throw new Error("no w:document root or w:body");
    const inner = withoutElements(body, "w:sectPr");
    if (!/<w:(p|tbl|sdt)\b/.test(inner)) throw new Error("the body holds no block-level content");
    const header = `${XML_DECL}<w:hdr${attributes}>${inner}</w:hdr>`;
    parseXml(header);
    return header;
};

const UNRELATED = "header83.xml";
/** The clean twin plus word/header83.xml, typed header and named by no relationship, holding the broken body. */
const withUnrelatedHeader = (clean: Parts, broken: Parts): Parts => {
    if ([...clean.keys()].some((name) => name.toLowerCase().includes(UNRELATED))) throw new Error(`the twin already stores ${UNRELATED}`);
    const out: Parts = new Map(clean);
    out.set(
        CT,
        encoder.encode(
            replaceOnce(textOf(clean, CT), "</Types>", `<Override PartName="/word/${UNRELATED}" ContentType="${WML}.header+xml"/></Types>`),
        ),
    );
    out.set(`word/${UNRELATED}`, encoder.encode(bodyAsHeader(textOf(broken, MAIN))));
    out.set(`word/_rels/${UNRELATED}.rels`, broken.get(MAIN_RELS)!);
    return out;
};

/** Session 41's pairs: the rule, the fixture Word refused, and the twin it opened clean. */
const PAIRS: Record<string, [string, string, string]> = {
    "row-without-cell": [
        "word-row-without-cell",
        "broken/package.word-row-without-cell.docx",
        "working/package.word-row-without-cell-repaired.docx",
    ],
    "cell-ends-with-table": [
        "word-cell-ends-with-table",
        "broken/package.word-cell-ends-with-table.docx",
        "working/package.word-cell-ends-with-table-repaired.docx",
    ],
    "arc-radius": ["word-drawing-arc-radius", "broken/package.drawing-arc-radius.docx", "working/package.drawing-arc-radius-integer.docx"],
    "extent-negative": [
        "word-drawing-extent-negative",
        "broken/package.word-drawing-extent-negative.docx",
        "working/package.word-drawing-extent-positive.docx",
    ],
    "empty-drawing": ["word-empty-drawing", "broken/package.word-empty-drawing.docx", "working/package.word-empty-drawing-removed.docx"],
    "anchor-open": [
        "word-anchor-missing-attribute",
        "broken/package.word-anchor-open.docx",
        "working/package.word-anchor-open-repaired.docx",
    ],
    "text-contains-paragraph": [
        "word-text-contains-paragraph",
        "broken/package.word-text-contains-paragraph.docx",
        "working/package.word-text-contains-paragraph-lifted.docx",
    ],
    "textbox-deleted-text": [
        "word-textbox-deleted-text",
        "broken/package.word-textbox-deleted-text-shape.docx",
        "working/package.word-textbox-deleted-text-shape-repaired.docx",
    ],
    "move-from-deleted-text": [
        "word-move-from-deleted-text",
        "broken/package.word-move-from-deleted-text.docx",
        "working/package.word-move-from-text.docx",
    ],
    "sdt-id-empty": ["word-sdt-id-empty", "broken/package.word-sdt-id-empty.docx", "working/package.word-sdt-id-empty-repaired.docx"],
    "choice-requires-undeclared": [
        "word-choice-requires-undeclared",
        "broken/package.word-choice-requires-undeclared.docx",
        "working/package.word-choice-requires-declared.docx",
    ],
};

type Row = [string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>];
/** The three rows for one pair. */
const rowsFor = (key: string): Row[] => {
    const [rule, broken, clean] = PAIRS[key]!;
    return [
        [
            `${key}-main`,
            `#1113 ${rule}: ${broken} with its main document stored as word/main.xml`,
            async () => pack(renameMain(await load(broken))),
        ],
        [`${key}-main-calibration`, `calibration: ${clean} renamed the same way`, async () => pack(renameMain(await load(clean)))],
        [
            `${key}-unrelated-header`,
            `#1113 ${rule}: ${clean} plus an unrelated word/${UNRELATED} holding ${broken}'s body`,
            async () => pack(withUnrelatedHeader(await load(clean), await load(broken))),
        ],
    ];
};
const control = () => buildDocx({ ...(MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>) });
const withControl = (chunk: string, keys: string[]): Row[] => [...keys.flatMap(rowsFor), [`${chunk}-control-minimal`, "control", control]];

const chunks: Record<string, Row[]> = {
    s83a: withControl("s83a", ["row-without-cell", "cell-ends-with-table", "arc-radius"]),
    s83b: withControl("s83b", ["extent-negative", "empty-drawing", "anchor-open"]),
    s83c: withControl("s83c", ["text-contains-paragraph", "textbox-deleted-text", "move-from-deleted-text"]),
    s83d: withControl("s83d", ["sdt-id-empty", "choice-requires-undeclared"]),
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "src");
// A rerun starts from an empty src, so a removed or renamed row leaves no stale specimen (CodeRabbit on #985).
rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
const jsonl = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "specimens.jsonl");
writeFileSync(jsonl, "");

const verdict = async (file: string, profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
    try {
        const r = await validate(file, { profile });
        return {
            valid: r.valid,
            errors: [
                ...new Set(
                    r.issues
                        .filter((x: { severity: string }) => x.severity === "error")
                        .map((x: { code: string; path?: string }) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`),
                ),
            ],
        };
    } catch (error) {
        return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
    }
};

for (const key of Object.keys(PAIRS)) {
    if (!specimens.some(([name]) => name.startsWith(`${key}-`))) continue;
    const [rule, broken] = PAIRS[key]!;
    const found = (await validate(path.join(FIXTURES, broken), { profile: "word-valid" })).issues.filter(
        (x: { code: string }) => x.code === rule,
    );
    if (found.length === 0 || found.some((x: { path?: string }) => x.path !== MAIN))
        throw new Error(`${broken}: ${rule} is not only in ${MAIN}`);
}

for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const target = path.join(dir, file);
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        control: issue === "control",
        validatorRevision: REVISION,
        wordValid: await verdict(target, "word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict(target, "strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(jsonl, JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid}`,
    );
}
```

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-83 chunks: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s83a", "s83b", "s83c", "s83d")
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0], "unknown") if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": spec["issue"] == "control",
                     # A match needs agreed readings: an unknown row matches nothing (CodeRabbit on #985).
                     "validatorMatchesWord": agreed and ((all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True))})
(ROOT / "s83/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

"""Render the session-83 parts of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s83/section.md.

Reads each chunk's specimens.jsonl (written by the builder, each row carrying the validator revision it was judged at),
both runs' logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and the results.json compare.py writes. The validator label comes from
the rows' `validatorRevision`, never from this script (CodeRabbit on #796). The text Word rendered is read from its own
PDFs with pdftotext, so the narrative's "rendered" claims are checked here.
"""

import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s83/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    # A builder records valid: null when validate() threw; render that as the exception, not as a rejection.
    if v["valid"] is None:
        return "threw: " + ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in v["errors"])
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in v["errors"])


def strict_cell(v):
    # Strict also reports the fixtures' own paraId, XSD and unreferenced-part findings; leave those out and name every
    # other code with its part, so the column shows whether strict judged the probed rule. The fixtures' other findings,
    # such as textid-missing-element, stay in the column (#1124).
    if v["valid"] is None:
        return cell(v)
    noise = ("rels-unreferenced@", "paraid-missing-element@", "xsd-summary@", "xsd-error@")
    rules = [e for e in v["errors"] if not e.startswith(noise)]
    if v["valid"]:
        return "valid"
    return "invalid: " + (", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in rules) if rules else "fixture findings only")


def manifest(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return row
    raise KeyError(file)


def run_at(run, file):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(manifest(run, file)["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


def rendered(run, file):
    pdf = run / "pdf" / (Path(file).stem + "_byword.pdf")
    if not pdf.exists():
        return None
    return " ".join(subprocess.run(["pdftotext", str(pdf), "-"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split())


rows, raw, starts, ends, revisions = [], [], [], [], set()
agreed = 0
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"]
    checks = [{json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (r / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()} for r in runs]
    for s in specs:
        revisions.add(s.get("validatorRevision", "unknown"))
        times = [run_at(r, s["file"]) for r in runs]

            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {strict_cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )
        for n, (r, c, t) in enumerate(zip(runs, checks, times), start=1):

### Session 84: 14:01Z–14:01Z on 2026-10-28, validator columns at 51288228

Whether Word judges markup compatibility in a `word/` part it does not read ([#1116](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/1116)). Session 83 (s83d) opened clean an undeclared-`Requires` Choice (`mce-malformed`) in a `word/header83.xml` that no relationship names, and refused it in a main document stored as `word/main.xml`. `mce-must-understand` in such a part was unprobed, and #639's rows pinned it blocking in a stray `word/foo.xml`. One chunk, s84a, mostly on the minimal package:

- `mu-unrelated-header` adds `word/header83.xml`, typed header by its Override and named by no relationship, whose `w:hdr` root carries `mc:MustUnderstand="foo"` for an unknown `urn:foo`; its `-calibration` drops the attribute;
- `mu-stray-foo` is #639's specimen, `word/foo.xml` with no Override and no relationship, a `w:document` root carrying the same attribute around an empty body, with its `-calibration`;
- `mu-used-header` has the main document relate the header and the body's `w:sectPr` reference it, and `mu-unused-header` has it related and referenced by nothing;
- `mu-main` puts the attribute on the main document's root;
- `choice-unused-header` is session 83's `choice-requires-undeclared-unrelated-header` with the main document relating the header and nothing referencing it.

The chunk ends with a minimal control. It ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; 9 of 9 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen. The builder recorded the validator revision in every row (`51288228dfe6ca4454d16562ec0a4798364614ab`), judging an export of that commit. The strict column names only the markup-compatibility findings.

Every calibration and the control opened clean. Every row Word opened renders the main document's `Hello` in both runs (`pdftotext`), never the header's `Header 84`; the Choice row renders no text, as its clean twin did in session 83. No refused row left a PDF.

- **Word refuses an unknown `mc:MustUnderstand` in a part it reads.** It offered to recover unreadable content for the main document's root and for a header the body references.
- **It does not judge it in a part no relationship names.** It opened clean the unrelated header and #639's stray `word/foo.xml`, as it opened session 83's Choice there.
- **Nor in a header the main document relates but does not use.** It opened clean the related, unreferenced header holding the attribute and the one holding session 83's Choice.

Staging the second run and reading the logs used session 41's `stage_pass2.py` and `logcheck.py`, above, unchanged. The builder ran on an export of the recorded revision (`git archive`), `node_modules` linked in, with `WT` and `REVISION` naming them.

```ts
// Session 84 (2026-10-28): does Word read markup compatibility in a word/ part no relationship names (#1116)?
// Session 83 (s83d) opened clean an undeclared-Requires Choice (`mce-malformed`) in an unrelated word/header83.xml and
// refused it in a main document stored as word/main.xml. #1116 lets `mce-malformed` and `mce-must-understand` warn in a
// word/ part no relationship names; `mce-must-understand` there is unprobed, and #639's rows pin it blocking in a stray
// word/foo.xml. Rows, on the minimal package (`tests/support/minimal-docx.ts`) unless named otherwise:
// - `mu-unrelated-header`: word/header83.xml, typed header by its Override, named by no relationship, whose w:hdr root
//   carries mc:MustUnderstand="foo" for an unknown urn:foo; its `-calibration` drops the attribute;
// - `mu-stray-foo`: #639's specimen, word/foo.xml with no Override and no relationship, a w:document root carrying the
//   same MustUnderstand and an empty body; its `-calibration` drops the attribute;
// - `mu-used-header`: the header related by the main document and referenced by its w:sectPr, the read placement;
// - `mu-unused-header`: the header related by the main document, referenced by nothing (unprobed for these findings);
// - `mu-main`: the main document's root carrying the MustUnderstand;
// - `choice-unused-header`: s83d's `choice-requires-undeclared-unrelated-header` with the main document relating the
//   header and nothing referencing it (`mce-malformed` in a related, unused part, unprobed);
// - a minimal control.
// Every row records the validator revision it was judged at (`validatorRevision`).
// Run: WT=<exported tree> REVISION=<its commit> CHUNK=s84a tsx <this file>
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const ROOT = path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);
// WT names an exported tree (no .git), REVISION the commit it was exported at.
const WT = process.env.WT ?? process.cwd();
const { validate } = await import(path.join(WT, "src/scripts/office/validate.ts"));
const { parseXml } = await import(path.join(WT, "src/lib/xml-helpers.ts"));
const { MINIMAL_PARTS, buildDocx } = await import(path.join(WT, "tests/support/minimal-docx.ts"));
const JSZip = createRequire(path.join(WT, "package.json"))("jszip");
const REVISION = process.env.REVISION ?? execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();
const FIXTURES = path.join(WT, "tests/fixtures");

const WML = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml";
const CT = "[Content_Types].xml";
const MAIN = "word/document.xml";
const MAIN_RELS = "word/_rels/document.xml.rels";
const XML_DECL = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\r\n`;

const replaceOnce = (text: string, from: string | RegExp, to: string) => {
    const count = typeof from === "string" ? text.split(from).length - 1 : (text.match(new RegExp(from.source, "g")) ?? []).length;
    if (count !== 1) throw new Error(`expected exactly one ${from}, found ${count}`);
    return text.replace(from, to);
};

type Parts = Map<string, Uint8Array>;
const utf8 = new TextDecoder("utf-8");
const encoder = new TextEncoder();
const textOf = (parts: Parts, name: string) => {
    const bytes = parts.get(name);
    if (!bytes) throw new Error(`no ${name}`);
    const text = utf8.decode(bytes);
    return text.charCodeAt(0) === 0xfeff ? text.slice(1) : text;
};

/** The fixture's parts in stored order. */
const load = async (rel: string): Promise<Parts> => {
    const zip = await JSZip.loadAsync(readFileSync(path.join(FIXTURES, rel)));
    const parts: Parts = new Map();
    for (const name of Object.keys(zip.files)) {
        if (!zip.files[name].dir) parts.set(name, await zip.files[name].async("uint8array"));
    }
    return parts;
};
const pack = async (parts: Parts): Promise<Uint8Array> => {
    const zip = new JSZip();
    for (const [name, bytes] of parts) zip.file(name, bytes, { compression: "DEFLATE" });
    return zip.generateAsync({ type: "uint8array", compression: "DEFLATE" });
};

/** The package with its main document stored as word/main.xml; every name that points at it follows. */
const renameMain = (parts: Parts): Parts => {
    if (!parts.has(MAIN)) throw new Error("no word/document.xml");
    const out: Parts = new Map();
    for (const [name, bytes] of parts) {
        if (name === MAIN) out.set("word/main.xml", bytes);
        else if (name === MAIN_RELS) out.set("word/_rels/main.xml.rels", bytes);
        else if (name === "_rels/.rels")
            out.set(
                name,
                encoder.encode(replaceOnce(textOf(parts, name), /Target="(\/?)word\/document\.xml"/, 'Target="$1word/main.xml"')),
            );
        else if (name === CT)
            out.set(name, encoder.encode(replaceOnce(textOf(parts, name), 'PartName="/word/document.xml"', 'PartName="/word/main.xml"')));
        else out.set(name, bytes);
    }
    return out;
};

/** `text` without its outermost `<tag>` elements, nested ones (a w:sectPr inside a w:sectPrChange) counted, not matched. */
const withoutElements = (text: string, tag: string): string => {
    const token = new RegExp(`<${tag}\\b[^>]*?(/?)>|</${tag}>`, "g");
    let out = "";
    let depth = 0;
    let start = 0;
    let cut = 0;
    for (let match = token.exec(text); match; match = token.exec(text)) {
        const closing = match[0].startsWith("</");
        const selfClosing = !closing && match[1] === "/";
        if (depth === 0 && !closing) {
            out += text.slice(cut, match.index);
            start = match.index;
            if (selfClosing) {
                cut = token.lastIndex;
                continue;
            }
            depth = 1;
        } else if (closing) {
            depth -= 1;
            if (depth < 0) throw new Error(`unbalanced </${tag}>`);
            if (depth === 0) cut = token.lastIndex;
        } else if (!selfClosing) {
            depth += 1;
        }
    }
    if (depth !== 0) throw new Error(`unclosed <${tag}> at ${start}`);
    return out + text.slice(cut);
};

/** `broken`'s main-document body as a header part: the w:document root's attributes on w:hdr, its w:sectPr elements dropped. */
const bodyAsHeader = (doc: string): string => {
    const attributes = doc.match(/<w:document\b([^>]*)>/)?.[1];
    const body = doc.match(/<w:body>([\s\S]*)<\/w:body>/)?.[1];
    if (attributes === undefined || body === undefined) throw new Error("no w:document root or w:body");
    const inner = withoutElements(body, "w:sectPr");
    if (!/<w:(p|tbl|sdt)\b/.test(inner)) throw new Error("the body holds no block-level content");
    const header = `${XML_DECL}<w:hdr${attributes}>${inner}</w:hdr>`;
    parseXml(header);
    return header;
};

const UNRELATED = "header83.xml";
/** The clean twin plus word/header83.xml, typed header and named by no relationship, holding the broken body. */
const withUnrelatedHeader = (clean: Parts, broken: Parts): Parts => {
    if ([...clean.keys()].some((name) => name.toLowerCase().includes(UNRELATED))) throw new Error(`the twin already stores ${UNRELATED}`);
    const out: Parts = new Map(clean);
    out.set(
        CT,
        encoder.encode(
            replaceOnce(textOf(clean, CT), "</Types>", `<Override PartName="/word/${UNRELATED}" ContentType="${WML}.header+xml"/></Types>`),
        ),
    );
    out.set(`word/${UNRELATED}`, encoder.encode(bodyAsHeader(textOf(broken, MAIN))));
    out.set(`word/_rels/${UNRELATED}.rels`, broken.get(MAIN_RELS)!);
    return out;
};

const R = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships";
const W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main";
const MC = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/markup-compatibility/2006";
const MU = `xmlns:mc="${MC}" xmlns:foo="urn:foo" mc:MustUnderstand="foo"`;
const minimal = (): Parts =>
    new Map(Object.entries(MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>).map(([name, text]) => [name, encoder.encode(text)]));
const headerXml = (mustUnderstand: boolean) =>
    `${XML_DECL}<w:hdr xmlns:w="${W}"${mustUnderstand ? ` ${MU}` : ""}><w:p><w:r><w:t>Header 84</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:hdr>`;
/** `parts` plus word/header83.xml typed header; `relate` adds the main document's relationship, `use` its w:sectPr reference. */
const withHeader = (parts: Parts, header: string | undefined, relate: boolean, use: boolean): Parts => {
    const out: Parts = new Map(parts);
    if (header !== undefined) {
        out.set(
            CT,
            encoder.encode(
                replaceOnce(
                    textOf(parts, CT),
                    "</Types>",
                    `<Override PartName="/word/${UNRELATED}" ContentType="${WML}.header+xml"/></Types>`,
                ),
            ),
        );
        out.set(`word/${UNRELATED}`, encoder.encode(header));
    }
    if (relate)
        out.set(
            MAIN_RELS,
            encoder.encode(
                replaceOnce(
                    textOf(parts, MAIN_RELS),
                    "</Relationships>",
                    `<Relationship Id="rId84" Type="${R}/header" Target="${UNRELATED}"/></Relationships>`,
                ),
            ),
        );
    if (use) {
        const main = textOf(parts, MAIN);
        const at = main.lastIndexOf("<w:sectPr");
        const open = main.indexOf(">", at) + 1;
        if (at < 0 || main[open - 2] === "/") throw new Error("no open w:sectPr");
        out.set(
            MAIN,
            encoder.encode(`${main.slice(0, open)}<w:headerReference xmlns:r="${R}" w:type="default" r:id="rId84"/>${main.slice(open)}`),
        );
    }
    return out;
};
const STRAY_FOO = (mustUnderstand: boolean) =>
    `${XML_DECL}<w:document xmlns:w="${W}"${mustUnderstand ? ` ${MU}` : ""}><w:body/></w:document>`;
const withStrayFoo = (mustUnderstand: boolean): Parts =>
    new Map([...minimal(), ["word/foo.xml", encoder.encode(STRAY_FOO(mustUnderstand))]]);
const mainMustUnderstand = (): Parts => {
    const parts = minimal();
    // The minimal root already binds mc; add the urn:foo binding and the MustUnderstand only.
    parts.set(
        MAIN,
        encoder.encode(
            replaceOnce(textOf(parts, MAIN), / mc:Ignorable="w14">/, ` xmlns:foo="urn:foo" mc:Ignorable="w14" mc:MustUnderstand="foo">`),
        ),
    );
    return parts;
};
const CHOICE_BROKEN = "broken/package.word-choice-requires-undeclared.docx";
const CHOICE_CLEAN = "working/package.word-choice-requires-declared.docx";

type Row = [string, string, () => Promise<Uint8Array>];
const chunks: Record<string, Row[]> = {
    s84a: [
        [
            "mu-unrelated-header",
            "#1116 mce-must-understand: minimal plus word/header83.xml, typed header, named by no relationship, root MustUnderstand urn:foo",
            async () => pack(withHeader(minimal(), headerXml(true), false, false)),
        ],
        [
            "mu-unrelated-header-calibration",
            "calibration: the same header without MustUnderstand",
            async () => pack(withHeader(minimal(), headerXml(false), false, false)),
        ],
        [
            "mu-stray-foo",
            "#1116/#639 mce-must-understand: minimal plus word/foo.xml (no Override, no relationship), w:document root MustUnderstand urn:foo",
            async () => pack(withStrayFoo(true)),
        ],
        ["mu-stray-foo-calibration", "calibration: the same word/foo.xml without MustUnderstand", async () => pack(withStrayFoo(false))],
        [
            "mu-used-header",
            "#1116 mce-must-understand: the header related by the main document and referenced by its w:sectPr",
            async () => pack(withHeader(minimal(), headerXml(true), true, true)),
        ],
        [
            "mu-unused-header",
            "#1116 mce-must-understand: the header related by the main document, referenced by nothing",
            async () => pack(withHeader(minimal(), headerXml(true), true, false)),
        ],
        [
            "mu-main",
            "#1116 mce-must-understand: the main document's root carrying MustUnderstand urn:foo",
            async () => pack(mainMustUnderstand()),
        ],
        [
            "choice-unused-header",
            `#1116 mce-malformed: ${CHOICE_CLEAN} plus word/${UNRELATED} holding ${CHOICE_BROKEN}'s body, related by the main document, referenced by nothing`,
            async () => pack(withHeader(withUnrelatedHeader(await load(CHOICE_CLEAN), await load(CHOICE_BROKEN)), undefined, true, false)),
        ],
        ["s84a-control-minimal", "control", async () => buildDocx({ ...(MINIMAL_PARTS as Record<string, string>) })],
    ],
};

const chunk = process.env.CHUNK ?? "";
const specimens = chunks[chunk];
if (!specimens) throw new Error(`CHUNK must be one of ${Object.keys(chunks).join(", ")}`);
const dir = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "src");
// A rerun starts from an empty src, so a removed or renamed row leaves no stale specimen (CodeRabbit on #985).
rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
const jsonl = path.join(ROOT, chunk, "specimens.jsonl");
writeFileSync(jsonl, "");

const verdict = async (file: string, profile: "word-valid" | "strict") => {
    try {
        const r = await validate(file, { profile });
        return {
            valid: r.valid,
            errors: [
                ...new Set(
                    r.issues
                        .filter((x: { severity: string }) => x.severity === "error")
                        .map((x: { code: string; path?: string }) => `${x.code}@${x.path ?? "-"}`),
                ),
            ],
        };
    } catch (error) {
        return { valid: null, errors: [`threw:${(error as Error).name}:${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 80)}`] };
    }
};

for (const [name, issue, make] of specimens) {
    const bytes = await make();
    const file = `${name}.docx`;
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, file), bytes);
    const sha256 = createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const target = path.join(dir, file);
    const row = {
        name,
        issue,
        file,
        sha256,
        calibration: name.includes("calibration"),
        control: issue === "control",
        validatorRevision: REVISION,
        wordValid: await verdict(target, "word-valid"),
        strict: await verdict(target, "strict"),
    };
    appendFileSync(jsonl, JSON.stringify(row) + "\n");
    console.log(
        `built ${file} ${sha256.slice(0, 16)} word-valid=${row.wordValid.valid} ${row.wordValid.errors.join(",")} strict=${row.strict.valid}`,
    );
}
```

```python
"""Join both passes of the session-84 chunk: log verdicts, table verdicts, validator verdicts, hashes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s84a",)
TO_MANIFEST = {"clean-open": "clean-open", "repair-warning": "unreadable-content-warning", "open-error": "open-error"}
REJECTIONS = {"repair-warning", "open-error"}
rows = []
for label in CHUNKS:
    specs = {json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / label / "specimens.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()}
    passes = []
    for run in (ROOT / label, ROOT / label / "pass2"):
        for name, spec in specs.items():
            digest = hashlib.sha256((run / "src" / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert digest == spec["sha256"], f"{run}/{name}: {digest} != {spec['sha256']}"
        passes.append({json.loads(l)["file"]: json.loads(l) for l in (run / "logcheck.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()})
    assert set(passes[0]) == set(passes[1]) == set(specs), label
    for name, spec in specs.items():
        p1, p2 = passes[0][name], passes[1][name]
        readings = [p1["logVerdict"], p1["outcomesVerdict"], p2["logVerdict"], p2["outcomesVerdict"]]
        agreed = len(set(readings)) == 1 and not p1["conflict"] and not p2["conflict"]
        outcome = TO_MANIFEST.get(readings[0], "unknown") if agreed else "unknown"
        all_rejected = all(r in REJECTIONS for r in readings)
        all_clean = all(r == "clean-open" for r in readings)
        rows.append({"chunk": label, "file": name, "sha256": spec["sha256"], "readings": readings, "agreed": agreed,
                     "outcome": outcome, "everyReadingRejects": all_rejected, "everyReadingClean": all_clean,
                     "wordValid": spec["wordValid"]["valid"], "control": spec["issue"] == "control",
                     # A match needs agreed readings: an unknown row matches nothing (CodeRabbit on #985).
                     "validatorMatchesWord": agreed and ((all_rejected and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is False) or (all_clean and spec["wordValid"]["valid"] is True))})
(ROOT / "s84/results.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + "\n")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['chunk']} {r['file']:<58} {r['sha256'][:16]} outcome={r['outcome']:<27} word-valid={r['wordValid']!s:<5} match={r['validatorMatchesWord']}")
print("agreed:", sum(r["agreed"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows), "| validator matches Word:", sum(r["validatorMatchesWord"] for r in rows), "/", len(rows))
```

"""Render the session-84 part of docs/plans/evidence/word-probes-2026-10-24.md into s84/section.md.

Reads the chunk's specimens.jsonl (written by the builder, each row carrying the validator revision it was judged at),
both runs' logcheck.jsonl and pdf/manifest.jsonl, and the results.json compare.py writes. The validator label comes from
the rows' `validatorRevision`, never from this script (CodeRabbit on #796). The text Word rendered is read from its own
PDFs with pdftotext, so the narrative's "rendered" claims are checked here.
"""
import json
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CHUNKS = ("s84a",)
results = {(r["chunk"], r["file"]): r for r in json.loads((ROOT / "s84/results.json").read_text())}


def cell(v):
    # A builder records valid: null when validate() threw; render that as the exception, not as a rejection.
    if v["valid"] is None:
        return "threw: " + ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in v["errors"])
    return "valid" if v["valid"] else "invalid: " + ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in v["errors"])


def strict_cell(v):
    # Strict also reports the specimens' unreferenced-part, paraId, content-type and XSD findings; the column names only
    # the markup-compatibility findings, the ones this session probes.
    if v["valid"] is None:
        return cell(v)
    if v["valid"]:
        return "valid"
    mce = [e for e in v["errors"] if e.startswith("mce-")]
    return "invalid: " + (", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in mce) if mce else "no markup-compatibility finding")


def manifest(run, file):
    for line in (run / "pdf/manifest.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row["original_filename"] == file:
            return row
    raise KeyError(file)


def run_at(run, file):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(manifest(run, file)["run_at"]).astimezone(timezone.utc)


def word_cell(check):
    log, table = check["logVerdict"], check["outcomesVerdict"]
    return log if log == table else f"log: {log}; table: {table}"


def rendered(run, file):
    pdf = run / "pdf" / (Path(file).stem + "_byword.pdf")
    if not pdf.exists():
        return None
    return " ".join(subprocess.run(["pdftotext", str(pdf), "-"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split())

            f"{word_cell(checks[0][s['file']])} | {word_cell(checks[1][s['file']])} | {result['outcome']} | {cell(s['wordValid'])} | {strict_cell(s['strict'])} |"
        )

### Session 85: 16:51Z–17:16Z on 2026-10-28, validator columns at 57e150ae

Three open questions, on the minimal package. Five chunks; s85e was added after s85c's first run.

- **s85a and s85b, [#1145](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/1145).** Does Word read a footnotes, endnotes or comments part the main document relates when the part's only reference sits in a used header? Each part's root carries `mc:MustUnderstand="foo"` for an unknown `urn:foo`, which Word refused on the main document's root and in a used header (session 84). Per kind: `-mu-header-reference` has a read header (`word/header1.xml`, referenced by the section) hold the part's only reference; `-mu-body-reference` references the same part from the body; `-header-reference-calibration` is the header-referenced part without the attribute; `-mu-unreferenced` relates the part and references it nowhere. s85b adds a footer holding the attribute, related and unused (`footer-mu-unused`) or referenced by the section (`footer-mu-used`).
- **s85c and s85e, [#1127](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/1127).** Does Word read a part an internal target names through a scheme-like spelling? s85c relates a used header through `Target="ftp:header1.xml"` or `"httpfoo:header1.xml"`, stored as `word/ftp:header1.xml` or `word/httpfoo:header1.xml`, and the styles part through `ftp:styles.xml`, each with an unclosed root and `-wellformed`; the plain-name twins of the unclosed header and styles part are calibrations. s85e separates the stored name from the target: `colon-part-unrelated` stores a well-formed `word/ftp:header1.xml`, typed header and named by no relationship, and `colon-part-default-type` the same part with no Override; `ftp-target-plain-part` and `httpfoo-target-plain-part` relate a used header through the scheme-like target while the part is stored as plain `word/header1.xml`; `header-dotslash-ftp-wellformed` uses the stored `word/ftp:header1.xml` through `Target="./ftp:header1.xml"`, which names it without a scheme.
- **s85d, [#1136](https://github.com/jandira-tech/docx-validate/issues/1136).** Does an unclosed relationships part Word never reads matter? Session 84's `mu-stray-foo` plus an unclosed `word/_rels/stray.xml.rels` with no source part, or plus a stray `word/x.xml` with an unclosed `word/_rels/x.xml.rels`; each broken sidecar alone; and `mu-stray-foo` again.

Each chunk ends with a minimal control. Each chunk ran twice, as two separate driver runs of byte-identical copies, and each run's rows were read twice: from its own Word log (session 41's `logcheck.py`) and by `wordpdf_outcomes.py`. Outcome is the manifest spelling when both runs and both readings agree, and `unknown` otherwise; 37 of 37 rows agree. The two times in Observed are the ends of the first and second runs. Shape is the builder's description of the specimen. The builder recorded the validator revision in every row (`57e150ae2ed41cec22d1b8b6b8888fff39e6ffbc`). The strict column names the markup-compatibility, XML-syntax and relationship findings, and counts the others.

Every calibration Word was meant to open, and every control, opened clean. Every row Word opened renders the main document's `Hello` in both runs (`pdftotext`), after the header's `Header 85` where the section references a header, and never a note's or comment's `Text 85`. No refused row left a PDF.

- **Word does not read a notes or comments part whose only reference is in a header.** It opened clean all three `-mu-header-reference` rows, and offered to recover unreadable content for the same parts referenced from the body. It opened clean the related, unreferenced part of each kind and the unused footer, and refused the used footer.
- **Word refuses a stored part name holding a colon, read or not.** It offered recovery for `word/ftp:header1.xml` named by no relationship, with or without its Override, and for every scheme-like s85c row, well-formed or not. The unclosed plain-name header drew an open error and the unclosed plain styles part a recovery offer.
- **It refuses a used header whose target spells a scheme, too.** With the part stored as plain `word/header1.xml` and no colon in any stored name, `Target="ftp:header1.xml"` and `"httpfoo:header1.xml"` drew the recovery offer. These rows do not show whether Word reads the target as a missing part or refuses the spelling.
- **A broken relationships part Word never reads does not matter.** It opened clean every s85d row, `mu-stray-foo` beside either broken sidecar included.

Word-valid at 57e150ae matches Word on 21 of 37 rows.
